chapters.en: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
Seeking the Aid of Great Men
The Office of Minister of state
Conduct in the Presence of the King
The Knowledge of the Council Chamber
The Way of Maintaining the Family

items.translit: Akara Mudhala Ezhuththellaam Aadhi / Pakavan Mudhatre Ulaku
items.en: A, as its first of letters, every speech maintains; The "Primal Deity" is first through all the world's domains
items.en_prose: As the letter A is the first of all letters, so the eternal God is first in the world

items.translit: Katradhanaal Aaya Payanenkol Vaalarivan / Natraal Thozhaaar Enin
items.en: No fruit have men of all their studied lore, Save they the 'Purely Wise One's' feet adore
items.en_prose: What Profit have those derived from learning, who worship not the good feet of Him who is possessed of pure knowledge ?

items.translit: Malarmisai Ekinaan Maanati Serndhaar / Nilamisai Neetuvaazh Vaar
items.en: His feet, 'Who o'er the full-blown flower hath past,' who gain / In bliss long time shall dwell above this earthly plain
items.en_prose: They who are united to the glorious feet of Him who passes swiftly over the flower of the mind, shall flourish long above all worlds

items.translit: Ventudhal Ventaamai Ilaanati Serndhaarkku / Yaantum Itumpai Ila
items.en: His foot, 'Whom want affects not, irks not grief,' who gain / Shall not, through every time, of any woes complain
items.en_prose: To those who meditate the feet of Him who is void of desire or aversion, evil shall never come

items.translit: Irulser Iruvinaiyum Seraa Iraivan / Porulser Pukazhpurindhaar Maattu
items.en: The men, who on the 'King's' true praised delight to dwell, Affects not them the fruit of deeds done ill or well
items.en_prose: The two-fold deeds that spring from darkness shall not adhere to those who delight in the true praise of God

items.translit: Porivaayil Aindhaviththaan Poidheer Ozhukka / Nerinindraar Neetuvaazh Vaar
items.en: Long live they blest, who 've stood in path from falsehood freed; His, 'Who quenched lusts that from the sense-gates five proceed'
items.en_prose: Those shall long proposer who abide in the faultless way of Him who has destroyed the five desires of the senses

items.translit: Thanakkuvamai Illaadhaan Thaalserndhaark Kallaal / Manakkavalai Maatral Aridhu
items.en: Unless His foot, 'to Whom none can compare,' men gain,'Tis hard for mind to find relief from anxious pain
items.en_prose: Anxiety of mind cannot be removed, except from those who are united to the feet of Him who is incomparable

items.translit: Aravaazhi Andhanan Thaalserndhaark Kallaal / Piravaazhi Neendhal Aridhu
items.en: Unless His feet 'the Sea of Good, the Fair and Bountiful,' men gain,'Tis hard the further bank of being's changeful sea to attain
items.en_prose: None can swim the sea of vice, but those who are united to the feet of that gracious Being who is a sea of virtue

items.translit: Kolil Poriyin Kunamilave Enkunaththaan / Thaalai Vanangaath Thalai
items.en: Before His foot, 'the Eight-fold Excellence,' with unbent head, Who stands, like palsied sense, is to all living functions dead
items.en_prose: The head that worships not the feet of Him who is possessed of eight attributes, is as useless as a sense without the power of sensation

items.translit: Piravip Perungatal Neendhuvar Neendhaar / Iraivan Atiseraa Thaar
items.en: They swim the sea of births, the 'Monarch's' foot who gain; None others reach the shore of being's mighty main
items.en_prose: None can swim the great sea of births but those who are united to the feet of God

items.translit: Vaannindru Ulakam Vazhangi Varudhalaal / Thaanamizhdham Endrunarar Paatru
items.en: The world its course maintains through life that rain unfailing gives; Thus rain is known the true ambrosial food of all that lives
items.en_prose: By the continuance of rain the world is preserved in existence; it is therefore worthy to be called ambrosia

items.translit: Thuppaarkkuth Thuppaaya Thuppaakkith Thuppaarkkuth / Thuppaaya Thooum Mazhai
items.en: The rain makes pleasant food for eaters rise; As food itself, thirst-quenching draught supplies
items.en_prose: Rain produces good food, and is itself food

items.translit: Vinindru Poippin Virineer Viyanulakaththu / Ulnindru Utatrum Pasi
items.en: If clouds, that promised rain, deceive, and in the sky remain, Famine, sore torment, stalks o'er earth's vast ocean-girdled plain
items.en_prose: If the cloud, withholding rain, deceive (our hopes) hunger will long distress the sea-girt spacious world

items.translit: Erin Uzhaaar Uzhavar Puyalennum / Vaari Valangundrik Kaal
items.en: If clouds their wealth of waters fail on earth to pour, The ploughers plough with oxen's sturdy team no more
items.en_prose: If the abundance of wealth imparting rain diminish, the labour of the plough must cease

items.translit: Ketuppadhooum Kettaarkkuch Chaarvaaimar Raange / Etuppadhooum Ellaam Mazhai
items.en: 'Tis rain works all: it ruin spreads, then timely aid supplies; As, in the happy days before, it bids the ruined rise
items.en_prose: Rain by its absence ruins men; and by its existence restores them to fortune

items.translit: Visumpin Thuliveezhin Allaalmar Raange / Pasumpul Thalaikaanpu Aridhu
items.en: If from the clouds no drops of rain are shed'Tis rare to see green herb lift up its head
items.en_prose: If no drop falls from the clouds, not even the green blade of grass will be seen

items.translit: Netungatalum Thanneermai Kundrum Thatindhezhili / Thaannalkaa Thaaki Vitin
items.en: If clouds restrain their gifts and grant no rain, The treasures fail in ocean's wide domain
items.en_prose: Even the wealth of the wide sea will be diminished, if the cloud that has drawn (its waters) up gives them not back again (in rain)

items.translit: Sirappotu Poosanai Sellaadhu Vaanam / Varakkumel Vaanorkkum Eentu
items.en: If heaven grow dry, with feast and offering never more, Will men on earth the heavenly ones adore
items.en_prose: If the heaven dry up, neither yearly festivals, nor daily worship will be offered in this world, to the celestials

items.translit: Thaanam Thavamirantum Thangaa Viyanulakam / Vaanam Vazhangaa Thenin
items.en: If heaven its watery treasures ceases to dispense, Through the wide world cease gifts, and deeds of 'penitence'
items.en_prose: If rain fall not, penance and alms-deeds will not dwell within this spacious world

items.translit: Neerindru Amaiyaadhu Ulakenin Yaaryaarkkum / Vaanindru Amaiyaadhu Ozhukku
items.en: When water fails, functions of nature cease, you say; Thus when rain fails, no men can walk in 'duty's ordered way'
items.en_prose: If it be said that the duties of life cannot be discharged by any person without water, so without rain there cannot be the flowing of water

items.translit: Ozhukkaththu Neeththaar Perumai Vizhuppaththu / Ventum Panuval Thunivu
items.en: The settled rule of every code requires, as highest good, Their greatness who, renouncing all, true to their rule have stood
items.en_prose: The end and aim of all treatise is to extol beyond all other excellence, the greatness of those who, while abiding in the rule of conduct peculiar to their state, have abandoned all desire

items.translit: Thurandhaar Perumai Thunaikkoorin Vaiyaththu / Irandhaarai Ennikkon Tatru
items.en: As counting those that from the earth have passed away,'Tis vain attempt the might of holy men to say
items.en_prose: To describe the measure of the greatness of those who have forsaken the two-fold desires, is like counting the dead

items.translit: Irumai Vakaidherindhu Eentuaram Poontaar / Perumai Pirangitru Ulaku
items.en: Their greatness earth transcends, who, way of both worlds weighed, In this world take their stand, in virtue's robe arrayed
items.en_prose: The greatness of those who have discovered the properties of both states of being, and renounced the world, shines forth on earth (beyond all others)

items.translit: Uranennum Thottiyaan Oraindhum Kaappaan / Varanennum Vaippirkor Viththu
items.en: He, who with firmness, curb the five restrains, Is seed for soil of yonder happy plains
items.en_prose: He who guides his five senses by the hook of wisdom will be a seed in the world of heaven

items.translit: Aindhaviththaan Aatral Akalvisumpu Laarkomaan / Indhirane Saalung Kari
items.en: Their might who have destroyed 'the five', shall soothly tell / Indra, the lord of those in heaven's wide realms that dwell
items.en_prose: Indra, the king of the inhabitants of the spacious heaven, is himself, a sufficient proof of the strength of him who has subdued his five senses

items.translit: Seyarkariya Seyvaar Periyar Siriyar / Seyarkariya Seykalaa Thaar
items.en: Things hard in the doing will great men do; Things hard in the doing the mean eschew
items.en_prose: The great will do those things which is difficult to be done; but the mean cannot do them

items.translit: Suvaioli Ooruosai Naatramendru Aindhin / Vakaidherivaan Katte Ulaku
items.en: Taste, light, touch, sound, and smell: who knows the way / Of all the five,- the world submissive owns his sway
items.en_prose: The world is within the knowledge of him who knows the properties of taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell

items.translit: Niraimozhi Maandhar Perumai Nilaththu / Maraimozhi Kaatti Vitum
items.en: The might of men whose word is never vain, The 'secret word' shall to the earth proclaim
items.en_prose: The hidden words of the men whose words are full of effect, will shew their greatness to the world

items.translit: Kunamennum Kundreri Nindraar Vekuli / Kanameyum Kaaththal Aridhu
items.en: The wrath 'tis hard e'en for an instant to endure, Of those who virtue's hill have scaled, and stand secure
items.en_prose: The anger of those who have ascended the mountain of goodness, though it continue but for a moment, cannot be resisted

items.translit: Andhanar Enpor Aravormar Revvuyir / Kkum Sendhanmai Poontozhuka Laan
items.en: Towards all that breathe, with seemly graciousness adorned they live; And thus to virtue's sons the name of 'Anthanar' men give
items.en_prose: The virtuous are truly called Anthanar; because in their conduct towards all creatures they are clothed in kindness

items.translit: Sirappu Eenum Selvamum Eenum / Araththinooungu Aakkam Evano Uyirkku
items.en: It yields distinction, yields prosperity; what gain / Greater than virtue can a living man obtain
items.en_prose: Virtue will confer heaven and wealth; what greater source of happiness can man possess ?

items.translit: Araththinooungu Aakkamum Illai Adhanai / Maraththalin Oongillai Ketu
items.en: No greater gain than virtue aught can cause; No greater loss than life oblivious of her laws
items.en_prose: There can be no greater source of good than (the practice of) virtue; there can be no greater source of evil than the forgetfulness of it

items.translit: Ollum Vakaiyaan Aravinai Ovaadhe / Sellumvaai Ellaanj Cheyal
items.en: To finish virtue's work with ceaseless effort strive, What way thou may'st, where'er thou see'st the work may thrive
items.en_prose: As much as possible, in every way, incessantly practise virtue

items.translit: Manaththukkan Maasilan Aadhal Anaiththu / Aran Aakula Neera Pira
items.en: Spotless be thou in mind! This only merits virtue's name; All else, mere pomp of idle sound, no real worth can claim
items.en_prose: Let him who does virtuous deeds be of spotless mind; to that extent is virtue; all else is vain show

items.translit: Azhukkaaru Avaavekuli Innaachchol Naankum / Izhukkaa Iyandradhu Aram
items.en: 'Tis virtue when, his footsteps sliding not through envy, wrath, Lust, evil speech-these four, man onwards moves in ordered path
items.en_prose: That conduct is virtue which is free from these four things, viz, malice, desire, anger and bitter speech

items.translit: Andrarivaam Ennaadhu Aranjeyka Matradhu / Pondrungaal Pondraath Thunai
items.en: Do deeds of virtue now Say not, 'To-morrow we'll be wise'; Thus, when thou diest, shalt thou find a help that never dies
items.en_prose: Defer not virtue to another day; receive her now; and at the dying hour she will be your undying friend

items.translit: Araththaaru Ithuvena Ventaa Sivikai / Poruththaanotu Oorndhaan Itai
items.en: Needs not in words to dwell on virtue's fruits: compare / The man in litter borne with them that toiling bear
items.en_prose: The fruit of virtue need not be described in books; it may be inferred from seeing the bearer of a palanquin and the rider therein

items.translit: Veezhnaal Pataaamai Nandraatrin Aqdhoruvan / Vaazhnaal Vazhiyataikkum Kal
items.en: If no day passing idly, good to do each day you toil, A stone it will be to block the way of future days of moil
items.en_prose: If one allows no day to pass without some good being done, his conduct will be a stone to block up the passage to other births

items.translit: Araththaan Varuvadhe Inpam Mar / Rellaam Puraththa Pukazhum Ila
items.en: What from virtue floweth, yieldeth dear delight; All else extern, is void of glory's light
items.en_prose: Only that pleasure which flows from domestic virtue is pleasure; all else is not pleasure, and it is without praise

items.translit: Seyarpaala Thorum Arane Oruvarku / Uyarpaala Thorum Pazhi
items.en: 'Virtue' sums the things that should be done;'Vice' sums the things that man should shun
items.en_prose: That is virtue which each ought to do, and that is vice which each should shun

items.translit: Ilvaazhvaan Enpaan Iyalputaiya Moovarkkum / Nallaatrin Nindra Thunai
items.en: The men of household virtue, firm in way of good, sustain / The other orders three that rule professed maintain
items.en_prose: He will be called a (true) householder, who is a firm support to the virtuous of the three orders in

items.translit: Thurandhaarkkum Thuvvaa Dhavarkkum Irandhaarkkum / Ilvaazhvaan Enpaan Thunai
items.en: To anchorites, to indigent, to those who've passed away, The man for household virtue famed is needful held and stay
items.en_prose: He will be said to flourish in domestic virtue who aids the forsaken, the poor, and the dead

items.translit: Thenpulaththaar Theyvam Virundhokkal Thaanendraangu / Aimpulaththaaru Ompal Thalai
items.en: The manes, God, guests kindred, self, in due degree, These five to cherish well is chiefest charity
items.en_prose: The chief (duty of the householder) is to preserve the five-fold rule (of conduct) towards the manes, the Gods, his guests, his relations and himself

items.translit: Pazhiyanjip Paaththoon Utaiththaayin Vaazhkkai / Vazhiyenjal Egngnaandrum Il
items.en: Who shares his meal with other, while all guilt he shuns, His virtuous line unbroken though the ages runs
items.en_prose: His descendants shall never fail who, living in the domestic state, fears vice (in the acquisition of property) and shares his food (with others)

items.translit: Anpum Aranum Utaiththaayin Ilvaazhkkai / Panpum Payanum Adhu
items.en: If love and virtue in the household reign, This is of life the perfect grace and gain
items.en_prose: If the married life possess love and virtue, these will be both its duty and reward

items.translit: Araththaatrin Ilvaazhkkai Aatrin Puraththaatril / Pooip Peruva Thevan?
items.en: If man in active household life a virtuous soul retain, What fruit from other modes of virtue can he gain
items.en_prose: What will he who lives virtuously in the domestic state gain by going into the other, (ascetic) state ?

items.translit: Iyalpinaan Ilvaazhkkai Vaazhpavan Enpaan / Muyalvaarul Ellaam Thalai
items.en: In nature's way who spends his calm domestic days,'Mid all that strive for virtue's crown hath foremost place
items.en_prose: Among all those who labour (for future happiness) he is greatest who lives well in the household state

items.translit: Aatrin Ozhukki Aranizhukkaa Ilvaazhkkai / Norpaarin Nonmai Utaiththu
items.en: Others it sets upon their way, itself from virtue ne'er declines; Than stern ascetics' pains such life domestic brighter shines
items.en_prose: The householder who, not swerving from virtue, helps the ascetic in his way, endures more than those who endure penance

items.translit: Aran Enap Pattadhe Ilvaazhkkai / Aqdhum Piranpazhippa Thillaayin Nandru
items.en: The life domestic rightly bears true virtue's name; That other too, if blameless found, due praise may claim
items.en_prose: The marriage state is truly called virtue The other state is also good, if others do not reproach it

items.translit: Vaiyaththul Vaazhvaangu Vaazhpavan Vaanu�ryum / Theyvaththul Vaikkap Patum
items.en: Who shares domestic life, by household virtues graced, Shall, mid the Gods, in heaven who dwell, be placed
items.en_prose: He who on earth has lived in the conjugal state as he should live, will be placed among the Gods who dwell in heaven

items.translit: Manaikdhakka Maanputaiyal Aakiththar Kontaan / Valaththakkaal Vaazhkkaith Thunai
items.en: As doth the house beseem, she shows her wifely dignity; As doth her husband's wealth befit, she spends: help - meet is she
items.en_prose: She who has the excellence of home virtues, and can expend within the means of her husband, is a help in the domestic state

items.translit: Manaimaatchi Illaalkan Illaayin Vaazhkkai / Enaimaatchith Thaayinum Il
items.en: If household excellence be wanting in the wife, Howe'er with splendour lived, all worthless is the life
items.en_prose: If the wife be devoid of domestic excellence, whatever (other) greatness be possessed, the conjugal state, is nothing

items.translit: Illadhen Illaval Maanpaanaal Ulladhen / Illaval Maanaak Katai?
items.en: There is no lack within the house, where wife in worth excels, There is no luck within the house, where wife dishonoured dwells
items.en_prose: If his wife be eminent (in virtue), what does (that man) not possess ? If she be without excellence, what does (he) possess ?

items.translit: Pennin Perundhakka Yaavula Karpennum / Thinmaiun Taakap Perin
items.en: If woman might of chastity retain, What choicer treasure doth the world contain
items.en_prose: What is more excellent than a wife, if she possess the stability of chastity ?

items.translit: Theyvam Thozhaaal Kozhunan Thozhudhezhuvaal / Peyyenap Peyyum Mazhai
items.en: No God adoring, low she bends before her lord; Then rising, serves: the rain falls instant at her word
items.en_prose: If she, who does not worship God, but who rising worships her husband, say, "let it rain," it will rain

items.translit: Tharkaaththuth Tharkontaar Penith Thakaisaandra / Sorkaaththuch Chorvilaal Pen
items.en: Who guards herself, for husband's comfort cares, her household's fame, In perfect wise with sleepless soul preserves, -give her a woman's name
items.en_prose: She is a wife who unweariedly guards herself, takes care of her husband, and preserves an unsullied fame

items.translit: Siraikaakkum Kaappevan Seyyum Makalir / Niraikaakkum Kaappe Thalai
items.en: Of what avail is watch and ward?Honour's woman's safest guard
items.en_prose: What avails the guard of a prison ? The chief guard of a woman is her chastity

items.translit: Petraar Perinperuvar Pentir Perunjirappup / Puththelir Vaazhum Ulaku
items.en: If wife be wholly true to him who gained her as his bride, Great glory gains she in the world where gods bliss abide
items.en_prose: If women shew reverence to their husbands, they will obtain great excellence in the world where the gods flourish

items.translit: Pukazhpurindha Illilorkku Illai Ikazhvaarmun / Erupol Peetu Natai
items.en: Who have not spouses that in virtue's praise delight, They lion-like can never walk in scorner's sight
items.en_prose: The man whose wife seeks not the praise (of chastity) cannot walk with lion-like stately step, before those who revile them

items.translit: Mangalam Enpa Manaimaatchi Matru / Adhan Nankalam Nanmakkat Peru
items.en: The house's 'blessing', men pronounce the house-wife excellent; The gain of blessed children is its goodly ornament
items.en_prose: The excellence of a wife is the good of her husband; and good children are the jewels of that goodness

items.translit: Perumavatrul Yaamarivadhu Illai Arivarindha / Makkatperu Alla Pira
items.en: Of all that men acquire, we know not any greater gain, Than that which by the birth of learned children men obtain
items.en_prose: Among all the benefits that may be acquired, we know no greater benefit than the acquisition of intelligent children

items.translit: Ezhupirappum Theeyavai Theentaa Pazhipirangaap / Panputai Makkat Perin
items.en: Who children gain, that none reproach, of virtuous worth, No evils touch them, through the sev'n-fold maze of birth
items.en_prose: The evils of the seven births shall not touch those who abtain children of a good disposition, free from vice

items.translit: Thamporul Enpadham Makkal Avarporul / Thamdham Vinaiyaan Varum
items.en: 'Man's children are his fortune,' say the wise; From each one's deeds his varied fortunes rise
items.en_prose: Men will call their sons their wealth, because it flows to them through the deeds which they (sons) perform on their behalf

items.translit: Amizhdhinum Aatra Inidhedham Makkal / Sirukai Alaaviya Koozh
items.en: Than God's ambrosia sweeter far the food before men laid, In which the little hands of children of their own have play'd
items.en_prose: The rice in which the little hand of their children has dabbled will be far sweeter (to the parent) than ambrosia

items.translit: Makkalmey Theental Utarkinpam Matru / Avar Sorkettal Inpam Sevikku
items.en: To patent sweet the touch of children dear; Their voice is sweetest music to his ear
items.en_prose: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and the hearing of their words, pleasure to the ear

items.translit: Kuzhal Inidhu Yaazhinidhu Enpadham / Makkal Mazhalaichchol Kelaa Thavar
items.en: 'The pipe is sweet,' 'the lute is sweet,' by them't will be averred, Who music of their infants' lisping lips have never heard
items.en_prose: "The pipe is sweet, the lute is sweet," say those who have not heard the prattle of their own children

items.translit: Thandhai Makarkaatrum Nandri Avaiyaththu / Mundhi Iruppach Cheyal
items.en: Sire greatest boon on son confers, who makes him meet, In councils of the wise to fill the highest seat
items.en_prose: The benefit which a father should confer on his son is to give him precedence in the assembly of the learned

items.translit: Thammindham Makkal Arivutaimai Maanilaththu / Mannuyirk Kellaam Inidhu
items.en: Their children's wisdom greater than their own confessed, Through the wide world is sweet to every human breast
items.en_prose: That their children should possess knowledge is more pleasing to all men of this great earth than to themselves

items.translit: Eendra Pozhudhin Peridhuvakkum Thanmakanaich / Chaandron Enakketta Thaai
items.en: When mother hears him named 'fulfill'd of wisdom's lore,'Far greater joy she feels, than when her son she bore
items.en_prose: The mother who hears her son called "a wise man" will rejoice more than she did at his birth

items.translit: Makandhandhaikku Aatrum Udhavi Ivandhandhai / Ennotraan Kol Enum Sol
items.en: To sire, what best requital can by grateful child be done?To make men say, 'What merit gained the father such a son?'
items.en_prose: (So to act) that it may be said "by what great penance did his father beget him," is the benefit which a son should render to his father

items.translit: Anpirkum Unto Ataikkundhaazh Aarvalar / Punkaneer Poosal Tharum
items.en: And is there bar that can even love restrain?The tiny tear shall make the lover's secret plain
items.en_prose: Is there any fastening that can shut in love ? Tears of the affectionate will publish the love that is within

items.translit: Anpilaar Ellaam Thamakkuriyar Anputaiyaar / Enpum Uriyar Pirarkku
items.en: The loveless to themselves belong alone; The loving men are others' to the very bone
items.en_prose: Those who are destitute of love appropriate all they have to themselves; but those who possess love consider even their bones to belong to others

items.translit: Anpotu Iyaindha Vazhakkenpa Aaruyirkku / Enpotu Iyaindha Thotarpu
items.en: Of precious soul with body's flesh and bone, The union yields one fruit, the life of love alone
items.en_prose: They say that the union of soul and body in man is the fruit of the union of love and virtue (in a former birth)

items.translit: Anpu Eenum Aarvam Utaimai / Adhueenum Nanpu Ennum Naataach
items.en: From love fond yearning springs for union sweet of minds; And that the bond of rare excelling friendship binds
items.en_prose: Love begets desire: and that (desire) begets the immeasureable excellence of friendship

items.translit: Anputru Amarndha Vazhakkenpa Vaiyakaththu / Inputraar Eydhum Sirappu
items.en: Sweetness on earth and rarest bliss above, These are the fruits of tranquil life of love
items.en_prose: These are the fruits of tranquil life of love

items.translit: Araththirke Anpusaar Penpa Ariyaar / Maraththirkum Aqdhe Thunai
items.en: The unwise deem love virtue only can sustain, It also helps the man who evil would restrain
items.en_prose: The ignorant say that love is an ally to virtue only, but it is also a help to get out of vice

items.translit: Enpi Ladhanai Veyilpolak Kaayume / Anpi Ladhanai Aram
items.en: As sun's fierce ray dries up the boneless things, So loveless beings virtue's power to nothing brings
items.en_prose: Virtue will burn up the soul which is without love, even as the sun burns up the creature which is without bone, ie worms

items.translit: Anpakath Thillaa Uyirvaazhkkai Vanpaarkan / Vatral Marandhalirth Thatru
items.en: The loveless soul, the very joys of life may know, When flowers, in barren soil, on sapless trees, shall blow
items.en_prose: The domestic state of that man whose mind is without love is like the flourishing of a withered tree upon the parched desert

items.translit: Puraththurup Pellaam Evanseyyum Yaakkai / Akaththuruppu Anpi Lavarkku
items.en: Though every outward part complete, the body's fitly framed; What good, when soul within, of love devoid, lies halt and maimed
items.en_prose: Of what avail are all the external members (of the body) to those who are destitute of love, the internal member

items.translit: Anpin Vazhiyadhu Uyirnilai Aqdhilaarkku / Enpudhol Porththa Utampu
items.en: Bodies of loveless men are bony framework clad with skin; Then is the body seat of life, when love resides within
items.en_prose: That body alone which is inspired with love contains a living soul: if void of it, (the body) is bone overlaid with skin

items.translit: Irundhompi Ilvaazhva Thellaam Virundhompi / Velaanmai Seydhar Poruttu
items.en: All household cares and course of daily life have this in view / Guests to receive with courtesy, and kindly acts to do
items.en_prose: The whole design of living in the domestic state and laying up (property) is (to be able) to exercise the benevolence of hospitality

items.translit: Virundhu Puraththadhaath Thaanuntal Saavaa / Marundheninum Ventarpaar Randru
items.en: Though food of immortality should crown the board, Feasting alone, the guests without unfed, is thing abhorred
items.en_prose: It is not fit that one should wish his guests to be outside (his house) even though he were eating the food of immortality

items.translit: Varuvirundhu Vaikalum Ompuvaan Vaazhkkai / Paruvandhu Paazhpatudhal Indru
items.en: Each day he tends the coming guest with kindly care; Painless, unfailing plenty shall his household share
items.en_prose: The domestic life of the man that daily entertains the guests who come to him shall not be laid waste by poverty

items.translit: Akanamarndhu Seyyaal Uraiyum Mukanamarndhu / Nalvirundhu Ompuvaan Il
items.en: With smiling face he entertains each virtuous guest,'Fortune' with gladsome mind shall in his dwelling rest
items.en_prose: Lakshmi with joyous mind shall dwell in the house of that man who, with cheerful countenance, entertains the good as guests

items.translit: Viththum Italventum Kollo Virundhompi / Michchil Misaivaan Pulam
items.en: Who first regales his guest, and then himself supplies, O'er all his fields, unsown, shall plenteous harvests rise
items.en_prose: Is it necessary to sow the field of the man who, having feasted his guests, eats what may remain ?

items.translit: Selvirundhu Ompi Varuvirundhu Paarththiruppaan / Nalvarundhu Vaanath Thavarkku
items.en: The guest arrived he tends, the coming guest expects to see; To those in heavenly homes that dwell a welcome guest is he
items.en_prose: He who, having entertained the guests that have come, looks out for others who may yet come, will be a welcome guest to the inhabitants of heaven

items.translit: Inaiththunaith Thenpadhon Rillai Virundhin / Thunaiththunai Velvip Payan
items.en: To reckon up the fruit of kindly deeds were all in vain; Their worth is as the worth of guests you entertain
items.en_prose: The advantages of benevolence cannot be measured; the measure (of the virtue) of the guests (entertained) is the only measure

items.translit: Parindhompip Patratrem Enpar Virundhompi / Velvi Thalaippataa Thaar
items.en: With pain they guard their stores, yet 'All forlorn are we,' they'll cry, Who cherish not their guests, nor kindly help supply
items.en_prose: Those who have taken no part in the benevolence of hospitality shall (at length lament) saying, "we have laboured and laid up wealth and are now without support."

items.translit: Utaimaiyul Inmai Virundhompal Ompaa / Matamai Matavaarkan Untu
items.en: To turn from guests is penury, though worldly goods abound;'Tis senseless folly, only with the senseless found
items.en_prose: That stupidity which excercises no hospitality is poverty in the midst of wealth It is the property of the stupid

items.translit: Moppak Kuzhaiyum Anichcham Mukandhirindhu / Nokkak Kuzhaiyum Virundhu
items.en: The flower of 'Anicha' withers away, If you do but its fragrance inhale; If the face of the host cold welcome convey, The guest's heart within him will fail
items.en_prose: As the Anicham flower fades in smelling, so fades the guest when the face is turned away

items.translit: Insolaal Eeram Alaiip Patiruilavaam / Semporul Kantaarvaaich Chol
items.en: Pleasant words are words with all pervading love that burn; Words from his guileless mouth who can the very truth discern
items.en_prose: Sweet words are those which imbued with love and free from deceit flow from the mouth of the virtuous

items.translit: Akanamarndhu Eedhalin Nandre Mukanamarndhu / Insolan Aakap Perin
items.en: A pleasant word with beaming smile's preferred, Even to gifts with liberal heart conferred
items.en_prose: Sweet speech, with a cheerful countenance is better than a gift made with a joyous mind

items.translit: Mukaththaan Amarndhuinidhu Nokki Akaththaanaam / Inso Linadhe Aram
items.en: With brightly beaming smile, and kindly light of loving eye, And heart sincere, to utter pleasant words is charity
items.en_prose: Sweet speech, flowing from the heart (uttered) with a cheerful countenance and a sweet look, is true virtue

items.translit: Thunpurooum Thuvvaamai Illaakum Yaarmaattum / Inpurooum Inso Lavarkku
items.en: The men of pleasant speech that gladness breathe around, Through indigence shall never sorrow's prey be found
items.en_prose: Sorrow-increasing poverty shall not come upon those who use towards all, pleasure-increasing sweetness of speech

items.translit: Panivutaiyan Insolan Aadhal Oruvarku / Aniyalla Matrup Pira
items.en: Humility with pleasant speech to man on earth, Is choice adornment; all besides is nothing worth
items.en_prose: Humility and sweetness of speech are the ornaments of man; all others are not (ornaments)

items.translit: Allavai Theya Aramperukum Nallavai / Naati Iniya Solin
items.en: Who seeks out good, words from his lips of sweetness flow; In him the power of vice declines, and virtues grow
items.en_prose: If a man, while seeking to speak usefully, speaks also sweetly, his sins will diminish and his virtue increase

items.translit: Nayan Eendru Nandri Payakkum / Payaneendru Panpin Thalaippiriyaach Chol
items.en: The words of sterling sense, to rule of right that strict adhere, To virtuous action prompting, blessings yield in every sphere
items.en_prose: That speech which, while imparting benefits ceases not to please, will yield righteousness (for this world) and merit (for the next world)

items.translit: Sirumaiyul Neengiya Insol Marumaiyum / Immaiyum Inpam Tharum
items.en: Sweet kindly words, from meanness free, delight of heart, In world to come and in this world impart
items.en_prose: Sweet speech, free from harm to others, will give pleasure both in this world and in the next

items.translit: Insol Inidheendral Kaanpaan Evankolo / Vansol Vazhangu Vadhu?
items.en: Who sees the pleasure kindly speech affords, Why makes he use of harsh, repellant words
items.en_prose: Why does he use harsh words, who sees the pleasure which sweet speech yields ?

items.translit: Iniya Ulavaaka Innaadha Kooral / Kaniiruppak Kaaikavarn Thatru
items.en: When pleasant words are easy, bitter words to use, Is, leaving sweet ripe fruit, the sour unripe to choose
items.en_prose: To say disagreeable things when agreeable are at hand is like eating unripe fruit when there is ripe

items.translit: Seyyaamal Seydha Udhavikku Vaiyakamum / Vaanakamum Aatral Aridhu
items.en: Assistance given by those who ne'er received our aid, Is debt by gift of heaven and earth but poorly paid
items.en_prose: (The gift of) heaven and earth is not an equivalent for a benefit which is conferred where none had been received

items.translit: Kaalaththi Naarseydha Nandri Siridheninum / Gnaalaththin Maanap Peridhu
items.en: A timely benefit, -though thing of little worth, The gift itself, -in excellence transcends the earth
items.en_prose: A favour conferred in the time of need, though it be small (in itself), is (in value) much larger than the world

items.translit: Payandhookkaar Seydha Udhavi Nayandhookkin / Nanmai Katalin Peridhu
items.en: Kindness shown by those who weigh not what the return may be:When you ponder right its merit, 'Tis vaster than the sea
items.en_prose: If we weigh the excellence of a benefit which is conferred without weighing the return, it is larger than the sea

items.translit: Thinaiththunai Nandri Seyinum Panaiththunaiyaak / Kolvar Payandheri Vaar
items.en: Each benefit to those of actions' fruit who rightly deem, Though small as millet-seed, as palm-tree vast will seem
items.en_prose: Though the benefit conferred be as small as a millet seed, those who know its advantage will consider it as large as a palmyra fruit

items.translit: Udhavi Varaiththandru Udhavi Udhavi / Seyappattaar Saalpin Varaiththu
items.en: The kindly aid's extent is of its worth no measure true; Its worth is as the worth of him to whom the act you do
items.en_prose: The benefit itself is not the measure of the benefit; the worth of those who have received it is its measure

items.translit: Maravarka Maasatraar Kenmai Thuravarka / Thunpaththul Thuppaayaar Natpu
items.en: Kindness of men of stainless soul remember evermore / Forsake thou never friends who were thy stay in sorrow sore
items.en_prose: Forsake not the friendship of those who have been your staff in adversity Forget not be benevolence of the blameless

items.translit: Ezhumai Ezhupirappum Ulluvar Thangan / Vizhuman Thutaiththavar Natpu
items.en: Through all seven worlds, in seven-fold birth, Remains in mem'ry of the wise / Friendship of those who wiped on earth, The tears of sorrow from their eyes
items.en_prose: (The wise) will remember throughout their seven-fold births the love of those who have wiped away their affliction

items.translit: Nandri Marappadhu Nandrandru Nandralladhu / Andre Marappadhu Nandru
items.en: 'Tis never good to let the thought of good things done thee pass away; Of things not good, 'tis good to rid thy memory that very day
items.en_prose: It is not good to forget a benefit; it is good to forget an injury even in the very moment (in which it is inflicted)

items.translit: Kondranna Innaa Seyinum Avarseydha / Ondrunandru Ullak Ketum
items.en: Effaced straightway is deadliest injury, By thought of one kind act in days gone by
items.en_prose: Though one inflict an injury great as murder, it will perish before the thought of one benefit (formerly) conferred

items.translit: Ennandri Kondraarkkum Uyvuntaam Uyvillai / Seynnandri Kondra Makarku
items.en: Who every good have killed, may yet destruction flee; Who 'benefit' has killed, that man shall ne'er 'scape free
items.en_prose: He who has killed every virtue may yet escape; there is no escape for him who has killed a benefit

items.translit: Thakudhi Enavondru Nandre Pakudhiyaal / Paarpattu Ozhukap Perin
items.en: If justice, failing not, its quality maintain, Giving to each his due, -'tis man's one highest gain
items.en_prose: That equity which consists in acting with equal regard to each of (the three) divisions of men [enemies, strangers and friends] is a pre-eminent virtue

items.translit: Seppam Utaiyavan Aakkanj Chidhaivindri / Echchaththir Kemaappu Utaiththu
items.en: The just man's wealth unwasting shall endure, And to his race a lasting joy ensure
items.en_prose: The wealth of the man of rectitude will not perish, but will bring happiness also to his posterity

items.translit: Nandre Tharinum Natuvikandhaam Aakkaththai / Andre Yozhiya Vital
items.en: Though only good it seem to give, yet gain / By wrong acquired, not e'en one day retain
items.en_prose: Forsake in the very moment (of acquisition) that gain which, though it should bring advantage, is without equity

items.translit: Thakkaar Thakavilar Enpadhu Avaravar / Echchaththaar Kaanap Patum
items.en: Who just or unjust lived shall soon appear:By each one's offspring shall the truth be clear
items.en_prose: The worthy and unworthy may be known by the existence or otherwise of good offsprings

items.translit: Ketum Perukkamum Illalla Nenjaththuk / Kotaamai Saandrork Kani
items.en: The gain and loss in life are not mere accident; Just mind inflexible is sages' ornament
items.en_prose: Loss and gain come not without cause; it is the ornament of the wise to preserve evenness of mind (under both)

items.translit: Ketuvalyaan Enpadhu Arikadhan Nenjam / Natuvoreei Alla Seyin
items.en: If, right deserting, heart to evil turn, Let man impending ruin's sign discern
items.en_prose: Let him whose mind departing from equity commits sin well consider thus within himself, "I shall perish."

items.translit: Ketuvaaka Vaiyaadhu Ulakam Natuvaaka / Nandrikkan Thangiyaan Thaazhvu
items.en: The man who justly lives, tenacious of the right, In low estate is never low to wise man's sight
items.en_prose: The great will not regard as poverty the low estate of that man who dwells in the virtue of equity

items.translit: Samanseydhu Seerdhookkung Kolpol Amaindhorupaal / Kotaamai Saandrork Kani
items.en: To stand, like balance-rod that level hangs and rightly weighs, With calm unbiassed equity of soul, is sages' praise
items.en_prose: To incline to neither side, but to rest impartial as the even-fixed scale is the ornament of the wise

items.translit: Sorkottam Illadhu Seppam Orudhalaiyaa / Utkottam Inmai Perin
items.en: Inflexibility in word is righteousness, If men inflexibility of soul possess
items.en_prose: Freedom from obliquity of speech is rectitude, if there be (corresponding) freedom from bias of mind

items.translit: Vaanikam Seyvaarkku Vaanikam Penip / Piravum Thamapol Seyin
items.en: As thriving trader is the trader known, Who guards another's interests as his own
items.en_prose: The true merchandize of merchants is to guard and do by the things of others as they do by their own

items.translit: Atakkam Amararul Uykkum Atangaamai / Aarirul Uyththu Vitum
items.en: Control of self does man conduct to bliss th' immortals share; Indulgence leads to deepest night, and leaves him there
items.en_prose: Self-control will place (a man) among the Gods; the want of it will drive (him) into the thickest darkness (of hell)

items.translit: Kaakka Porulaa Atakkaththai Aakkam / Adhaninooung Killai Uyirkku
items.en: Guard thou as wealth the power of self-control; Than this no greater gain to living soul
items.en_prose: Let self-control be guarded as a treasure; there is no greater source of good for man than that

items.translit: Serivarindhu Seermai Payakkum Arivarindhu / Aatrin Atangap Perin
items.en: If versed in wisdom's lore by virtue's law you self restrain / Your self-repression known will yield you glory's gain
items.en_prose: Knowing that self-control is knowledge, if a man should control himself, in the prescribed course, such self-control will bring him distinction among the wise

items.translit: Nilaiyin Thiriyaadhu Atangiyaan Thotram / Malaiyinum Maanap Peridhu
items.en: In his station, all unswerving, if man self subdue, Greater he than mountain proudly rising to the view
items.en_prose: More lofty than a mountain will be the greatness of that man who without swerving from his domestic state, controls himself

items.translit: Ellaarkkum Nandraam Panidhal Avarullum / Selvarkke Selvam Thakaiththu
items.en: To all humility is goodly grace; but chief to them / With fortune blessed, -'tis fortune's diadem
items.en_prose: Humility is good in all; but especially in the rich it is (the excellence of) higher riches

items.translit: Orumaiyul Aamaipol Aindhatakkal Aatrin / Ezhumaiyum Emaap Putaiththu
items.en: Like tortoise, who the five restrains / In one, through seven world bliss obtains
items.en_prose: Should one throughout a single birth, like a tortoise keep in his five senses, the fruit of it will prove a safe-guard to him throughout the seven-fold births.

items.translit: Yaakaavaa Raayinum Naakaakka Kaavaakkaal / Sokaappar Sollizhukkup Pattu
items.en: Whate'er they fail to guard, o'er lips men guard should keep; If not, through fault of tongue, they bitter tears shall weep
items.en_prose: Whatever besides you leave unguarded, guard your tongue; otherwise errors of speech and the consequent misery will ensue

items.translit: Ondraanun Theechchol Porutpayan Untaayin / Nandraakaa Thaaki Vitum
items.en: Though some small gain of good it seem to bring, The evil word is parent still of evil thing
items.en_prose: If a man's speech be productive of a single evil, all the good by him will be turned into evil

items.translit: Theeyinaar Suttapun Ullaarum Aaraadhe / Naavinaar Sutta Vatu
items.en: In flesh by fire inflamed, nature may thoroughly heal the sore; In soul by tongue inflamed, the ulcer healeth never more
items.en_prose: The wound which has been burnt in by fire may heal, but a wound burnt in by the tongue will never heal

items.translit: Kadhangaaththuk Katratangal Aatruvaan Sevvi / Arampaarkkum Aatrin Nuzhaindhu
items.en: Who learns restraint, and guards his soul from wrath, Virtue, a timely aid, attends his path
items.en_prose: Virtue, seeking for an opportunity, will come into the path of that man who, possessed of learning and self-control, guards himself against anger

items.translit: Ozhukkam Vizhuppan Tharalaan Ozhukkam / Uyirinum Ompap Patum
items.en: 'Decorum' gives especial excellence; with greater care'Decorum' should men guard than life, which all men share
items.en_prose: Propriety of conduct leads to eminence, it should therefore be preserved more carefully than life

items.translit: Parindhompik Kaakka Ozhukkam Therindhompith / Therinum Aqdhe Thunai
items.en: Searching, duly watching, learning, 'decorum' still we find; Man's only aid; toiling, guard thou this with watchful mind
items.en_prose: Let propriety of conduct be laboriously preserved and guarded; though one know and practise and excel in many virtues, that will be an eminent aid

items.translit: Ozhukkam Utaimai Kutimai Izhukkam / Izhindha Pirappaai Vitum
items.en: 'Decorum's' true nobility on earth;'Indecorum's' issue is ignoble birth
items.en_prose: Propriety of conduct is true greatness of birth, and impropriety will sink into a mean birth

items.translit: Marappinum Oththuk Kolalaakum Paarppaan / Pirappozhukkang Kundrak Ketum
items.en: Though he forget, the Brahman may regain his Vedic lore; Failing in 'decorum due,' birthright's gone for evermore
items.en_prose: A Brahman though he should forget the Vedas may recover it by reading; but, if he fail in propriety of conduct even his high birth will be destroyed

items.translit: Azhukkaa Rutaiyaankan Aakkampondru Illai / Ozhukka Milaankan Uyarvu
items.en: The envious soul in life no rich increase of blessing gains, So man of 'due decorum' void no dignity obtains
items.en_prose: Just as the envious man will be without wealth, so will the man of destitute of propriety of conduct be without greatness

items.translit: Ozhukkaththin Olkaar Uravor Izhukkaththin / Edham Patupaak Karindhu
items.en: The strong of soul no jot abate of 'strict decorum's' laws, Knowing that 'due decorum's' breach foulest disgrace will cause
items.en_prose: Those firm in mind will not slacken in their observance of the proprieties of life, knowing, as they do, the misery that flows from the transgression from them

items.translit: Ozhukkaththin Eydhuvar Menmai Izhukkaththin / Eydhuvar Eydhaap Pazhi
items.en: 'Tis source of dignity when 'true decorum' is preserved; Who break 'decorum's' rules endure e'en censures undeserved
items.en_prose: From propriety of conduct men obtain greatness; from impropriety comes insufferable disgrace

items.translit: Nandrikku Viththaakum Nallozhukkam Theeyozhukkam / Endrum Itumpai Tharum
items.en: 'Decorum true' observed a seed of good will be;'Decorum's breach' will sorrow yield eternally
items.en_prose: Propriety of conduct is the seed of virtue; impropriety will ever cause sorrow

items.translit: Ozhukka Mutaiyavarkku Ollaave Theeya / Vazhukkiyum Vaayaar Solal
items.en: It cannot be that they who 'strict decorum's' law fulfil, E'en in forgetful mood, should utter words of ill
items.en_prose: Those who study propriety of conduct will not speak evil, even forgetfully

items.translit: Ulakaththotu Otta Ozhukal Palakatrum / Kallaar Arivilaa Thaar
items.en: Who know not with the world in harmony to dwell, May many things have learned, but nothing well
items.en_prose: Those who know not how to act agreeably to the world, though they have learnt many things, are still ignorant

items.translit: Piranporulaal Pettozhukum Pedhaimai Gnaalaththu / Aramporul Kantaarkan Il
items.en: Who laws of virtue and possession's rights have known, Indulge no foolish love of her by right another's own
items.en_prose: The folly of desiring her who is the property of another will not be found in those who know (the attributes of) virtue and (the rights of) property

items.translit: Arankatai Nindraarul Ellaam Pirankatai / Nindraarin Pedhaiyaar Il
items.en: No fools, of all that stand from virtue's pale shut out, Like those who longing lurk their neighbour's gate without
items.en_prose: Among all those who stand on the outside of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand outside their neighbour's door

items.translit: Vilindhaarin Verallar Mandra Thelindhaaril / Theemai Purindhu Ozhuku Vaar
items.en: They're numbered with the dead, e'en while they live, -how otherwise?With wife of sure confiding friend who evil things devise
items.en_prose: Certainly they are no better than dead men who desire evil towards the wife of those who

items.translit: Enaiththunaiyar Aayinum Ennaam Thinaiththunaiyum / Theraan Piranil Pukal
items.en: How great soe'er they be, what gain have they of life, Who, not a whit reflecting, seek a neighbour's wife
items.en_prose: However great one may be, what does it avail if, without at all considering his guilt, he goes unto the wife of another ?

items.translit: Elidhena Illirappaan Eydhumenj Gnaandrum / Viliyaadhu Nirkum Pazhi
items.en: 'Mere triflel' saying thus, invades the home, so he ensures / A gain of guilt that deathless aye endures
items.en_prose: He who thinks lightly of going into the wife of another acquires guilt that will abide with him imperishably and for ever

items.translit: Pakaipaavam Achcham Pazhiyena Naankum / Ikavaavaam Illirappaan Kan
items.en: Who home ivades, from him pass nevermore, Hatred and sin, fear, foul disgrace; these four
items.en_prose: Hatred, sin, fear, disgrace; these four will never leave him who goes in to his neighbour's wife

items.translit: Araniyalaan Ilvaazhvaan Enpaan Piraniyalaal / Penmai Nayavaa Thavan
items.en: Who sees the wife, another's own, with no desiring eye / In sure domestic bliss he dwelleth ever virtuously
items.en_prose: He who desires not the womanhood of her who should walk according to the will of another will be praised as a virtuous house-holder

items.translit: Piranmanai Nokkaadha Peraanmai Saandrorkku / Aranondro Aandra Vozhukku
items.en: Manly excellence, that looks not on another's wife, Is not virtue merely, 'tis full 'propriety' of life
items.en_prose: That noble manliness which looks not at the wife of another is the virtue and dignity of the great

items.translit: Nalakkuriyaar Yaarenin Naamaneer Vaippin / Pirarkkuriyaal Tholdhoyaa Thaar
items.en: Who 're good indeed, on earth begirt by ocean's gruesome tide?The men who touch not her that is another's bride
items.en_prose: Is it asked, "who are those who shall obtain good in this world surrounded by the terror-producing sea ?" Those who touch not the shoulder of her who belongs to another

items.translit: Aranvaraiyaan Alla Seyinum Piranvaraiyaal / Penmai Nayavaamai Nandru
items.en: Though virtue's bounds he pass, and evil deeds hath wrought; At least, 'tis good if neighbour's wife he covet not
items.en_prose: Though a man perform no virtuous deeds and commit (every) vice, it will be well if he desire not the womanhood of her who is within the limit (of the house) of another

items.translit: Akazhvaaraith Thaangum Nilampolath Thammai / Ikazhvaarp Poruththal Thalai
items.en: As earth bears up the men who delve into her breast, To bear with scornful men of virtues is the best
items.en_prose: To bear with those who revile us, just as the earth bears up those who dig it, is the first of virtues

items.translit: Poruththal Irappinai Endrum Adhanai / Maraththal Adhaninum Nandru
items.en: Forgiving trespasses is good always; Forgetting them hath even higher praise;
items.en_prose: Bear with reproach even when you can retaliate; but to forget it will be still better than that

items.translit: Inmaiyul Inmai Virundhoraal Vanmaiyul / Vanmai Matavaarp Porai
items.en: The sorest poverty is bidding guest unfed depart; The mightiest might to bear with men of foolish heart
items.en_prose: To neglect hospitality is poverty of poverty To bear with the ignorant is might of might

items.translit: Niraiyutaimai Neengaamai Ventin Poraiyutaimai / Potri Yozhukap Patum
items.en: Seek'st thou honour never tarnished to retain; So must thou patience, guarding evermore, maintain
items.en_prose: If you desire that greatness should never leave, you preserve in your conduct the exercise of patience

items.translit: Oruththaarai Ondraaka Vaiyaare Vaippar / Poruththaaraip Ponpor Podhindhu
items.en: Who wreak their wrath as worthless are despised; Who patiently forbear as gold are prized
items.en_prose: (The wise) will not at all esteem the resentful They will esteem the patient just as the gold which they lay up with care

items.translit: Oruththaarkku Orunaalai Inpam Poruththaarkkup / Pondrun Thunaiyum Pukazh
items.en: Who wreak their wrath have pleasure for a day; Who bear have praise till earth shall pass away
items.en_prose: The pleasure of the resentful continues for a day The praise of the patient will continue until (the final destruction of) the world

items.translit: Thiranalla Tharpirar Seyyinum Nonondhu / Aranalla Seyyaamai Nandru
items.en: Though others work thee ill, thus shalt thou blessing reap; Grieve for their sin, thyself from vicious action keep
items.en_prose: Though others inflict injuries on you, yet compassionating the evil (that will come upon them) it will be well not to do them anything contrary to virtue

items.translit: Mikudhiyaan Mikkavai Seydhaaraith Thaandham / Thakudhiyaan Vendru Vital
items.en: With overweening pride when men with injuries assail, By thine own righteous dealing shalt thou mightily prevail
items.en_prose: Let a man by patience overcome those who through pride commit excesses

items.translit: Thurandhaarin Thooimai Utaiyar Irandhaarvaai / Innaachchol Norkir Pavar
items.en: They who transgressors' evil words endure / With patience, are as stern ascetics pure
items.en_prose: Those who bear with the uncourteous speech of the insolent are as pure as the ascetics

items.translit: Unnaadhu Norpaar Periyar Pirarsollum / Innaachchol Norpaarin Pin
items.en: Though 'great' we deem the men that fast and suffer pain, Who others' bitter words endure, the foremost place obtain
items.en_prose: Those who endure abstinence from food are great, next to those who endure the uncourteous speech of others

items.translit: Ozhukkaaraak Kolka Oruvandhan Nenjaththu / Azhukkaaru Ilaadha Iyalpu
items.en: As 'strict decorum's' laws, that all men bind, Let each regard unenvying grace of mind
items.en_prose: Let a man esteem that disposition which is free from envy in the same manner as propriety of conduct

items.translit: Vizhuppetrin Aqdhoppadhu Illaiyaar Maattum / Azhukkaatrin Anmai Perin
items.en: If man can learn to envy none on earth,'Tis richest gift, -beyond compare its worth
items.en_prose: Amongst all attainable excellences there is none equal to that of being free from envy towords others

items.translit: Aranaakkam Ventaadhaan Enpaan Piranaakkam / Penaadhu Azhukkarup Paan
items.en: Nor wealth nor virtue does that man desire 'tis plain, Whom others' wealth delights not, feeling envious pain
items.en_prose: Of him who instead of rejoicing in the wealth of others, envies it, it will be said "he neither desires virtue not wealth."

items.translit: Azhukkaatrin Allavai Seyyaar Izhukkaatrin / Edham Patupaakku Arindhu
items.en: The wise through envy break not virtue's laws, Knowing ill-deeds of foul disgrace the cause
items.en_prose: (The wise) knowing the misery that comes from transgression will not through envy commit unrighteous deeds

items.translit: Azhukkaaru Utaiyaarkku Adhusaalum Onnaar / Vazhukka�yum Keteen Padhu
items.en: Envy they have within! Enough to seat their fate!Though foemen fail, envy can ruin consummate
items.en_prose: To those who cherish envy that is enough Though free from enemies that (envy) will bring destruction

items.translit: Kotuppadhu Azhukkaruppaan Sutram Utuppadhooum / Unpadhooum Indrik Ketum
items.en: Who scans good gifts to others given with envious eye, His kin, with none to clothe or feed them, surely die
items.en_prose: He who is envious at a gift (made to another) will with his relations utterly perish destitute of food and rainment

items.translit: Avviththu Azhukkaaru Utaiyaanaich Cheyyaval / Thavvaiyaik Kaatti Vitum
items.en: From envious man good fortune's goddess turns away, Grudging him good, and points him out misfortune's prey
items.en_prose: Lakshmi envying (the prosperity) of the envious man will depart and introduce him to her sister

items.translit: Azhukkaaru Enaoru Paavi Thiruchchetruth / Theeyuzhi Uyththu Vitum
items.en: Envy, embodied ill, incomparable bane, Good fortune slays, and soul consigns to fiery pain
items.en_prose: Envy will destroy (a man's) wealth (in his world) and drive him into the pit of fire (in the world to come.)

items.translit: Avviya Nenjaththaan Aakkamum Sevviyaan / Ketum Ninaikkap Patum
items.en: To men of envious heart, when comes increase of joy, Or loss to blameless men, the 'why' will thoughtful hearts employ
items.en_prose: The wealth of a man of envious mind and the poverty of the righteous will be pondered

items.translit: Azhukkatru Akandraarum Illai Aqdhuillaar / Perukkaththil Theerndhaarum Il
items.en: No envious men to large and full felicity attain; No men from envy free have failed a sure increase to gain
items.en_prose: Never have the envious become great; never have those who are free from envy been without greatness

items.translit: Natuvindri Nanporul Veqkin Kutipondrik / Kutramum Aange Tharum
items.en: With soul unjust to covet others' well-earned store, Brings ruin to the home, to evil opes the door
items.en_prose: If a man departing from equity covet the property (of others), at that very time will his family be destroyed and guilt be incurred

items.translit: Patupayan Veqkip Pazhippatuva Seyyaar / Natuvanmai Naanu Pavar
items.en: Through lust of gain, no deeds that retribution bring, Do they, who shrink with shame from every unjust thing
items.en_prose: Those who blush at the want of equity will not commit disgraceful acts through desire of the profit that may be gained

items.translit: Sitrinpam Veqki Aranalla Seyyaare / Matrinpam Ventu Pavar
items.en: No deeds of ill, misled by base desire, Do they, whose souls to other joys aspire
items.en_prose: Those who desire the higher pleasures (of heaven) will not act unjustly through desire of the trifling joy. (in this life.)

items.translit: Ilamendru Veqkudhal Seyyaar Pulamvendra / Punmaiyil Kaatchi Yavar
items.en: Men who have conquered sense, with sight from sordid vision freed, Desire not other's goods, e'en in the hour of sorest need
items.en_prose: The wise who have conquered their senses and are free from crime, will not covet (the things of others), with the thought "we are destitute."

items.translit: Aqki Akandra Arivennaam Yaarmaattum / Veqki Veriya Seyin
items.en: What gain, though lore refined of amplest reach he learn, His acts towards all mankind if covetous desire to folly turn
items.en_prose: What is the advantage of extensive and accurate knowledge if a man through covetousness act senselessly towards all ?

items.translit: Arulveqki Aatrinkan Nindraan Porulveqkip / Pollaadha Soozhak Ketum
items.en: Though, grace desiring, he in virtue's way stand strong, He's lost who wealth desires, and ponders deeds of wrong
items.en_prose: If he, who through desire of the virtue of kindness abides in the domestic state ie, the path in which it may be obtained, covet (the property of others) and think of evil methods (to obtain it), he will perish

items.translit: Ventarka Veqkiyaam Aakkam Vilaivayin / Maantar Karidhaam Payan
items.en: Seek not increase by greed of gain acquired; That fruit matured yields never good desired
items.en_prose: Desire not the gain of covetousness In the enjoyment of its fruits there is no glory

items.translit: Aqkaamai Selvaththirku Yaadhenin Veqkaamai / Ventum Pirankaip Porul
items.en: What saves prosperity from swift decline?Absence of lust to make another's cherished riches thine
items.en_prose: If it is weighed, "what is the indestructibility of wealth," it is freedom from covetousness

items.translit: Aranarindhu Veqkaa Arivutaiyaarch Cherum / Thiranarin Thaange Thiru
items.en: Good fortune draws anigh in helpful time of need, To him who, schooled in virtue, guards his soul from greed
items.en_prose: Lakshmi, knowing the manner (in which she may approach) will immediately come to those wise men who, knowing that it is virtue, covet not the property of others

items.translit: Iraleenum Ennaadhu Veqkin Viraleenum / Ventaamai Ennunj Cherukku
items.en: From thoughtless lust of other's goods springs fatal ill, Greatness of soul that covets not shall triumph still
items.en_prose: To covet (the wealth of another) regardless of consequences will bring destruction That greatness (of mind) which covets not will give victory

items.translit: Arangooraan Alla Seyinum Oruvan / Purangooraan Endral Inidhu
items.en: Though virtuous words his lips speak not, and all his deeds are ill / If neighbour he defame not, there's good within him still
items.en_prose: Though one do not even speak of virtue and live in sin, it will be well if it be said of him "he does not backbite."

items.translit: Aranazheei Allavai Seydhalin Theedhe / Puranazheeip Poiththu Nakai
items.en: Than he who virtue scorns, and evil deeds performs, more vile, Is he that slanders friend, then meets him with false smile
items.en_prose: To smile deceitfully (in another's presence) after having reviled him to his destruction (behind his back) is a greater evil than the commission of (every other) sin and the destruction of (every) virtue

items.translit: Purangoorip Poiththuyir Vaazhdhalin Saadhal / Arangootrum Aakkath Tharum
items.en: 'Tis greater gain of virtuous good for man to die, Than live to slander absent friend, and falsely praise when nigh
items.en_prose: Death rather than life will confer upon the deceitful backbiter the profit which (the treatises on) virtue point out

items.translit: Kannindru Kannarach Chollinum Sollarka / Munnindru Pinnokkaach Chol
items.en: In presence though unkindly words you speak, say not / In absence words whose ill result exceeds your thought
items.en_prose: Though you speak without kindness before another's face speak not in his absence words which regard not the evil subsequently resulting from it

items.translit: Aranjollum Nenjaththaan Anmai Puranjollum / Punmaiyaar Kaanap Patum
items.en: The slanderous meanness that an absent friend defames,'This man in words owns virtue, not in heart,' proclaims
items.en_prose: The emptiness of that man's mind who (merely) praises virtue will be seen from the meanness of reviling another behind his back

items.translit: Piranpazhi Kooruvaan Thanpazhi Yullum / Thirandherindhu Koorap Patum
items.en: Who on his neighbours' sins delights to dwell, The story of his sins, culled out with care, the world will tell
items.en_prose: The character of the faults of that man who publishes abroad the faults of others will be sought out and published

items.translit: Pakachchollik Kelirp Pirippar Nakachcholli / Natpaatal Thetraa Thavar
items.en: With friendly art who know not pleasant words to say, Speak words that sever hearts, and drive choice friends away
items.en_prose: Those who know not to live in friendship with amusing conversation will by back-biting estrange even their relatives

items.translit: Thunniyaar Kutramum Thootrum Marapinaar / Ennaikol Edhilaar Maattu
items.en: Whose nature bids them faults of closest friends proclaim / What mercy will they show to other men's good name
items.en_prose: What will those not do to strangers whose nature leads them to publish abroad the faults of their intimate friends ?

items.translit: Arannokki Aatrungol Vaiyam Purannokkip / Punsol Uraippaan Porai
items.en: 'Tis charity, I ween, that makes the earth sustain their load / Who, neighbours' absence watching, tales or slander tell abroad
items.en_prose: The world through charity supports the weight of those who reproach others observing their absence

items.translit: Edhilaar Kutrampol Thangutrang Kaankirpin / Theedhunto Mannum Uyirkku
items.en: If each his own, as neighbours' faults would scan, Could any evil hap to living man
items.en_prose: If they observed their own faults as they observe the faults of others, would any evil happen to men ?

items.translit: Pallaar Muniyap Payanila Solluvaan / Ellaarum Ellap Patum
items.en: Words without sense, while chafe the wise, Who babbles, him will all despise
items.en_prose: He who to the disgust of many speaks useless things will be despised by all

items.translit: Payanila Pallaarmun Sollal Nayanila / Nattaarkan Seydhalir Reedhu
items.en: Words without sense, where many wise men hear, to pour / Than deeds to friends ungracious done offendeth more
items.en_prose: To speak useless things in the presence of many is a greater evil than to do unkind things towards friends

items.translit: Nayanilan Enpadhu Sollum Payanila / Paarith Thuraikkum Urai
items.en: Diffusive speech of useless words proclaims / A man who never righteous wisdom gains
items.en_prose: That conversation in which a man utters forth useless things will say of him "he is without virtue."

items.translit: Nayansaaraa Nanmaiyin Neekkum Payansaaraap / Panpilsol Pallaa Rakaththu
items.en: Unmeaning, worthless words, said to the multitude, To none delight afford, and sever men from good
items.en_prose: The words devoid of profit or pleasure which a man speaks will, being inconsistent with virtue,

items.translit: Seermai Sirappotu Neengum Payanila / Neermai Yutaiyaar Solin
items.en: Gone are both fame and boasted excellence, When men of worth speak of words devoid of sense
items.en_prose: If the good speak vain words their eminence and excellence will leave them

items.translit: Payanil Sol Paaraattu Vaanai / Makanenal Makkat Padhati Yenal
items.en: Who makes display of idle words' inanity, Call him not man, -chaff of humanity
items.en_prose: Call not him a man who parades forth his empty words Call him the chaff of men

items.translit: Nayanila Sollinunj Cholluka Saandror / Payanila Sollaamai Nandru
items.en: Let those who list speak things that no delight afford,'Tis good for men of worth to speak no idle word
items.en_prose: Let the wise if they will, speak things without excellence; it will be well for them not to speak useless things

items.translit: Arumpayan Aayum Arivinaar Sollaar / Perumpayan Illaadha Sol
items.en: The wise who weigh the worth of every utterance, Speak none but words of deep significance
items.en_prose: The wise who seek after rare pleasures will not speak words that have not much weight in them

items.translit: Poruldheerndha Pochchaandhunj Chollaar Maruldheerndha / Maasaru Kaatchi Yavar
items.en: The men of vision pure, from wildering folly free, Not e'en in thoughtless hour, speak words of vanity
items.en_prose: Those wise men who are without faults and are freed from ignorance will not even forgetfully speak things that profit not

items.translit: Solluka Sollir Payanutaiya Sollarka / Sollir Payanilaach Chol
items.en: If speak you will, speak words that fruit afford, If speak you will, speak never fruitless word
items.en_prose: Speak what is useful, and speak not useless words

items.translit: Theevinaiyaar Anjaar Vizhumiyaar Anjuvar / Theevinai Ennum Serukku
items.en: With sinful act men cease to feel the dread of ill within, The excellent will dread the wanton pride of cherished sin
items.en_prose: Those who have experience of evil deeds will not fear, but the excellent will fear the pride of sin

items.translit: Theeyavai Theeya Payaththalaal Theeyavai / Theeyinum Anjap Patum
items.en: Since evils new from evils ever grow, Evil than fire works out more dreaded woe
items.en_prose: Because evil produces evil, therefore should evil be feared more than fire

items.translit: Arivinul Ellaan Thalaiyenpa Theeya / Seruvaarkkum Seyyaa Vital
items.en: Even to those that hate make no return of ill; So shalt thou wisdom's highest law, 'tis said, fulfil
items.en_prose: So shalt thou wisdom's highest law, 'tis said, fulfil

items.translit: Marandhum Piranketu Soozharka Soozhin / Aranjoozham Soozhndhavan Ketu
items.en: Though good thy soul forget, plot not thy neighbour's fall, Thy plans shall 'virtue's Power' by ruin to thyself forestall
items.en_prose: Even though forgetfulness meditate not the ruin of another Virtue will meditate the ruin of him who thus meditates

items.translit: Ilan Endru Theeyavai Seyyarka / Seyyin Ilanaakum Matrum Peyarththu
items.en: Make not thy poverty a plea for ill; Thy evil deeds will make thee poorer still
items.en_prose: Commit not evil, saying, "I am poor": if you do, you will become poorer still

items.translit: Theeppaala Thaanpirarkan Seyyarka Noippaala / Thannai Atalventaa Thaan
items.en: What ranks as evil spare to do, if thou would'st shun / Affliction sore through ill to thee by others done
items.en_prose: Let him not do evil to others who desires not that sorrows should pursue him

items.translit: Enaippakai Yutraarum Uyvar Vinaippakai / Veeyaadhu Pinsendru Atum
items.en: From every enmity incurred there is to 'scape, a way; The wrath of evil deeds will dog men's steps, and slay
items.en_prose: However great be the enmity men have incurred they may still live The enmity of sin will incessantly pursue and kill

items.translit: Theeyavai Seydhaar Ketudhal Nizhaldhannai / Veeyaadhu Atiurain Thatru
items.en: Man's shadow dogs his steps where'er he wends; Destruction thus on sinful deeds attends
items.en_prose: Destruction will dwell at the heels of those who commit evil even as their shadow that leaves them not

items.translit: Thannaiththaan Kaadhala Naayin Enaiththondrum / Thunnarka Theevinaip Paal
items.en: Beware, if to thyself thyself is dear, Lest thou to aught that ranks as ill draw near
items.en_prose: If a man love himself, let him not commit any sin however small

items.translit: Arungetan Enpadhu Arika Marungotith / Theevinai Seyyaan Enin
items.en: The man, to devious way of sin that never turned aside, From ruin rests secure, whatever ills betide
items.en_prose: Know ye that he is freed from destruction who commits no evil, going to neither side of the right path

items.translit: Kaimmaaru Ventaa Katappaatu Maarimaattu / En Aatrung Kollo Ulaku
items.en: Duty demands no recompense; to clouds of heaven, By men on earth, what answering gift is given
items.en_prose: Benevolence seeks not a return. What does the world give back to the clouds ?

items.translit: Thaalaatrith Thandha Porulellaam Thakkaarkku / Velaanmai Seydhar Poruttu
items.en: The worthy say, when wealth rewards their toil-spent hours, For uses of beneficence alone 'tis ours
items.en_prose: All the wealth acquired with perseverance by the worthy is for the exercise of benevolence

items.translit: Puththe Lulakaththum Eentum Peralaridhe / Oppuravin Nalla Pira
items.en: To 'due beneficence' no equal good we know, Amid the happy gods, or in this world below
items.en_prose: It is difficult to obtain another good equal to benevolence either in this world or in that of the gods

items.translit: Oththa Tharavon Uyirvaazhvaan Matraiyaan / Seththaarul Vaikkap Patum
items.en: Who knows what's human life's befitting grace, He lives; the rest 'mongst dead men have their place
items.en_prose: He truly lives who knows (and discharges) the proper duties (of benevolence) He who knows them not will be reckoned among the dead

items.translit: Ooruni Neernirain Thatre Ulakavaam / Perari Vaalan Thiru
items.en: The wealth of men who love the 'fitting way,' the truly wise, Is as when water fills the lake that village needs supplies
items.en_prose: The wealth of that man of eminent knowledge who desires to exercise the benevolence approved of by the world, is like the full waters of a city-tank

items.translit: Payanmaram Ulloorp Pazhuththatraal Selvam / Nayanutai Yaankan Patin
items.en: A tree that fruits in th' hamlet's central mart, Is wealth that falls to men of liberal heart
items.en_prose: The wealth of a man (possessed of the virtue) of benevolence is like the ripening of a fruitful tree in the midst of a town

items.translit: Marundhaakith Thappaa Maraththatraal Selvam / Perundhakai Yaankan Patin
items.en: Unfailing tree that healing balm distils from every part, Is ample wealth that falls to him of large and noble heart
items.en_prose: If wealth be in the possession of a man who has the great excellence (of benevolence), it is like a tree which as a medicine is an infallible cure for disease

items.translit: Itanil Paruvaththum Oppuravirku Olkaar / Katanari Kaatchi Yavar
items.en: E'en when resources fall, they weary not of 'kindness due,'-They to whom Duty's self appears in vision true
items.en_prose: The wise who know what is duty will not scant their benevolence even when they are without wealth

items.translit: Nayanutaiyaan Nalkoorndhaa Naadhal Seyumneera / Seyyaadhu Amaikalaa Vaaru
items.en: The kindly-hearted man is poor in this alone, When power of doing deeds of goodness he finds none
items.en_prose: The poverty of a benevolent man, is nothing but his inability to exercise the same

items.translit: Oppuravi Naalvarum Ketenin Aqdhoruvan / Vitrukkol Thakka Thutaiththu
items.en: Though by 'beneficence,' the loss of all should come,'Twere meet man sold himself, and bought it with the sum
items.en_prose: If it be said that loss will result from benevolence, such loss is worth being procured even by the sale of one's self

items.translit: Variyaarkkondru Eevadhe Eekaimar Rellaam / Kuriyedhirppai Neera Thutaiththu
items.en: Call that a gift to needy men thou dost dispense, All else is void of good, seeking for recompense
items.en_prose: To give to the destitute is true charity All other gifts have the nature of (what is done for) a measured return

items.translit: Nallaaru Eninum Kolaldheedhu Melulakam / Illeninum Eedhale Nandru
items.en: Though men declare it heavenward path, yet to receive is ill; Though upper heaven were not, to give is virtue still
items.en_prose: To beg is evil, even though it were said that it is a good path (to heaven) To give is good, even though it were said that those who do so cannot obtain heaven

items.translit: Ilanennum Evvam Uraiyaamai Eedhal / Kulanutaiyaan Kanne Yula
items.en: 'I've nought' is ne'er the high-born man's reply; He gives to those who raise themselves that cry
items.en_prose: (Even in a low state) not to adopt the mean expedient of saying "I have nothing," but to give, is the characteristic of the mad of noble birth

items.translit: Innaadhu Irakkap Patudhal Irandhavar / Inmukang Kaanum Alavu
items.en: The suppliants' cry for aid yields scant delight, Until you see his face with grateful gladness bright
items.en_prose: To see men begging from us in disagreeable, until we see their pleasant countenance

items.translit: Aatruvaar Aatral Pasiaatral Appasiyai / Maatruvaar Aatralin Pin
items.en: 'Mid devotees they're great who hunger's pangs sustain, Who hunger's pangs relieve a higher merit gain
items.en_prose: The power of those who perform penance is the power of enduring hunger It is inferior to the power of those who remove the hunger (of others)

items.translit: Atraar Azhipasi Theerththal Aqdhoruvan / Petraan Porulvaip Puzhi
items.en: Let man relieve the wasting hunger men endure; For treasure gained thus finds he treasure-house secure
items.en_prose: The removal of the killing hunger of the poor is the place for one to lay up his wealth

items.translit: Paaththoon Mareei Yavanaip Pasiyennum / Theeppini Theental Aridhu
items.en: Whose soul delights with hungry men to share his meal, The hand of hunger's sickness sore shall never feel
items.en_prose: The fiery disease of hunger shall never touch him who habitually distributes his food to others

items.translit: Eeththuvakkum Inpam Ariyaarkol Thaamutaimai / Vaiththizhakkum Vanka Navar
items.en: Delight of glad'ning human hearts with gifts do they not know.Men of unpitying eye, who hoard their wealth and lose it so
items.en_prose: Do the hard-eyed who lay up and lose their possessions not know the happiness which springs from the pleasure of giving ?

items.translit: Iraththalin Innaadhu Mandra Nirappiya / Thaame Thamiyar Unal
items.en: They keep their garners full, for self alone the board they spread;-'Tis greater pain, be sure, than begging daily bread
items.en_prose: Solitary and unshared eating for the sake of filling up one's own riches is certainly much more

items.translit: Saadhalin Innaadha Thillai Inidhadhooum / Eedhal Iyaiyaak Katai
items.en: 'Tis bitter pain to die, 'Tis worse to live.For him who nothing finds to give
items.en_prose: Nothing is more unpleasant than death: yet even that is pleasant where charity cannot be exercised

items.translit: Eedhal Isaipata Vaazhdhal Adhuvalladhu / Oodhiyam Illai Uyirkku
items.en: See that thy life the praise of generous gifts obtain; Save this for living man exists no real gain
items.en_prose: Give to the poor and live with praise There is no greater profit to man than that

items.translit: Uraippaar Uraippavai Ellaam Irappaarkkondru / Eevaarmel Nirkum Pukazh
items.en: The speech of all that speak agrees to crown / The men that give to those that ask, with fair renown
items.en_prose: Whatsoever is spoken in the world will abide as praise upon that man who gives alms to the poor

items.translit: Ondraa Ulakaththu Uyarndha Pukazhallaal / Pondraadhu Nirpadhon Ril
items.en: Save praise alone that soars on high, Nought lives on earth that shall not die
items.en_prose: There is nothing that stands forth in the world imperishable, except fame, exalted in solitary greatness

items.translit: Nilavarai Neelpukazh Aatrin Pulavaraip / Potraadhu Puththel Ulaku
items.en: If men do virtuous deeds by world-wide ample glory crowned, The heavens will cease to laud the sage for other gifts renowned
items.en_prose: If one has acquired extensive fame within the limits of this earth, the world of the Gods will no longer praise those sages who have attained that world

items.translit: Naththampol Ketum Uladhaakum Saakkaatum / Viththakark Kallaal Aridhu
items.en: Loss that is gain, and death of life's true bliss fulfilled, Are fruits which only wisdom rare can yield
items.en_prose: Prosperity to the body of fame, resulting in poverty to the body of flesh and the stability to the former arising from the death of the latter, are achievable only by the wise

items.translit: Thondrin Pukazhotu Thondruka Aqdhilaar / Thondralin Thondraamai Nandru
items.en: If man you walk the stage, appear adorned with glory's grace; Save glorious you can shine, 'twere better hide your face
items.en_prose: If you are born (in this world), be born with qualities conductive to fame From those who are destitute of them it will be better not to be born

items.translit: Pukazhpata Vaazhaadhaar Thannovaar Thammai / Ikazhvaarai Novadhu Evan?
items.en: If you your days will spend devoid of goodly fame, When men despise, why blame them? You've yourself to blame
items.en_prose: Why do those who cannot live with praise, grieve those who despise them, instead of grieving themselves for their own inability

items.translit: Vasaiyenpa Vaiyaththaark Kellaam Isaiyennum / Echcham Peraaa Vitin
items.en: Fame is virtue's child, they say; if, then, You childless live, you live the scorn of men
items.en_prose: Not to beget fame will be esteemed a disgrace by the wise in this world

items.translit: Vasaiyilaa Vanpayan Kundrum Isaiyilaa / Yaakkai Poruththa Nilam
items.en: The blameless fruits of fields' increase will dwindle down, If earth the burthen bear of men without renown
items.en_prose: The ground which supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce

items.translit: Vasaiyozhiya Vaazhvaare Vaazhvaar Isaiyozhiya / Vaazhvaare Vaazhaa Thavar
items.en: Who live without reproach, them living men we deem; Who live without renown, live not, though living men they seem
items.en_prose: Those live who live without disgrace Those who live without fame live not

items.translit: Arutchelvam Selvaththul Selvam Porutchelvam / Pooriyaar Kannum Ula
items.en: Wealth 'mid wealth is wealth 'kindliness'; Wealth of goods the vilest too possess
items.en_prose: The wealth of kindness is wealth of wealth, in as much as the wealth of property is possessed by the basest of men

items.translit: Nallaatraal Naati Arulaalka Pallaatraal / Therinum Aqdhe Thunai
items.en: The law of 'grace' fulfil, by methods good due trial made, Though many systems you explore, this is your only aid
items.en_prose: (Stand) in the good path, consider, and be kind. Even considering according to the conflicting tenets of the different sects, kindness will be your best aid, (in the acquisition of heavenly bliss.)

items.translit: Arulserndha Nenjinaark Killai Irulserndha / Innaa Ulakam Pukal
items.en: They in whose breast a 'gracious kindliness' resides, See not the gruesome world, where darkness drear abides
