items.en_prose: They will never enter the world of darkness and wretchedness whose minds are the abode of kindness

items.translit: Mannuyir Ompi Arulaalvaarkku Illenpa / Thannuyir Anjum Vinai
items.en: Who for undying souls of men provides with gracious zeal, In his own soul the dreaded guilt of sin shall never feel
items.en_prose: (The wise) say that the evils, which his soul would dread, will never come upon the man who exercises kindness and protects the life (of other creatures)

items.translit: Allal Arulaalvaarkku Illai Valivazhangum / Mallanmaa Gnaalang Kari
items.en: The teeming earth's vast realm, round which the wild winds blow, Is witness, men of 'grace' no woeful want shall know
items.en_prose: This great rich earth over which the wind blows, is a witness that sorrow never comes upon the kindhearted

items.translit: Porulneengip Pochchaandhaar Enpar Arulneengi / Allavai Seydhozhuku Vaar
items.en: Gain of true wealth oblivious they eschew, Who 'grace' forsake, and graceless actions do
items.en_prose: (The wise) say that those who neglect kindness and practise cruelties, neglected virtue (in their former birth), and forgot (the sorrows which they must suffer.)

items.translit: Arulillaarkku Avvulakam Illai Porulillaarkku / Ivvulakam Illaaki Yaangu
items.en: As to impoverished men this present world is not; The 'graceless' in you world have neither part nor lot
items.en_prose: As this world is not for those who are without wealth, so that world is not for those who are without kindness

items.translit: Porulatraar Pooppar Orukaal Arulatraar / Atraarmar Raadhal Aridhu
items.en: Who lose the flower of wealth, when seasons change, again may bloom; Who lose 'benevolence', lose all; nothing can change their doom
items.en_prose: Those who are without wealth may, at some future time, become prosperous; those who are destitute of kindness are utterly destitute; for them there is no change

items.translit: Therulaadhaan Meypporul Kantatraal Therin / Arulaadhaan Seyyum Aram
items.en: When souls unwise true wisdom's mystic vision see, The 'graceless' man may work true works of charity
items.en_prose: If you consider, the virtue of him who is without kindness is like the perception of the true being by him who is without wisdom

items.translit: Valiyaarmun Thannai Ninaikka Thaan / Thannin Meliyaarmel Sellu Mitaththu
items.en: When weaker men you front with threat'ning brow, Think how you felt in presence of some stronger foe
items.en_prose: When a man is about to rush upon those who are weaker than himself, let him remember how he has stood (trembling) before those who are stronger than himself

items.translit: Thannoon Perukkarkuth Thaanpiridhu Oonunpaan / Engnganam Aalum Arul?
items.en: How can the wont of 'kindly grace' to him be known, Who other creatures' flesh consumes to feed his own
items.en_prose: How can he be possessed of kindness, who to increase his own flesh, eats the flesh of other creatures

items.translit: Porulaatchi Potraadhaarkku Illai Arulaatchi / Aangillai Oondhin Pavarkku
items.en: No use of wealth have they who guard not their estate; No use of grace have they with flesh who hunger sate
items.en_prose: As those possess no property who do not take care of it, so those possess no kindness who feed on flesh

items.translit: Pataikontaar Nenjampol Nannookkaadhu Ondran / Utalsuvai Untaar Manam
items.en: Like heart of them that murderous weapons bear, his mind, Who eats of savoury meat, no joy in good can find
items.en_prose: Like the (murderous) mind of him who carries a weapon (in his hand), the mind of him who feasts with pleasure on the body of another (creature), has no regard for goodness

items.translit: Arulalladhu Yaadhenin Kollaamai Koral / Porulalladhu Avvoon Thinal
items.en: 'What's grace, or lack of grace'? 'To kill' is this, that 'not to kill'; To eat dead flesh can never worthy end fulfil
items.en_prose: If it be asked what is kindness and what its opposite, the answer would be preservation and destruction of life; and therefore it is not right to feed on the flesh (obtained by taking away life)

items.translit: Unnaamai Ulladhu Uyirnilai Oonunna / Annaaththal Seyyaadhu Alaru
items.en: If flesh you eat not, life's abodes unharmed remain; Who eats, hell swallows him, and renders not again
items.en_prose: Not to eat flesh contributes to the continuance of life; therefore if a man eat flesh, hell will not open its mouth (to let him escape out, after he has once fallen in)

items.translit: Thinarporuttaal Kollaadhu Ulakenin Yaarum / Vilaipporuttaal Oondraruvaa Ril
items.en: 'We eat the slain,' you say, by us no living creatures die; Who'd kill and sell, I pray, if none came there the flesh to buy
items.en_prose: If the world does not destroy life for the purpose of eating, then no one would sell flesh for the sake of money

items.translit: Unnaamai Ventum Pulaaal Piridhondran / Punnadhu Unarvaarp Perin
items.en: With other beings' ulcerous wounds their hunger they appease; If this they felt, desire to eat must surely cease
items.en_prose: If men should come to know that flesh is nothing but the unclean ulcer of a body, let them abstain from eating it

items.translit: Seyirin Thalaippirindha Kaatchiyaar Unnaar / Uyirin Thalaippirindha Oon
items.en: Whose souls the vision pure and passionless perceive, Eat not the bodies men of life bereave
items.en_prose: The wise, who have freed themselves from mental delusion, will not eat the flesh which has been severed from an animal

items.translit: Avisorin Thaayiram Vettalin Ondran / Uyirsekuth Thunnaamai Nandru
items.en: Than thousand rich oblations, with libations rare, Better the flesh of slaughtered beings not to share
items.en_prose: Not to kill and eat (the flesh of) an animal, is better than the pouring forth of ghee etc, in a thousand sacrifices

items.translit: Kollaan Pulaalai Maruththaanaik Kaikooppi / Ellaa Uyirun Thozhum
items.en: Who slays nought,- flesh rejects- his feet before / All living things with clasped hands adore
items.en_prose: All creatures will join their hands together, and worship him who has never taken away life, nor eaten flesh

items.translit: Utranoi Nondral Uyirkkurukan Seyyaamai / Atre Thavaththir Kuru
items.en: To bear due penitential pains, while no offence / He causes others, is the type of 'penitence'
items.en_prose: The nature of religious discipline consists, in the endurance (by the ascetic) of the sufferings which it brings on himself, and in abstaining from giving pain to others

items.translit: Thavamum Thavamutaiyaarkku Aakum Adhanai / Aqdhilaar Merkol Vadhu
items.en: To 'penitents' sincere avails their 'penitence'; Where that is not, 'tis but a vain pretence
items.en_prose: Austerities can only be borne, and their benefits enjoyed, by those who have practised them (in a former birth); it will be useless for those who have not done so, to attempt to practise them (now)

items.translit: Thurandhaarkkuth Thuppuravu Venti Marandhaarkol / Matrai Yavarkal Thavam
items.en: Have other men forgotten 'penitence' who strive / To earn for penitents the things by which they live
items.en_prose: It is to provide food etc, for the ascetics who have abandoned (the desire of earthly possessions) that other persons have forgotten (to practise) austerity ?

items.translit: Onnaarth Theralum Uvandhaarai Aakkalum / Ennin Thavaththaan Varum
items.en: Destruction to his foes, to friends increase of joy / The 'penitent' can cause, if this his thoughts employ
items.en_prose: If (the ascetic) desire the destruction of his enemies, or the aggrandizement of his friends, it will be effected by (the power of) his austerities

items.translit: Ventiya Ventiyaang Keydhalaal Seydhavam / Eentu Muyalap Patum
items.en: That what they wish may, as they wish, be won, By men on earth are works of painful 'penance' done
items.en_prose: Religious dislipline is practised in this world, because it secures the attainment of whatever one may wish to enjoy (in the world to come)

items.translit: Thavanj Cheyvaar Thangarumanj Cheyvaarmar / Rallaar Avanjeyvaar Aasaiyut Pattu
items.en: Who works of 'penance' do, their end attain, Others in passion's net enshared, toil but in vain
items.en_prose: Those discharge their duty who perform austerities; all others accomplish their own destruction, through the entanglement of the desire (of riches and sensual pleasure)

items.translit: Sutachchutarum Ponpol Olivitum Thunpanjjch / Utachchuta Norkir Pavarkku
items.en: The hotter glows the fining fire, the gold the brighter shines; The pain of penitence, like fire, the soul of man refines
items.en_prose: Just as gold is purified as heated in the fire, will those shine, who have endured the burning of pain (in frequent austerities)

items.translit: Thannuyir Thaanarap Petraanai Enaiya / Mannuyi Rellaan Thozhum
items.en: Who gains himself in utter self-control, Him worships every other living soul
items.en_prose: All other creatures will worship him who has attained the control of his own soul

items.translit: Kootram Kudhiththalum Kaikootum Notralin / Aatral Thalaippat Tavarkkul
items.en: E'en over death the victory he may gain, If power by penance won his soul obtain
items.en_prose: Those who have attained the power which religious discipline confers, will be able also to pass the limit of Yama, (the God of death)

items.translit: Ilarpala Raakiya Kaaranam Norpaar / Silarpalar Nolaa Thavar
items.en: The many all things lack! The cause is plain, The 'penitents' are few The many shun such pain
items.en_prose: Because there are few who practise austerity and many who do not, there are many destitute and few rich in this world

items.translit: Vanja Manaththaan Patitrozhukkam Poodhangal / Aindhum Akaththe Nakum
items.en: Who with deceitful mind in false way walks of covert sin, The five-fold elements his frame compose, decide within
items.en_prose: The five elements (of his body) will laugh within him at the feigned conduct of the deceitful minded man

items.translit: Vaanuyar Thotram Evanseyyum Thannenjam / Thaanari Kutrap Patin
items.en: What gain, though virtue's semblance high as heaven his fame exalt, If heart dies down through sense of self-detected fault
items.en_prose: What avails an appearance (of sanctity) high as heaven, if his mind suffers (the indulgence) of conscious sin

items.translit: Valiyil Nilaimaiyaan Valluruvam Petram / Puliyindhol Porththumeyn Thatru
items.en: As if a steer should graze wrapped round with tiger's skin, Is show of virtuous might when weakness lurks within
items.en_prose: The assumed appearance of power, by a man who has no power (to restrain his senses and perform austerity), is like a cow feeding on grass covered with a tiger's skin

items.translit: Thavamaraindhu Allavai Seydhal Pudhalmaraindhu / Vettuvan Pulsimizhth Thatru
items.en: 'Tis as a fowler, silly birds to snare, in thicket lurks / When, clad in stern ascetic garb, one secret evil works
items.en_prose: He who hides himself under the mask of an ascetic and commits sins, like a sportsman who conceals himself in the thicket to catch birds

items.translit: Patratrem Enpaar Patitrozhukkam Etretrendru / Edham Palavun Tharum
items.en: 'Our souls are free,' who say, yet practise evil secretly,'What folly have we wrought!' by many shames o'er-whelmed, shall cry
items.en_prose: The false conduct of those who say they have renounced all desire will one day bring them sorrows that will make them cry out, "Oh! what have we done, what have we done."

items.translit: Nenjin Thuravaar Thurandhaarpol Vanjiththu / Vaazhvaarin Vankanaar Il
items.en: In mind renouncing nought, in speech renouncing every tie, Who guileful live,- no men are found than these of 'harder eye'
items.en_prose: Amongst living men there are none so hard-hearted as those who without to saking (desire) in their heart, falsely take the appearance of those who have forsaken (it)

items.translit: Purangundri Kantanaiya Renum Akangundri / Mukkir Kariyaar Utaiththu
items.en: Outward, they shine as 'kunri' berry's scarlet bright; Inward, like tip of 'kunri' bead, as black as night
items.en_prose: (The world) contains persons whose outside appears (as fair) as the (red) berry of the Abrus, but whose inside is as black as the nose of that berry

items.translit: Manaththadhu Maasaaka Maantaar Neeraati / Maraindhozhuku Maandhar Palar
items.en: Many wash in hollowed waters, living lives of hidden shame; Foul in heart, yet high upraised of men in virtuous fame
items.en_prose: There are many men of masked conduct, who perform their ablutions, and (make a show) of

items.translit: Kanaikotidhu Yaazhkotu Sevvidhuaang Kanna / Vinaipatu Paalaal Kolal
items.en: Cruel is the arrow straight, the crooked lute is sweet, Judge by their deeds the many forms of men you meet
items.en_prose: As, in its use, the arrow is crooked, and the curved lute is straight, so by their deeds, (and not by their appearance) let (the uprightness or crookedness of) men be estimated

items.translit: Mazhiththalum Neettalum Ventaa Ulakam / Pazhiththadhu Ozhiththu Vitin
items.en: What's the worth of shaven head or tresses long, If you shun what all the world condemns as wrong
items.en_prose: There is no need of a shaven crown, nor of tangled hair, if a man abstain from those deeds which the wise have condemned

items.translit: Ellaamai Ventuvaan Enpaan Enaiththondrum / Kallaamai Kaakkadhan Nenju
items.en: Who seeks heaven's joys, from impious levity secure, Let him from every fraud preserve his spirit pure
items.en_prose: Let him, who desires not to be despised, keep his mind from (the desire of) defrauding another of the smallest thing

items.translit: Ullaththaal Ullalum Theedhe Piranporulaik / Kallaththaal Kalvem Enal
items.en: 'Tis sin if in the mind man but thought conceive;'By fraud I will my neighbour of his wealth bereave.'
items.en_prose: Even the thought (of sin) is sin; think not then of crafiily stealing the property of another

items.translit: Kalavinaal Aakiya Aakkam Alavirandhu / Aavadhu Polak Ketum
items.en: The gain that comes by fraud, although it seems to grow / With limitless increase, to ruin swift shall go
items.en_prose: The property, which is acquired by fraud, will entirely perish, even while it seems to increase

items.translit: Kalavinkan Kandriya Kaadhal Vilaivinkan / Veeyaa Vizhumam Tharum
items.en: The lust inveterate of fraudful gain, Yields as its fruit undying pain
items.en_prose: The eager desire of defrauding others will, when it brings forth its fruit, produce undying sorrow

items.translit: Arulkarudhi Anputaiya Raadhal Porulkarudhip / Pochchaappup Paarppaarkan Il
items.en: 'Grace' is not in their thoughts, nor know they kind affection's power, Who neighbour's goods desire, and watch for his unguarded hour
items.en_prose: The study of kindness and the exercise of benevolence is not with those who watch for another's forgetfulness, though desire of his property

items.translit: Alavinkan Nindrozhukal Aatraar Kalavinkan / Kandriya Kaadha Lavar
items.en: They cannot walk restrained in wisdom's measured bound, In whom inveterate lust of fraudful gain is found
items.en_prose: They cannot walk steadfastly, according to rule, who eagerly desire to defraud others

items.translit: Kalavennum Kaarari Vaanmai Alavennum / Aatral Purindhaarkanta Il
items.en: Practice of fraud's dark cunning arts they shun, Who long for power by 'measured wisdom' won
items.en_prose: That black-knowledge which is called fraud, is not in those who desire that greatness which is called rectitude

items.translit: Alavarindhaar Nenjath Tharampola Nirkum / Kalavarindhaar Nenjil Karavu
items.en: As virtue dwells in heart that 'measured wisdom' gains; Deceit in hearts of fraudful men established reigns
items.en_prose: Deceit dwells in the mind of those who are conversant with fraud, even as virtue in the minds of those who are conversant with rectitude

items.translit: Alavalla Seydhaange Veevar Kalavalla / Matraiya Thetraa Thavar
items.en: Who have no lore save that which fraudful arts supply, Acts of unmeasured vice committing straightway die
items.en_prose: Those, who are acquainted with nothing but fraud, will perish in the very commission of transgression

items.translit: Kalvaarkkuth Thallum Uyirnilai Kalvaarkkuth / Thallaadhu Puththe Lulaku
items.en: The fraudful forfeit life and being here below; Who fraud eschew the bliss of heavenly beings know
items.en_prose: Even their body will fail the fraudulent; but even the world of the gods will not fail those who are free from fraud

items.translit: Vaaimai Enappatuvadhu Yaadhenin Yaadhondrum / Theemai Ilaadha Solal
items.en: You ask, in lips of men what 'truth' may be;'Tis speech from every taint of evil free
items.en_prose: Truth is the speaking of such words as are free from the least degree of evil (to others)

items.translit: Poimaiyum Vaaimai Yitaththa Puraidheerndha / Nanmai Payakkum Enin
items.en: Falsehood may take the place of truthful word, If blessing, free from fault, it can afford
items.en_prose: Even falsehood has the nature of truth, if it confer a benefit that is free from fault

items.translit: Thannenj Charivadhu Poiyarka Poiththapin / Thannenje Thannaich Chutum
items.en: Speak not a word which false thy own heart knows / Self-kindled fire within the false one's spirit glows
items.en_prose: Let not a man knowingly tell a lie; for after he has told the lie, his mind will burn him (with the memory of his guilt)

items.translit: Ullaththaar Poiyaa Thozhukin Ulakaththaar / Ullaththu Lellaam Ulan
items.en: True to his inmost soul who lives,- enshrined / He lives in souls of all mankind
items.en_prose: He who, in his conduct, preserves a mind free from deceit, will dwell in the minds of all men

items.translit: Manaththotu Vaaimai Mozhiyin Thavaththotu / Thaananjey Vaarin Thalai
items.en: Greater is he who speaks the truth with full consenting mind / Than men whose lives have penitence and charity combined
items.en_prose: He, who speaks truth with all his heart, is superior to those who make gifts and practise austerities

items.translit: Poiyaamai Anna Pukazhillai Eyyaamai / Ellaa Aramun Tharum
items.en: No praise like that of words from falsehood free; This every virtue yields spontaneously
items.en_prose: There is no praise like the praise of never uttering a falsehood: without causing any suffering, it will lead to every virtue

items.translit: Poiyaamai Poiyaamai Aatrin Arampira / Seyyaamai Seyyaamai Nandru
items.en: If all your life be utter truth, the truth alone,'Tis well, though other virtuous acts be left undone
items.en_prose: If a man has the power to abstain from falsehood, it will be well with him, even though he practise no other virtue

items.translit: Puraldhooimai Neeraan Amaiyum Akandhooimai / Vaaimaiyaal Kaanap Patum
items.en: Outward purity the water will bestow; Inward purity from truth alone will flow
items.en_prose: Purity of body is produced by water and purity of mind by truthfulness

items.translit: Ellaa Vilakkum Vilakkalla Saandrorkkup / Poiyaa Vilakke Vilakku
items.en: Every lamp is not a lamp in wise men's sight; That's the lamp with truth's pure radiance bright
items.en_prose: All lamps of nature are not lamps; the lamp of truth is the lamp of the wise

items.translit: Yaameyyaak Kantavatrul Illai Enaiththondrum / Vaaimaiyin Nalla Pira
items.en: Of all good things we've scanned with studious care, There's nought that can with truthfulness compare
items.en_prose: Amidst all that we have seen (described) as real (excellence), there is nothing so good as truthfulness

items.translit: Sellitaththuk Kaappaan Sinangaappaan Allitaththuk / Kaakkinen Kaavaakkaal En?
items.en: Where thou hast power thy angry will to work, thy wrath restrain; Where power is none, what matter if thou check or give it rein
items.en_prose: He restrains his anger who restrains it when it can injure; when it cannot injure, what does it matter whether he restrain it, or not ?

items.translit: Sellaa Itaththuch Chinandheedhu Sellitaththum / Iladhanin Theeya Pira
items.en: Where power is none to wreak thy wrath, wrath importent is ill; Where thou hast power thy will to work, 'tis greater, evil still
items.en_prose: Anger is bad, even when it cannot injure; when it can injure; there is no greater evil

items.translit: Maraththal Vekuliyai Yaarmaattum Theeya / Piraththal Adhanaan Varum
items.en: If any rouse thy wrath, the trespass straight forget; For wrath an endless train of evils will beget
items.en_prose: Forget anger towards every one, as fountains of evil spring from it

items.translit: Nakaiyum Uvakaiyum Kollum Sinaththin / Pakaiyum Ulavo Pira
items.en: Wrath robs the face of smiles, the heart of joy, What other foe to man works such annoy
items.en_prose: What other foe to man works such annoy?

items.translit: Thannaiththaan Kaakkin Sinangaakka Kaavaakkaal / Thannaiye Kollunj Chinam
items.en: If thou would'st guard thyself, guard against wrath alway;'Gainst wrath who guards not, him his wrath shall slay
items.en_prose: If a man would guard himself, let him guard against anger; if he do not guard it, anger will kill him

items.translit: Sinamennum Serndhaaraik Kolli Inamennum / Emap Punaiyaich Chutum
items.en: Wrath, the fire that slayeth whose draweth near, Will burn the helpful 'raft' of kindred dear
items.en_prose: The fire of anger will burn up even the pleasant raft of friendship

items.translit: Sinaththaip Porulendru Kontavan Ketu / Nilaththaraindhaan Kaipizhaiyaa Thatru
items.en: The hand that smites the earth unfailing feels the sting; So perish they who nurse their wrath as noble thing
items.en_prose: Destruction will come upon him who ragards anger as a good thing, as surely as the hand of him who strikes the ground will not fail

items.translit: Inareri Thoivanna Innaa Seyinum / Punarin Vekulaamai Nandru
items.en: Though men should work thee woe, like touch of tongues of fire'Tis well if thou canst save thy soul from burning ire
items.en_prose: Though one commit things against you as painful (to bear) as if a bundle of fire had been thrust upon you, it will be well, to refrain, if possible, from anger

items.translit: Ulliya Thellaam Utaneydhum Ullaththaal / Ullaan Vekuli Enin
items.en: If man his soul preserve from wrathful fires, He gains with that whate'er his soul desires
items.en_prose: If a man never indulges anger in his heart, he will at once obtain whatever he has thought of

items.translit: Irandhaar Irandhaar Anaiyar Sinaththaith / Thurandhaar Thurandhaar Thunai
items.en: Men of surpassing wrath are like the men who've passed away; Who wrath renounce, equals of all-renouncing sages they
items.en_prose: Those, who give way to excessive anger, are no better than dead men; but those, who are freed from it, are equal to those who are freed (from death)

items.translit: Sirappeenum Selvam Perinum Pirarkku / Innaa Seyyaamai Maasatraar Kol
items.en: Though ill to neighbour wrought should glorious pride of wealth secure, No ill to do is fixed decree of men in spirit pure
items.en_prose: It is the determination of the spotless not to cause sorrow to others, although they could (by so causing) obtain the wealth which confers greatness

items.translit: Karuththuinnaa Seydhavak Kannum Maruththinnaa / Seyyaamai Maasatraar Kol
items.en: Though malice work its worst, planning no ill return, to endure, And work no ill, is fixed decree of men in spirit pure
items.en_prose: It is the determination of the spotless not to do evil, even in return, to those who have cherished enmity and done them evil

items.translit: Seyyaamal Setraarkkum Innaadha Seydhapin / Uyyaa Vizhuman Tharum
items.en: Though unprovoked thy soul malicious foes should sting, Retaliation wrought inevitable woes will bring
items.en_prose: In an ascetic inflict suffering even on those who hate him, when he has not done them any evil, it will afterwards give him irretrievable sorrow

items.translit: Innaasey Thaarai Oruththal Avarnaana / Nannayanj Cheydhu Vital
items.en: To punish wrong, with kindly benefits the doers ply; Thus shame their souls; but pass the ill unheeded by
items.en_prose: The (proper) punishment to those who have done evil (to you), is to put them to shame by showing them kindness, in return and to forget both the evil and the good done on both sides

items.translit: Arivinaan Aakuva Thunto Piridhinnoi / Thannoipol Potraak Katai
items.en: From wisdom's vaunted lore what doth the learner gain, If as his own he guard not others' souls from pain
items.en_prose: What benefit has he derived from his knowledge, who does not endeavour to keep off pain from another as much as from himself ?

items.translit: Innaa Enaththaan Unarndhavai Thunnaamai / Ventum Pirankan Seyal
items.en: What his own soul has felt as bitter pain, From making others feel should man abstain
items.en_prose: Let not a man consent to do those things to another which, he knows, will cause sorrow

items.translit: Enaiththaanum Egngnaandrum Yaarkkum Manaththaanaam / Maanaasey Yaamai Thalai
items.en: To work no wilful woe, in any wise, through all the days, To any living soul, is virtue's highest praise
items.en_prose: It is the chief of all virtues not knowingly to do any person evil, even in the lowest degree, and at any time

items.translit: Thannuyirkaku Ennaamai Thaanarivaan Enkolo / Mannuyirkku Innaa Seyal
items.en: Whose soul has felt the bitter smart of wrong, how can / He wrongs inflict on ever-living soul of man
items.en_prose: Why does a man inflict upon other creatures those sufferings, which he has found by experience are sufferings to himself ?

items.translit: Pirarkkinnaa Murpakal Seyyin Thamakku / Innaa Pirpakal Thaame Varum
items.en: If, ere the noontide, you to others evil do, Before the eventide will evil visit you
items.en_prose: If a man inflict sorrow upon others in the morning, it will come upon him unsought in the very evening

items.translit: Noyellaam Noiseydhaar Melavaam Noiseyyaar / Noyinmai Ventu Pavar
items.en: O'er every evil-doer evil broodeth still; He evil shuns who freedom seeks from ill
items.en_prose: Sorrow will come upon those who cause pain to others; therfore those, who desire to be free from sorrow, give no pain to others

items.translit: Aravinai Yaadhenin Kollaamai Koral / Piravinai Ellaan Tharum
items.en: What is the work of virtue? 'Not to kill'; For 'killing' leads to every work of ill
items.en_prose: Never to destroy life is the sum of all virtuous conduct The destruction of life leads to every evil

items.translit: Pakuththuntu Palluyir Ompudhal Noolor / Thokuththavatrul Ellaan Thalai
items.en: Let those that need partake your meal; guard every-thing that lives; This the chief and sum of lore that hoarded wisdom gives
items.en_prose: The chief of all (the virtues) which authors have summed up, is the partaking of food that has been shared with others, and the preservation of the mainfold life of other creatures

items.translit: Ondraaka Nalladhu Kollaamai Matradhan / Pinsaarap Poiyaamai Nandru
items.en: Alone, first of goods things, is 'not to slay'; The second is, no untrue word to say
items.en_prose: Not to destroy life is an incomparably (great) good next to it in goodness ranks freedom from falsehood

items.translit: Nallaaru Enappatuvadhu Yaadhenin Yaadhondrum / Kollaamai Soozhum Neri
items.en: You ask, What is the good and perfect way?'Tis path of him who studies nought to slay
items.en_prose: Good path is that which considers how it may avoid killing any creature

items.translit: Nilaianji Neeththaarul Ellaam Kolaianjik / Kollaamai Soozhvaan Thalai
items.en: Of those who 'being' dread, and all renounce, the chief are they, Who dreading crime of slaughter, study nought to slay
items.en_prose: Of all those who, fearing the permanence of earthly births, have abandoned desire, he is the chief who, fearing (the guilt of) murder, considers how he may avoid the destruction of life

items.translit: Kollaamai Merkon Tozhukuvaan Vaazhnaalmel / Sellaadhu Uyirunnung Kootru
items.en: Ev'n death that life devours, their happy days shall spare, Who law, 'Thou shall not kill', uphold with reverent care
items.en_prose: Yama, the destroyer of life, will not attack the life of him, who acts under the determination of never destroying life

items.translit: Thannuyir Neeppinum Seyyarka Thaanpiridhu / Innuyir Neekkum Vinai
items.en: Though thine own life for that spared life the price must pay, Take not from aught that lives gift of sweet life away
items.en_prose: Let no one do that which would destroy the life of another, although he should by so doing, lose his own life

items.translit: Nandraakum Aakkam Peridheninum Saandrorkkuk / Kondraakum Aakkang Katai
items.en: Though great the gain of good should seem, the wise / Will any gain by staughter won despise
items.en_prose: The advantage which might flow from destroying life in sacrifice, is dishonourable to the wise (who renounced the world), even although it should be said to be productive of great good

items.translit: Kolaivinaiya Raakiya Maakkal Pulaivinaiyar / Punmai Therivaa Rakaththu
items.en: Whose trade is 'killing', always vile they show, To minds of them who what is vileness know
items.en_prose: To minds of them who what is vileness know

items.translit: Uyir Utampin Neekkiyaar Enpa / Seyir Utampin Sellaaththee Vaazhkkai
items.en: Who lead a loathed life in bodies sorely pained, Are men, the wise declare, by guilt of slaughter stained
items.en_prose: (The wise) will say that men of diseased bodies, who live in degradation and in poverty, are those who separated the life from the body of animals (in a former birth)

items.translit: Nillaadha Vatrai Nilaiyina Endrunarum / Pullari Vaanmai Katai
items.en: Lowest and meanest lore, that bids men trust secure, In things that pass away, as things that shall endure
items.en_prose: That ignorance which considers those things to be stable which are not so, is dishonourable (to the wise)

items.translit: Kooththaattu Avaik Kuzhaath Thatre / Perunjelvam Pokkum Adhuvilin Thatru
items.en: As crowds round dancers fill the hall, is wealth's increase; Its loss, as throngs dispersing, when the dances cease
items.en_prose: The acquisition of wealth is like the gathering together of an assembly for a theatre; its expenditure is like the breaking up of that assembly

items.translit: Arkaa Iyalpitruch Chelvam Adhupetraal / Arkupa Aange Seyal
items.en: Unenduring is all wealth; if you wealth enjoy, Enduring works in working wealth straightway employ
items.en_prose: Wealth is perishable; let those who obtain it immediately practise those (virtues) which are imperishable

items.translit: Naalena Ondrupor Kaatti Uyir / Eerum Vaaladhu Unarvaarp Perin
items.en: As 'day' it vaunts itself; well understood, 'tis knife', That daily cuts away a portion from thy life
items.en_prose: Time, which shows itself (to the ignorant) as if it were something (real) is in the estimation of the wise (only) a saw which cuts down life

items.translit: Naachchetru Vikkulmel Vaaraamun Nalvinai / Mersendru Seyyap Patum
items.en: Before the tongue lie powerless, 'mid the gasp of gurgling breath, Arouse thyself, and do good deeds beyond the power of death
items.en_prose: Let virtuous deeds be done quickly, before the hiccup comes making the tongue silent

items.translit: Nerunal Ulanoruvan Indrillai Ennum / Perumai Utaiththuiv Vulaku
items.en: Existing yesterday, today to nothing hurled!-Such greatness owns this transitory world
items.en_prose: This world possesses the greatness that one who yesterday was is not today

items.translit: Orupozhudhum Vaazhvadhu Ariyaar Karudhupa / Kotiyum Alla Pala
items.en: Who know not if their happy lives shall last the day, In fancies infinite beguile the hours away
items.en_prose: Innumerable are the thoughts which occupy the mind of (the unwise), who know not that they shall live another moment

items.translit: Kutampai Thaniththu Ozhiyap Pulparan / Thatre Utampotu Uyiritai Natpu
items.en: Birds fly away, and leave the nest deserted bare; Such is the short-lived friendship soul and body share
items.en_prose: The love of the soul to the body is like (the love of) a bird to its egg which it flies away from and leaves empty

items.translit: Urangu Vadhupolunj Chaakkaatu Urangi / Vizhippadhu Polum Pirappu
items.en: Death is sinking into slumbers deep; Birth again is waking out of sleep
items.en_prose: Death is like sleep; birth is like awaking from it

items.translit: Pukkil Amaindhindru Kollo Utampinul / Thuchchil Irundha Uyirkku
items.en: The soul in fragile shed as lodger courts repose:-Is it because no home's conclusive rest it knows
items.en_prose: It seems as if the soul, which takes a temporary shelter in a body, had not attained a home

items.translit: Yaadhanin Yaadhanin Neengiyaan Nodhal / Adhanin Adhanin Ilan
items.en: From whatever, aye, whatever, man gets free, From what, aye, from that, no more of pain hath he
items.en_prose: Whatever thing, a man has renounced, by that thing; he cannot suffer pain

items.translit: Ventin Un Taakath Thurakka / Thurandhapin Eentuiyar Paala Pala
items.en: 'Renunciation' made- ev'n here true pleasures men acquire;'Renounce' while time is yet, if to those pleasures you aspire
items.en_prose: After a man has renounced (all things), there will still be many things in this world (which he may enjoy); if he should desire them, let him, while it is time abandon (the world)

items.translit: Atalventum Aindhan Pulaththai Vitalventum / Ventiya Vellaam Orungu
items.en: 'Perceptions of the five' must all expire;-Relinquished in its order each desire
items.en_prose: Let the five senses be destroyed; and at the same time, let everything be abandoned that (the ascetic) has (formerly) desired

items.translit: Iyalpaakum Nonpirkondru Inmai Utaimai / Mayalaakum Matrum Peyarththu
items.en: 'Privation absolute' is penance true;'Possession' brings bewilderment anew
items.en_prose: To be altogether destitute is the proper condition of those who perform austerities; if they possess anything, it will change (their resolution) and bring them back to their confused state

items.translit: Matrum Thotarppaatu Evankol Pirapparukkal / Utraarkku Utampum Mikai
items.en: To those who sev'rance seek from being's varied strife, Flesh is burthen sore; what then other bonds of life
items.en_prose: What means the addition of other things those who are attempting to cut off (future) births, when even their body is too much (for them)

items.translit: Yaan Enadhu Ennum Serukku / Aruppaan Vaanorkku Uyarndha Ulakam
items.en: Who kills conceit that utters 'I' and 'mine', Shall enter realms above the powers divine
items.en_prose: Shall enter realms above the powers divine

items.translit: Patri Vitaaa Itumpaikal Patrinaip / Patri Vitaaa Thavarkku
items.en: Who cling to things that cling and eager clasp, Griefs cling to them with unrelaxing grasp
items.en_prose: Sorrows will never let go their hold of those who give not up their hold of desire

items.translit: Thalaippattaar Theerath Thurandhaar Mayangi / Valaippattaar Matrai Yavar
items.en: Who thoroughly 'renounce' on highest height are set; The rest bewildered, lie entangled in the net
items.en_prose: Those who have entirely renounced (all things and all desire) have obtained (absorption into God); all others wander in confusion, entangled in the net of (many) births

items.translit: Patratra Kanne Pirapparukkum Matru / Nilaiyaamai Kaanap Patum
items.en: When that which clings falls off, severed is being's tie; All else will then be seen as instability
items.en_prose: At the moment in which desire has been abandoned, (other) births will be cut off; when that has not been done, instability will be seen

items.translit: Patruka Patratraan Patrinai Appatraip / Patruka Patru Vitarku
items.en: Cling thou to that which He, to Whom nought clings, hath bid thee cling, Cling to that bond, to get thee free from every clinging thing
items.en_prose: Desire the desire of Him who is without desire; in order to renounce desire, desire that desire

items.translit: Porulalla Vatraip Porulendru Unarum / Marulaanaam Maanaap Pirappu
items.en: Of things devoid of truth as real things men deem;-Cause of degraded birth the fond delusive dream
items.en_prose: Inglorious births are produced by the confusion (of mind) which considers those things to be real which are not real

items.translit: Irulneengi Inpam Payakkum Marulneengi / Maasaru Kaatchi Yavarkku
items.en: Darkness departs, and rapture springs to men who see, The mystic vision pure, from all delusion free
items.en_prose: A clear, undimmed vision of things will deliver its possessors from the darkness of future births, and confer the felicity (of heaven)

items.translit: Aiyaththin Neengith Thelindhaarkku Vaiyaththin / Vaanam Naniya Thutaiththu
items.en: When doubts disperse, and mists of error roll / Away, nearer is heav'n than earth to sage's soul
items.en_prose: Heaven is nearer than earth to those men of purified minds who are freed from from doubt

items.translit: Aiyunarvu Eydhiyak Kannum Payamindre / Meyyunarvu Illaa Thavarkku
items.en: Five-fold perception gained, what benefits accrue / To them whose spirits lack perception of the true
items.en_prose: Even those who have all the knowledge which can be attained by the five senses, will derive no benefit from it, if they are without a knowledge of the true nature of things

items.translit: Epporul Eththanmaith Thaayinum Apporul / Meypporul Kaanpadhu Arivu
items.en: Whatever thing, of whatsoever kind it be,'Tis wisdom's part in each the very thing to see
items.en_prose: (True) knowledge is the perception concerning every thing of whatever kind, that that thing is the true thing

items.translit: Katreentu Meypporul Kantaar Thalaippatuvar / Matreentu Vaaraa Neri
items.en: Who learn, and here the knowledge of the true obtain, Shall find the path that hither cometh not again
items.en_prose: They, who in this birth have learned to know the True Being, enter the road which returns not into this world

items.translit: Orththullam Ulladhu Unarin Orudhalaiyaap / Perththulla Ventaa Pirappu
items.en: The mind that knows with certitude what is, and ponders well, Its thoughts on birth again to other life need not to dwell
items.en_prose: Let it not be thought that there is another birth for him whose mind having thoroughly considered (all it has been taught) has known the True Being

items.translit: Pirappennum Pedhaimai Neengach Chirappennum / Semporul Kaanpadhu Arivu
items.en: When folly, cause of births, departs; and soul can view / The truth of things, man's dignity- 'tis wisdom true
items.en_prose: True knowledge consists in the removal of ignorance; which is (the cause of) births, and the perception of the True Being who is (the bestower of) heaven

items.translit: Saarpunarndhu Saarpu Ketaozhukin Matrazhiththuch / Chaardharaa Saardharu Noi
items.en: The true 'support' who knows- rejects 'supports' he sought before-Sorrow that clings all destroys, shall cling to him no more
items.en_prose: He who so lives as to know Him who is the support of all things and abandon all desire, will be freed from the evils which would otherwise cleave to him and destroy (his efforts after absorption)

items.translit: Kaamam Vekuli Mayakkam Ivaimundran / Naamam Ketakketum Noi
items.en: When lust and wrath and error's triple tyranny is o'er, Their very names for aye extinct, then pain shall be no more
items.en_prose: If the very names of these three things, desire, anger, and confusion of mind, be destroyed, then will also perish evils (which flow from them)

items.translit: Avaaenpa Ellaa Uyirkkum Enj / Gnaandrum Thavaaap Pirappeenum Viththu
items.en: The wise declare, through all the days, to every living thing / That ceaseless round of birth from seed of strong desire doth spring
items.en_prose: (The wise) say that the seed, which produces unceasing births, at all times, to all creatures, is desire

items.translit: Ventungaal Ventum Piravaamai Matradhu / Ventaamai Venta Varum
items.en: If desire you feel, freedom from changing birth require!'I' will come, if you desire to 'scape, set free from all desire
items.en_prose: If anything be desired, freedom from births should be desired; that (freedom from births) will be attained by desiring to be without desire

items.translit: Ventaamai Anna Vizhuchchelvam Eentillai / Aantum Aqdhoppadhu Il
items.en: No glorious wealth is here like freedom from desire; To bliss like this not even there can soul aspire
items.en_prose: There is in this world no excellence equal to freedom from desire; and even in that world, there is nothing like it

items.translit: Thoouymai Enpadhu Avaavinmai Matradhu / Vaaaimai Venta Varum
items.en: Desire's decease as purity men know; That, too, from yearning search for truth will grow
items.en_prose: Purity (of mind) consists in freedom from desire; and that (freedom from desire) is the fruit of the love of truth

items.translit: Atravar Enpaar Avaaatraar Matraiyaar / Atraaka Atradhu Ilar
items.en: Men freed from bonds of strong desire are free; None other share such perfect liberty
items.en_prose: They are said to be free (from future birth) who are freed from desire; all others (who, whatever else they may be free from, are not freed from desire) are not thus free

items.translit: Anjuva Thorum Arane Oruvanai / Vanjippa Thorum Avaa
items.en: Desire each soul beguiles; True virtue dreads its wiles
items.en_prose: It is the chief duty of (an ascetic) to watch against desire with (jealous) fear; for it has power to deceive (and destroy) him

items.translit: Avaavinai Aatra Aruppin Thavaavinai / Thaanventu Maatraan Varum
items.en: Who thoroughly rids his life of passion-prompted deed, Deeds of unfailing worth shall do, which, as he plans, succeed
items.en_prose: If a man thoroughly cut off all desire, the deeds, which confer immortality, will come to him, in the path in which he seeks them

items.translit: Avaaillaark Killaakun Thunpam Aqdhuntel / Thavaaadhu Menmel Varum
items.en: Affliction is not known where no desires abide; Where these are, endless rises sorrow's tide
items.en_prose: There is no sorrow to those who are without desire; but where that is, (sorrow) will incessantly come, more and more

items.translit: Inpam Itaiyaraa Theentum Avaavennum / Thunpaththul Thunpang Ketin
items.en: When dies away desire, that woe of woes / Ev'n here the soul unceasing rapture knows
items.en_prose: Even while in this body, joy will never depart (from the mind, in which) desire, that sorrow of sorrows, has been destroyed

items.translit: Aaraa Iyarkai Avaaneeppin Annilaiye / Peraa Iyarkai Tharum
items.en: Drive from thy soul desire insatiate; Straight'way is gained the moveless blissful state
items.en_prose: The removal of desire, whose nature it is never to be satisfied, will immediately confer a nature that can never be changed

items.translit: Aakoozhaal Thondrum Asaivinmai Kaipporul / Pokoozhaal Thondrum Mati
items.en: Wealth-giving fate power of unflinching effort brings; From fate that takes away idle remissness springs
items.en_prose: Perseverance comes from a prosperous fate, and idleness from an adverse fate

items.translit: Pedhaip Patukkum Izhavoozh Arivakatrum / Aakaloozh Utrak Katai
items.en: The fate that loss ordains makes wise men's wisdom foolishness; The fate that gain bestows with ampler powers will wisdom bless
items.en_prose: An adverse fate produces folly, and a prosperous fate produces enlarged knowledge

items.translit: Nunniya Noolpala Karpinum Matrundhan / Unmai Yarive Mikum
items.en: In subtle learning manifold though versed man be,'The wisdom, truly his, will gain supremacy
items.en_prose: Although (a man) may study the most polished treatises, the knowledge which fate has decreed to him will still prevail

items.translit: Iruveru Ulakaththu Iyarkai Thiruveru / Thelliya Raadhalum Veru
items.en: Two fold the fashion of the world: some live in fortune's light; While other some have souls in wisdom's radiance bright
items.en_prose: There are (through fate) two different natures in the world, hence the difference (observable in men) in (their acquisition of) wealth, and in their attainment of knowledge

items.translit: Nallavai Ellaaan Theeyavaam Theeyavum / Nallavaam Selvam Seyarku
items.en: All things that good appear will oft have ill success; All evil things prove good for gain of happiness
items.en_prose: In the acquisition of property, every thing favourable becomes unfavourable, and (on the other hand) everything unfavourable becomes favourable, (through the power of fate)

items.translit: Pariyinum Aakaavaam Paalalla Uyththuch / Choriyinum Pokaa Thama
items.en: Things not your own will yield no good, howe'er you guard with pain; Your own, howe'er you scatter them abroad, will yours remain
items.en_prose: Whatever is not conferred by fate cannot be preserved although it be guarded with most painful care; and that, which fate has made his, cannot be lost, although one should even take it and throw it away

items.translit: Vakuththaan Vakuththa Vakaiyallaal Koti / Thokuththaarkku Thuyththal Aridhu
items.en: Save as the 'sharer' shares to each in due degree, To those who millions store enjoyment scarce can be
items.en_prose: Even those who gather together millions will only enjoy them, as it has been determined by the disposer (of all things)

items.translit: Thurappaarman Thuppura Villaar Urarpaala / Oottaa Kazhiyu Menin
items.en: The destitute with ascetics merit share, If fate to visit with predestined ills would spare
items.en_prose: The destitute will renounce desire (and become ascetics), if (fate) do not make them suffer the hindrances to which they are liable, and they pass away

items.translit: Nandraangaal Nallavaak Kaanpavar Andraangaal / Allar Patuva Thevan?
items.en: When good things come, men view them all as gain; When evils come, why then should they complain
items.en_prose: How is it that those, who are pleased with good fortune, trouble themselves when evil comes, (since both are equally the decree of fate) ?

items.translit: Oozhir Peruvali Yaavula Matrondru / Soozhinun Thaanmun Thurum
items.en: What powers so great as those of Destiny? Man's skill / Some other thing contrives; but fate's beforehand still
items.en_prose: What is stronger than fate ? If we think of an expedient (to avert it), it will itself be with us before (the thought)

items.translit: Pataikuti Koozhamaichchu Natparan Aarum / Utaiyaan Arasarul Eru
items.en: An army, people, wealth, a minister, friends, fort: six things-Who owns them all, a lion lives amid the kings
items.en_prose: He who possesses these six things, an army, a people, wealth, ministers, friends and a fortress, is a lion among kings

items.translit: Anjaamai Eekai Arivookkam Innaankum / Enjaamai Vendhark Kiyalpu
items.en: Courage, a liberal hand, wisdom, and energy: these four / Are qualities a king adorn for evermore
items.en_prose: Never to fail in these four things, fearlessness, liberality, wisdom, and energy, is the kingly character

items.translit: Thoongaamai Kalvi Thunivutaimai Immoondrum / Neengaa Nilanaan Pavarkku
items.en: A sleepless promptitude, knowledge, decision strong:These three for aye to rulers of the land belong
items.en_prose: These three things, viz, vigilance, learning, and bravery, should never be wanting in the ruler of a country

items.translit: Aranizhukkaa Thallavai Neekki Maranizhukkaa / Maanam Utaiya Tharasu
items.en: Kingship, in virtue failing not, all vice restrains, In courage failing not, it honour's grace maintains
items.en_prose: He is a king who, with manly modesty, swerves not from virtue, and refrains from vice

items.translit: Iyatralum Eettalung Kaaththalum Kaaththa / Vakuththalum Valla Tharasu
items.en: A king is he who treasure gains, stores up, defends, And duly for his kingdom's weal expends
items.en_prose: He is a king who is able to acquire (wealth), to lay it up, to guard, and to distribute it

items.translit: Kaatchik Keliyan Katunjollan Allanel / Meekkoorum Mannan Nilam
items.en: Where king is easy of access, where no harsh word repels, That land's high praises every subject swells
items.en_prose: The whole world will exalt the country of the king who is easy of access, and who is free from harsh language

items.translit: Insolaal Eeththalikka Vallaarkkuth Thansolaal / Thaankan Tanaiththiv Vulaku
items.en: With pleasant speech, who gives and guards with powerful liberal hand, He sees the world obedient all to his command
items.en_prose: The world will praise and submit itself to the mind of the king who is able to give with affability, and to protect all who come to him

items.translit: Muraiseydhu Kaappaatrum Mannavan Makkatku / Iraiyendru Vaikkap Patum
items.en: Who guards the realm and justice strict maintains, That king as god o'er subject people reigns
items.en_prose: That king, will be esteemed a God among men, who performs his own duties, and protects (his subjects).

items.translit: Sevikaippach Chorporukkum Panputai Vendhan / Kavikaikkeezhth Thangum Ulaku
items.en: The king of worth, who can words bitter to his ear endure, Beneath the shadow of his power the world abides secure
items.en_prose: The whole world will dwell under the umbrella of the king, who can bear words that embitter the ear

items.translit: Kotaiyali Sengol Kutiyompal Naankum / Utaiyaanaam Vendhark Koli
items.en: Gifts, grace, right sceptre, care of people's weal; These four a light of dreaded kings reveal
items.en_prose: He is the light of kings who has there four things, beneficence, benevolence, rectitude, and care for his people

items.translit: Karka Kasatarak Karpavai Katrapin / Nirka Adharkuth Thaka
items.en: So learn that you may full and faultless learning gain, Then in obedience meet to lessons learnt remain
items.en_prose: Let a man learn thoroughly whatever he may learn, and let his conduct be worthy of his learning

items.translit: Ennenpa Enai Ezhuththenpa Ivvirantum / Kannenpa Vaazhum Uyirkku
items.en: The twain that lore of numbers and of letters give / Are eyes, the wise declare, to all on earth that live
items.en_prose: Letters and numbers are the two eyes of man

items.translit: Kannutaiyar Enpavar Katror Mukaththirantu / Punnutaiyar Kallaa Thavar
items.en: Men who learning gain have eyes, men say; Blockheads' faces pairs of sores display
items.en_prose: The learned are said to have eyes, but the unlearned have (merely) two sores in their face

items.translit: Uvappath Thalaikkooti Ullap Piridhal / Anaiththe Pulavar Thozhil
items.en: You meet with joy, with pleasant thought you part; Such is the learned scholar's wonderous art
items.en_prose: It is the part of the learned to give joy to those whom they meet, and on leaving, to make them think (Oh! when shall we meet them again.)

items.translit: Utaiyaarmun Illaarpol Ekkatrung Katraar / Kataiyare Kallaa Thavar
items.en: With soul submiss they stand, as paupers front a rich man's face; Yet learned men are first; th'unlearned stand in lowest place
items.en_prose: The unlearned are inferior to the learned, before whom they stand begging, as the destitute before the wealthy

items.translit: Thottanaith Thoorum Manarkeni Maandharkkuk / Katranaith Thoorum Arivu
items.en: In sandy soil, when deep you delve, you reach the springs below; The more you learn, the freer streams of wisdom flow
items.en_prose: Water will flow from a well in the sand in proportion to the depth to which it is dug, and knowledge will flow from a man in proportion to his learning

items.translit: Yaadhaanum Naataamaal Ooraamaal Ennoruvan / Saandhunaiyung Kallaadha Vaaru
items.en: The learned make each land their own, in every city find a home; Who, till they die; learn nought, along what weary ways they roam
items.en_prose: How is it that any one can remain without learning, even to his death, when (to the learned man) every country is his own (country), and every town his own (town) ?

items.translit: Orumaikkan Thaan Katra Kalvi / Oruvarku Ezhumaiyum Emaap Putaiththu
items.en: The man who store of learning gains, In one, through seven worlds, bliss attains
items.en_prose: The learning, which a man has acquired in one birth, will yield him pleasure during seven births

items.translit: Thaamin Puruvadhu Ulakin Purak / Kantu Kaamuruvar Katrarin Thaar
items.en: Their joy is joy of all the world, they see; thus more / The learners learn to love their cherished lore
items.en_prose: The learned will long (for more learning), when they see that while it gives pleasure to themselves, the world also derives pleasure from it

items.translit: Ketil Vizhuchchelvam Kalvi Yoruvarku / Maatalla Matrai Yavai
items.en: Learning is excellence of wealth that none destroy; To man nought else affords reality of joy
items.en_prose: Learning is the true imperishable riches; all other things are not riches

items.translit: Arangindri Vattaati Yatre Nirampiya / Noolindrik Kotti Kolal
items.en: Like those at draughts would play without the chequered square, Men void of ample lore would counsels of the learned share
items.en_prose: To speak in an assembly (of the learned) without fullness of knowledge, is like playing at chess (on a board) without squares

items.translit: Kallaadhaan Sorkaa Murudhal Mulaiyirantum / Illaadhaal Penkaamur Ratru
items.en: Like those who doat on hoyden's undeveloped charms are they, Of learning void, who eagerly their power of words display
items.en_prose: The desire of the unlearned to speak (in an assembly), is like a woman without breasts desiring (the enjoyment of ) woman-hood

items.translit: Kallaa Thavarum Naninallar Katraarmun / Sollaa Thirukkap Perin
items.en: The blockheads, too, may men of worth appear, If they can keep from speaking where the learned hear
items.en_prose: The unlearned also are very excellent men, if they know how to keep silence before the learned

items.translit: Kallaadhaan Otpam Kazhiyanan Raayinum / Kollaar Arivutai Yaar
items.en: From blockheads' lips, when words of wisdom glibly flow, The wise receive them not, though good they seem to show
items.en_prose: Although the natural knowledge of an unlearned man may be very good, the wise will not accept for true knowledge

items.translit: Kallaa Oruvan Thakaimai Thalaippeydhu / Sollaatach Chorvu Patum
items.en: As worthless shows the worth of man unlearned, When council meets, by words he speaks discerned
items.en_prose: The self-conceit of an unlearned man will fade away, as soon as he speaks in an assembly (of

items.translit: Ularennum Maaththiraiyar Allaal Payavaak / Kalaranaiyar Kallaa Thavar
items.en: 'They are': so much is true of men untaught; But, like a barren field, they yield us nought
items.en_prose: The unlearned are like worthless barren land: all that can be said of them is, that they exist

items.translit: Nunmaan Nuzhaipulam Illaan Ezhilnalam / Manmaan Punaipaavai Yatru
items.en: Who lack the power of subtle, large, and penetrating sense, Like puppet, decked with ornaments of clay, their beauty's vain pretence
items.en_prose: The beauty and goodness of one who is destitute of knowledge by the study of great and exquisite works, is like (the beauty and goodness) of a painted earthen doll

items.translit: Nallaarkan Patta Varumaiyin Innaadhe / Kallaarkan Patta Thiru
items.en: To men unlearned, from fortune's favour greater-evil springs / Than poverty to men of goodly wisdom brings
items.en_prose: Wealth, gained by the unlearned, will give more sorrow than the poverty which may come upon the learned

items.translit: Merpirandhaa Raayinum Kallaadhaar Keezhppirandhum / Katraar Anaiththilar Paatu
items.en: Lower are men unlearned, though noble be their race, Than low-born men adorned with learning's grace
items.en_prose: The unlearned, though born in a high caste, are not equal in dignity to the learned; though they may have been born in a low caste

items.translit: Vilangotu Makkal Anaiyar Ilangunool / Katraarotu Enai Yavar
items.en: Learning's irradiating grace who gain, Others excel, as men the bestial train
items.en_prose: As beasts by the side of men, so are other men by the side of those who are learned in celebrated works

items.translit: Selvaththut Selvanj Chevichchelvam Achchelvam / Selvaththu Lellaan Thalai
items.en: Wealth of wealth is wealth acquired be ear attent; Wealth mid all wealth supremely excellent
items.en_prose: Wealth (gained) by the ear is wealth of wealth; that wealth is the chief of all wealth

items.translit: Sevikkuna Villaadha Pozhdhu Siridhu / Vayitrukkum Eeyap Patum
items.en: When 'tis no longer time the listening ear to feed / With trifling dole of food supply the body's need
items.en_prose: When there is no food for the ear, give a little also to the stomach

items.translit: Seviyunavir Kelvi Yutaiyaar Aviyunavin / Aandraaro Toppar Nilaththu
items.en: Who feed their ear with learned teachings rare, Are like the happy gods oblations rich who share
items.en_prose: Those who in this world enjoy instruction which is the food of the ear, are equal to the Gods, who enjoy the food of the sacrifices

items.translit: Katrila Naayinung Ketka Aqdhoruvarku / Orkaththin Ootraan Thunai
items.en: Though learning none hath he, yet let him hear alway:In weakness this shall prove a staff and stay
items.en_prose: Although a man be without learning, let him listen (to the teaching of the learned); that will be to him a staff in adversity

items.translit: Izhukkal Utaiyuzhi Ootrukkol Atre / Ozhukka Mutaiyaarvaaich Chol
items.en: Like staff in hand of him in slippery ground who strays / Are words from mouth of those who walk in righteous ways
items.en_prose: The words of the good are like a staff in a slippery place

items.translit: Enaiththaanum Nallavai Ketka Anaiththaanum / Aandra Perumai Tharum
items.en: Let each man good things learn, for e'en as he / Shall learn, he gains increase of perfect dignity
items.en_prose: Let a man listen, never so little, to good (instruction), even that will bring him great dignity

items.translit: Pizhaith Thunarndhum Pedhaimai Sollaa / Rizhaiththunarn Theentiya Kelvi Yavar
items.en: Not e'en through inadvertence speak they foolish word, With clear discerning mind who've learning's ample lessons heard
items.en_prose: Not even when they have imperfectly understood (a matter), will those men speak foolishly, who have profoundly studied and diligently listened (to instruction)

items.translit: Ketpinung Kelaath Thakaiyave Kelviyaal / Thotkap Pataadha Sevi
items.en: Where teaching hath not oped the learner's ear, The man may listen, but he scarce can hear
items.en_prose: The ear which has not been bored by instruction, although it hears, is deaf

items.translit: Nunangiya Kelviya Rallaar Vanangiya / Vaayina Raadhal Aridhu
items.en: 'Tis hard for mouth to utter gentle, modest word, When ears discourse of lore refined have never heard
items.en_prose: It is a rare thing to find modesty, a reverend mouth- with those who have not received choice instruction

items.translit: Seviyir Suvaiyunaraa Vaayunarvin Maakkal / Aviyinum Vaazhinum En?
items.en: His mouth can taste, but ear no taste of joy can give!What matter if he die, or prosperous live
items.en_prose: What does it matter whether those men live or die, who can judge of tastes by the mouth, and not by the ear ?

items.translit: Arivatrang Kaakkung Karuvi Seruvaarkkum / Ullazhikka Laakaa Aran
items.en: True wisdom wards off woes, A circling fortress high; Its inner strength man's eager foes Unshaken will defy
items.en_prose: Wisdom is a weapon to ward off destruction; it is an inner fortress which enemies cannot destroy

items.translit: Sendra Itaththaal Selavitaa Theedhoreei / Nandrinpaal Uyppa Tharivu
items.en: Wisdom restrains, nor suffers mind to wander where it would; From every evil calls it back, and guides in way of good
items.en_prose: Not to permit the mind to go where it lists, to keep it from evil, and to employ it in good, this is wisdom

items.translit: Epporul Yaaryaarvaaik Ketpinum Apporul / Meypporul Kaanpa Tharivu
items.en: Though things diverse from divers sages' lips we learn,'Tis wisdom's part in each the true thing to discern
items.en_prose: To discern the truth in every thing, by whomsoever spoken, is wisdom

items.translit: Enporula Vaakach Chelachchollith Thaanpirarvaai / Nunporul Kaanpa Tharivu
items.en: Wisdom hath use of lucid speech, words that acceptance win, And subtle sense of other men's discourse takes in
items.en_prose: To speak so as that the meaning may easily enter the mind of the hearer, and to discern the subtlest thought which may lie hidden in the words of others, this is wisdom

items.translit: Ulakam Thazheeiya Thotpam Malardhalum / Koompalum Illa Tharivu
items.en: Wisdom embraces frank the world, to no caprice exposed; Unlike the lotus flower, now opened wide, now petals strictly closed
items.en_prose: To secure the friendship of the great is true wisdom; it is (also) wisdom to keep (that friendship unchanged, and) not opening and closing (like the lotus flower)

items.translit: Evva Thuraivadhu Ulakam Ulakaththotu / Avva Thuraiva Tharivu
items.en: As dwells the world, so with the world to dwell / In harmony- this is to wisely live and well
items.en_prose: To live as the world lives, is wisdom

items.translit: Arivutaiyaar Aava Tharivaar Arivilaar / Aqdhari Kallaa Thavar
items.en: The wise discern, the foolish fail to see, And minds prepare for things about to be
items.en_prose: The wise are those who know beforehand what will happen; those who do not know this are the unwise

items.translit: Anjuva Thanjaamai Pedhaimai Anjuvadhu / Anjal Arivaar Thozhil
items.en: Folly meets fearful ills with fearless heart; To fear where cause of fear exists is wisdom's part
items.en_prose: Not to fear what ought to be feared, is folly; it is the work of the wise to fear what should be feared

items.translit: Edhiradhaak Kaakkum Arivinaark Killai / Adhira Varuvadhor Noi
items.en: The wise with watchful soul who coming ills foresee; From coming evil's dreaded shock are free
items.en_prose: No terrifying calamity will happen to the wise, who (foresee) and guard against coming evils

items.translit: Arivutaiyaar Ellaa Mutaiyaar Arivilaar / Ennutaiya Renum Ilar
items.en: The wise is rich, with ev'ry blessing blest; The fool is poor, of everything possessed
items.en_prose: Those who possess wisdom, possess every thing; those who have not wisdom, whatever they may possess, have nothing

items.translit: Serukkunj Chinamum Sirumaiyum Illaar / Perukkam Perumidha Neerththu
items.en: Who arrogance, and wrath, and littleness of low desire restrain, To sure increase of lofty dignity attain
items.en_prose: Truly great is the excellence of those (kings) who are free from pride, anger, and lust

items.translit: Ivaralum Maanpirandha Maanamum Maanaa / Uvakaiyum Edham Iraikku
items.en: A niggard hand, o'erweening self-regard, and mirth / Unseemly, bring disgrace to men of kingly brith
items.en_prose: Avarice, undignified pride, and low pleasures are faults in a king

items.translit: Thinaiththunaiyaang Kutram Varinum Panaiththunaiyaak / Kolvar Pazhinaanu Vaar
items.en: Though small as millet-seed the fault men deem; As palm tree vast to those who fear disgrace 'twill seem
items.en_prose: Those who fear guilt, if they commit a fault small as a millet seed, will consider it to be as large as a palmyra tree

items.translit: Kutrame Kaakka Porulaakak Kutrame / Atran Tharooum Pakai
items.en: Freedom from faults is wealth; watch heedfully'Gainst these, for fault is fatal enmity
items.en_prose: Guard against faults as a matter (of great consequence; for) faults are a deadly enemy

items.translit: Varumunnark Kaavaadhaan Vaazhkkai Erimunnar / Vaiththooru Polak Ketum
items.en: His joy who guards not 'gainst the coming evil day, Like straw before the fire shall swift consume away
items.en_prose: The prosperity of him who does not timely guard against faults, will perish like straw before fire

items.translit: Thankutram Neekkip Pirarkutrang Kaankirpin / Enkutra Maakum Iraikku?
items.en: Faultless the king who first his own faults cures, and then / Permits himself to scan faults of other men
items.en_prose: What fault will remain in the king who has put away his own evils, and looks after the evils of others

items.translit: Seyarpaala Seyyaa Thivariyaan Selvam / Uyarpaala Thandrik Ketum
items.en: Who leaves undone what should be done, with niggard mind, His wealth shall perish, leaving not a wrack behind
items.en_prose: The wealth of the avaricious man, who does not expend it for the purposes for which he ought to expend it will waste away and not continue

items.translit: Patrullam Ennum Ivaranmai Etrullum / Ennap Patuvadhon Randru
items.en: The greed of soul that avarice men call, When faults are summed, is worst of all
items.en_prose: Griping avarice is not to be reckoned as one among other faults; (it stands alone - greater than all)

items.translit: Viyavarka Egngnaandrum Thannai Nayavarka / Nandri Payavaa Vinai
items.en: Never indulge in self-complaisant mood, Nor deed desire that yields no gain of good
items.en_prose: Let no (one) praise himself, at any time; let him not desire to do useless things

items.translit: Kaadhala Kaadhal Ariyaamai Uykkirpin / Edhila Edhilaar Nool
items.en: If, to your foes unknown, you cherish what you love, Counsels of men who wish you harm will harmless prove
items.en_prose: If (a king) enjoys, privately the things which he desires, the designs of his enemies will be useless

items.translit: Aranarindhu Mooththa Arivutaiyaar Kenmai / Thiranarindhu Therndhu Kolal
items.en: As friends the men who virtue know, and riper wisdom share, Their worth weighed well, the king should choose with care
items.en_prose: Let (a king) ponder well its value, and secure the friendship of men of virtue and of mature knowledge

items.translit: Utranoi Neekki Uraaamai Murkaakkum / Petriyaarp Penik Kolal
items.en: Cherish the all-accomplished men as friends, Whose skill the present ill removes, from coming ill defends
items.en_prose: Let (a king) procure and kindly care for men who can overcome difficulties when they occur, and guard against them before they happen

items.translit: Ariyavatru Lellaam Aridhe Periyaaraip / Penith Thamaraak Kolal
items.en: To cherish men of mighty soul, and make them all their own, Of kingly treasures rare, as rarest gift is known
items.en_prose: To cherish great men and make them his own, is the most difficult of all difficult things

items.translit: Thammir Periyaar Thamaraa Ozhukudhal / Vanmaiyu Lellaan Thalai
items.en: To live with men of greatness that their own excels, As cherished friends, is greatest power that with a monarch dwells
items.en_prose: So to act as to make those men, his own, who are greater than himself is of all powers the highest

items.translit: Soozhvaarkan Naaka Ozhukalaan Mannavan / Soozhvaaraik Soozhndhu Kolal
items.en: The king, since counsellors are monarch's eyes, Should counsellors select with counsel wise
items.en_prose: As a king must use his ministers as eyes (in managing his kingdom), let him well examine their character and qualifications before he engages them

items.translit: Thakkaa Rinaththanaaith Thaanozhuka Vallaanaich / Chetraar Seyakkitandha Thil
items.en: The king, who knows to live with worthy men allied, Has nought to fear from any foeman's pride
items.en_prose: There will be nothing left for enemies to do, against him who has the power of acting (so as to secure) the fellowship of worthy men

items.translit: Itikkun Thunaiyaarai Yaalvarai Yaare / Ketukkun Thakaimai Yavar
items.en: What power can work his fall, who faithful ministers / Employs, that thunder out reproaches when he errs
items.en_prose: Who are great enough to destroy him who has servants that have power to rebuke him ?

items.translit: Itippaarai Illaadha Emaraa Mannan / Ketuppaa Rilaanung Ketum
items.en: The king with none to censure him, bereft of safeguards all, Though none his ruin work, shall surely ruined fall
items.en_prose: The king, who is without the guard of men who can rebuke him, will perish, even though there be no one to destroy him

items.translit: Mudhalilaarkku Oodhiya Millai Madhalaiyaanjjch / Aarpilaark Killai Nilai
items.en: Who owns no principal, can have no gain of usury; Who lacks support of friends, knows no stability
items.en_prose: There can be no gain to those who have no capital; and in like manner there can be no permanence to

items.translit: Pallaar Pakai Kolalir Paththatuththa / Theemaiththe Nallaar Thotarkai Vital
items.en: Than hate of many foes incurred, works greater woe / Ten-fold, of worthy men the friendship to forego
items.en_prose: It is tenfold more injurious to abandon the friendship of the good, than to incur the hatred of the many

items.translit: Sitrinam Anjum Perumai Sirumaidhaan / Sutramaach Choozhndhu Vitum
items.en: The great of soul will mean association fear; The mean of soul regard mean men as kinsmen dear
items.en_prose: (True) greatness fears the society of the base; it is only the low - minded who will regard them as friends

items.translit: Nilaththiyalpaal Neerdhirin Thatraakum Maandharkku / Inaththiyalpa Thaakum Arivu
items.en: The waters' virtues change with soil through which they flow; As man's companionship so will his wisdom show
items.en_prose: As water changes (its nature), from the nature of the soil (in which it flows), so will the character of men resemble that of their associates

items.translit: Manaththaanaam Maandhark Kunarchchi Inaththaanaam / Innaan Enappatunj Chol
items.en: Perceptions manifold in men are of the mind alone; The value of the man by his companionship is known
items.en_prose: The power of knowing is from the mind; (but) his character is from that of his associates

items.translit: Manaththu Ladhupolak Kaatti Oruvarku / Inaththula Thaakum Arivu
items.en: Man's wisdom seems the offspring of his mind;'Tis outcome of companionship we find
items.en_prose: Wisdom appears to rest in the mind, but it really exists to a man in his companions

items.translit: Manandhooimai Seyvinai Thooimai Irantum / Inandhooimai Thoovaa Varum
items.en: Both purity of mind, and purity of action clear, Leaning no staff of pure companionship, to man draw near
items.en_prose: Chaste company is the staff on which come, these two things, viz, purity of mind and purity of conduct

items.translit: Manandhooyaark Kechchamnan Raakum Inandhooyaarkku / Illainan Raakaa Vinai
items.en: From true pure-minded men a virtuous race proceeds; To men of pure companionship belong no evil deeds
items.en_prose: To the pure-minded there will be a good posterity By those whose associates are pure, no deeds will be done that are not good

items.translit: Mananalam Mannuyirk Kaakkam Inanalam / Ellaap Pukazhum Tharum
items.en: Goodness of mind to lives of men increaseth gain; And good companionship doth all of praise obtain
items.en_prose: Goodness of mind will give wealth, and good society will bring with it all praise, to men

items.translit: Mananalam Nankutaiya Raayinum Saandrorkku / Inanalam Emaap Putaiththu
items.en: To perfect men, though minds right good belong, Yet good companionship is confirmation strong
items.en_prose: Yet good companionship is confirmation strong

items.translit: Mananalaththin Aakum Marumaimar Raqdhum / Inanalaththin Emaap Putaiththu
items.en: Although to mental goodness joys of other life belong, Yet good companionship is confirmation strong
items.en_prose: Future bliss is (the result) of goodness of mind; and even this acquires strength from the society of the good

items.translit: Nallinaththi Noongun Thunaiyillai Theeyinaththin / Allar Patuppadhooum Il
items.en: Than good companionship no surer help we know; Than bad companionship nought causes direr woe
items.en_prose: There is no greater help than the company of the good; there is no greater source of sorrow than the company of the wicked

items.translit: Azhivadhooum Aavadhooum Aaki Vazhipayakkum / Oodhiyamum Soozhndhu Seyal
items.en: Expenditure, return, and profit of the deed / In time to come; weigh these- than to the act proceed
items.en_prose: Let a man reflect on what will be lost, what will be acquired and (from these) what will be his ultimate gain, and (then, let him) act

items.translit: Therindha Inaththotu Therndhennich Cheyvaarkku / Arumporul Yaadhondrum Il
items.en: With chosen friends deliberate; next use the private thought; Then act By those who thus proceed all works with ease are wrought
items.en_prose: There is nothing too difficult to (be attained by) those who, before they act, reflect well themselves, and thoroughly consider (the matter) with chosen friends

items.translit: Aakkam Karudhi Mudhalizhakkum Seyvinai / Ookkaar Arivutai Yaar
items.en: To risk one's all and lose, aiming at added gain, Is rash affair, from which the wise abstain
items.en_prose: Wise men will not, in the hopes of profit, undertake works that will consume their principal

items.translit: Thelivi Ladhanaith Thotangaar Ilivennum / Edhappaatu Anju Pavar
items.en: A work of which the issue is not clear, Begin not they reproachful scorn who fear
items.en_prose: Those who fear reproach will not commence anything which has not been (thoroughly considered) and made clear to them

items.translit: Vakaiyarach Choozhaa Thezhudhal Pakaivaraip / Paaththip Patuppadho Raaru
items.en: With plans not well matured to rise against your foe, Is way to plant him out where he is sure to grow
items.en_prose: One way to promote the prosperity of an enemy, is (for a king) to set out (to war) without having thoroughly weighed his ability (to cope with its chances)

items.translit: Seydhakka Alla Seyak Ketum / Seydhakka Seyyaamai Yaanung Ketum
items.en: 'Tis ruin if man do an unbefitting thing; Fit things to leave undone will equal ruin bring
items.en_prose: He will perish who does not what is not fit to do; and he also will perish who does not do what it is fit to

items.translit: Ennith Thunika Karumam Thunindhapin / Ennuvam Enpadhu Izhukku
items.en: Think, and then dare the deed! Who cry,'Deed dared, we'll think,' disgraced shall be
items.en_prose: Consider, and then undertake a matter; after having undertaken it, to say "We will consider," is folly

items.translit: Aatrin Varundhaa Varuththam Palarnindru / Potrinum Poththup Patum
items.en: On no right system if man toil and strive, Though many men assist, no work can thrive
items.en_prose: The work, which is not done by suitable methods, will fail though many stand to uphold it

items.translit: Nandraatra Lullun Thavuruntu Avaravar / Panparin Thaatraak Katai
items.en: Though well the work be done, yet one mistake is made, To habitudes of various men when no regard is paid
items.en_prose: There are failures even in acting well, when it is done without knowing the various dispositions of men

items.translit: Ellaadha Ennich Cheyalventum Thammotu / Kollaadha Kollaadhu Ulaku
items.en: Plan and perform no work that others may despise; What misbeseems a king the world will not approve as wise
items.en_prose: Let a man reflect, and do things which bring no reproach; the world will not approve, with him, of things which do not become of his position to adopt

items.translit: Vinaivaliyum Thanvaliyum Maatraan Valiyum / Thunaivaliyum Thookkich Cheyal
items.en: The force the strife demands, the force he owns, the force of foes, The force of friends; these should he weigh ere to the war he goes
items.en_prose: Let (one) weigh well the strength of the deed (he purposes to do), his own strength, the strength of his enemy, and the strength of the allies (of both), and then let him act

items.translit: Olva Tharivadhu Arindhadhan Kandhangich / Chelvaarkkuch Chellaadhadhu Il
items.en: Who know what can be wrought, with knowledge of the means, on this, Their mind firm set, go forth, nought goes with them amiss
items.en_prose: There is nothing which may not be accomplished by those who, before they attack (an enemy), make themselves acquainted with their own ability, and with whatever else is (needful) to be known, and

items.translit: Utaiththam Valiyariyaar Ookkaththin Ookki / Itaikkan Murindhaar Palar
items.en: Ill-deeming of their proper powers, have many monarchs striven, And midmost of unequal conflict fallen asunder riven
items.en_prose: There are many who, ignorant of their (want of) power (to meet it), have haughtily set out to war, and broken down in the midst of it

items.translit: Amaindhaang Kozhukaan Alavariyaan Thannai / Viyandhaan Viraindhu Ketum
items.en: Who not agrees with those around, no moderation knows, In self-applause indulging, swift to ruin goes
items.en_prose: He will quickly perish who, ignorant of his own resources flatters himself of his greatness, and does

items.translit: Peelipey Saakaatum Achchirum Appantanjjch / Aala Mikuththup Peyin
items.en: With peacock feathers light, you load the wain; Yet, heaped too high, the axle snaps in twain
items.en_prose: The axle tree of a bandy, loaded only with peacocks' feathers will break, if it be greatly overloaded

items.translit: Nunikkompar Erinaar Aqdhiran Thookkin / Uyirkkirudhi Aaki Vitum
items.en: Who daring climbs, and would himself upraise / Beyond the branch's tip, with life the forfeit pays
items.en_prose: There will be an end to the life of him who, having climbed out to the end of a branch, ventures to go further

items.translit: Aatrin Aravarindhu Eeka Adhuporul / Potri Vazhangu Neri
items.en: With knowledge of the measure due, as virtue bids you give!That is the way to guard your wealth, and seemly live
items.en_prose: Let a man know the measure of his ability (to give), and let him give accordingly; such giving is the way to preserve his property

items.translit: Aakaaru Alavitti Thaayinung Ketillai / Pokaaru Akalaak Katai
items.en: Incomings may be scant; but yet, no failure there, If in expenditure you rightly learn to spare
items.en_prose: Even though the income (of a king) be small, it will not cause his (ruin), if his outgoings be not larger than his income

items.translit: Alavara�ndhu Vaazhaadhaan Vaazhkkai Ulapola / Illaakith Thondraak Ketum
items.en: Who prosperous lives and of enjoyment knows no bound, His seeming wealth, departing, nowhere shall be found
items.en_prose: The prosperity of him who lives without knowing the measure (of his property), will perish, even while it seems to continue

items.translit: Ulavarai Thookkaadha Oppura Vaanmai / Valavarai Vallaik Ketum
items.en: Beneficence that measures not its bound of means, Will swiftly bring to nought the wealth on which it leans
items.en_prose: The measure of his wealth will quickly perish, whose liberality weighs not the measure of his property

items.translit: Pakalvellum Kookaiyaik Kaakkai Ikalvellum / Vendharkku Ventum Pozhudhu
items.en: A crow will conquer owl in broad daylight; The king that foes would crush, needs fitting time to fight
items.en_prose: A crow will overcome an owl in the day time; so the king who would conquer his enemy must have (a suitable) time

items.translit: Paruvaththotu Otta Ozhukal Thiruvinaith / Theeraamai Aarkkung Kayiru
items.en: The bond binds fortune fast is ordered effort made, Strictly observant still of favouring season's aid
items.en_prose: Acting at the right season, is a cord that will immoveably bind success (to a king)

items.translit: Aruvinai Yenpa Ulavo Karuviyaan / Kaalam Arindhu Seyin
items.en: Can any work be hard in very fact, If men use fitting means in timely act
items.en_prose: Is there anything difficult for him to do, who acts, with (the right) instruments at the right time ?

items.translit: Gnaalam Karudhinung Kaikootung Kaalam / Karudhi Itaththaar Seyin
items.en: The pendant world's dominion may be won, In fitting time and place by action done
