items.en_prose: Though (a man) should meditate (the conquest of) the world, he may accomplish it if he acts in the right time, and at the right place

items.translit: Kaalam Karudhi Iruppar Kalangaadhu / Gnaalam Karudhu Pavar
items.en: Who think the pendant world itself to subjugate, With mind unruffled for the fitting time must wait
items.en_prose: They who thoughtfully consider and wait for the (right) time (for action), may successfully meditate (the conquest of) the world

items.translit: Ookka Mutaiyaan Otukkam Porudhakar / Thaakkarkup Perun Thakaiththu
items.en: The men of mighty power their hidden energies repress, As fighting ram recoils to rush on foe with heavier stress
items.en_prose: The self-restraint of the energetic (while waiting for a suitable opportunity), is like the drawing back of a fighting-ram in order to butt

items.translit: Pollena Aange Puramveraar Kaalampaarththu / Ulverppar Olli Yavar
items.en: The glorious once of wrath enkindled make no outward show, At once; they bide their time, while hidden fires within them glow
items.en_prose: The wise will not immediately and hastily shew out their anger; they will watch their time, and restrain it within

items.translit: Serunaraik Kaanin Sumakka Iruvarai / Kaanin Kizhakkaam Thalai
items.en: If foes' detested form they see, with patience let them bear; When fateful hour at last they spy,- the head lies there
items.en_prose: If one meets his enemy, let him show him all respect, until the time for his destruction is come; when that is come, his head will be easily brought low

items.translit: Eydhar Kariyadhu Iyaindhakkaal Annilaiye / Seydhar Kariya Seyal
items.en: When hardest gain of opportunity at last is won, With promptitude let hardest deed be done
items.en_prose: If a rare opportunity occurs, while it lasts, let a man do that which is rarely to be accomplished (but for such an opportunity)

items.translit: Kokkokka Koompum Paruvaththu Matradhan / Kuththokka Seerththa Itaththu
items.en: As heron stands with folded wing, so wait in waiting hour; As heron snaps its prey, when fortune smiles, put forth your power
items.en_prose: At the time when one should use self-control, let him restrain himself like a heron; and, let him like it, strike, when there is a favourable opportunity

items.translit: Thotangarka Evvinaiyum Ellarka Mutrum / Itanganta Pinal Ladhu
items.en: Begin no work of war, depise no foe, Till place where you can wholly circumvent you know
items.en_prose: Let not (a king) despise (an enemy), nor undertake any thing (against him), until he has obtained (a suitable) place for besieging him

items.translit: Muranserndha Moimpi Navarkkum Aranserndhaam / Aakkam Palavun Tharum
items.en: Though skill in war combine with courage tried on battle-field, The added gain of fort doth great advantage yield
items.en_prose: Even to those who are men of power and expedients, an attack in connection with a fortification will yield many advantages

items.translit: Aatraarum Aatri Atupa Itanarindhu / Potraarkan Potrich Cheyin
items.en: E'en weak ones mightily prevail, if place of strong defence, They find, protect themselves, and work their foes offence
items.en_prose: Even the powerless will become powerful and conquer, if they select a proper field (of action), and guard themselves, while they make war on their enemies

items.translit: Enniyaar Ennam Izhappar Itanarindhu / Thunniyaar Thunnich Cheyin
items.en: The foes who thought to triumph, find their thoughts were vain, If hosts advance, seize vantage ground, and thence the fight maintain
items.en_prose: If they who draw near (to fight) choose a suitable place to approach (their enemy), the latter, will have to relinquish the thought which they once entertained, of conquering them

items.translit: Netumpunalul Vellum Mudhalai Atumpunalin / Neengin Adhanaip Pira
items.en: The crocodile prevails in its own flow of water wide, If this it leaves, 'tis slain by anything beside
items.en_prose: In deep water, a crocodile will conquer (all other animals); but if it leave the water, other animals will conquer it

items.translit: Katalotaa Kaalval Netundher Katalotum / Naavaayum Otaa Nilaththu
items.en: The lofty car, with mighty wheel, sails not o'er watery main, The boat that skims the sea, runs not on earth's hard plain
items.en_prose: Wide chariots, with mighty wheels, will not run on the ocean; neither will ships that the traverse ocean, move on the earth

items.translit: Anjaamai Allaal Thunaiventaa Enjaamai / Enni Itaththaal Seyin
items.en: Save their own fearless might they need no other aid, If in right place they fight, all due provision made
items.en_prose: You will need no other aid than fearlessness, if you thoroughly reflect (on what you are to do), and select (a suitable) place for your operations

items.translit: Sirupataiyaan Sellitam Serin Urupataiyaan / Ookkam Azhindhu Vitum
items.en: If lord of army vast the safe retreat assail / Of him whose host is small, his mightiest efforts fail
items.en_prose: The power of one who has a large army will perish, if he goes into ground where only a small army can act

items.translit: Sirainalanum Seerum Ilareninum Maandhar / Urainilaththotu Ottal Aridhu
items.en: Though fort be none, and store of wealth they lack,'Tis hard a people's homesteads to attack
items.en_prose: It is a hazardous thing to attack men in their own country, although they may neither have power nor a good fortress

items.translit: Kaalaazh Kalaril Nariyatum Kannanjaa / Velaal Mukaththa Kaliru
items.en: The jackal slays, in miry paths of foot-betraying fen, The elephant of fearless eye and tusks transfixing armed men
items.en_prose: A fox can kill a fearless, warrior-faced elephant, if it go into mud in which its legs sink down

items.translit: Aramporul Inpam Uyirachcham Naankin / Thirandherindhu Therap Patum
items.en: How treats he virtue, wealth and pleasure? How, when life's at stake, Comports himself? This four-fold test of man will full assurance make
items.en_prose: Let (a minister) be chosen, after he has been tried by means of these four things, viz,-his virtue, (love of) money, (love of) sexual pleasure, and tear of (losing) life

items.translit: Kutippirandhu Kutraththin Neengi Vatuppariyum / Naanutaiyaan Sutte Thelivu
items.en: Of noble race, of faultless worth, of generous pride / That shrinks from shame or stain; in him may king confide
items.en_prose: (The king's) choice should (fall) on him, who is of good family, who is free from faults, and who has the modesty which fears the wounds (of sin)

items.translit: Ariyakatru Aasatraar Kannum Theriyungaal / Inmai Aridhe Veliru
items.en: Though deeply learned, unflecked by fault, 'tis rare to see, When closely scanned, a man from all unwisdom free
items.en_prose: When even men, who have studied the most difficult works, and who are free from faults, are (carefully) examined, it is a rare thing to find them without ignorance

items.translit: Kunamnaatik Kutramum Naati Avatrul / Mikainaati Mikka Kolal
items.en: Weigh well the good of each, his failings closely scan, As these or those prevail, so estimate the man
items.en_prose: Let (a king) consider (a man's) good qualities, as well as his faults, and then judge (of his character) by that which prevails

items.translit: Perumaikkum Enaich Chirumaikkum Thaththam / Karumame Kattalaik Kal
items.en: Of greatness and of meanness too, The deeds of each are touchstone true
items.en_prose: A man's deeds are the touchstone of his greatness and littleness

items.translit: Atraaraith Therudhal Ompuka Matravar / Patrilar Naanaar Pazhi
items.en: Beware of trusting men who have no kith of kin; No bonds restrain such men, no shame deters from sin
items.en_prose: Let (a king) avoid choosing men who have no relations; such men have no attachment, and thereforehave no fear of crime

items.translit: Kaadhanmai Kandhaa Arivariyaarth Therudhal / Pedhaimai Ellaan Tharum
items.en: By fond affection led who trusts in men of unwise soul, Yields all his being up to folly's blind control
items.en_prose: Yields all his being up to folly's blind control

items.translit: Theraan Piranaith Thelindhaan Vazhimurai / Theeraa Itumpai Tharum
items.en: Who trusts an untried stranger, brings disgrace, Remediless, on all his race
items.en_prose: Sorrow that will not leave even his posterity will come upon him chooses a stranger whose character he has not known

items.translit: Therarka Yaaraiyum Theraadhu Therndhapin / Theruka Therum Porul
items.en: Trust no man whom you have not fully tried, When tested, in his prudence proved confide
items.en_prose: Let (a king) choose no one without previous consideration; after he has made his choice, let him unhesitatingly select for each such duties as are appropriate

items.translit: Theraan Thelivum Thelindhaankan Aiyuravum / Theeraa Itumpai Tharum
items.en: Trust where you have not tried, doubt of a friend to feel, Once trusted, wounds inflict that nought can heal
items.en_prose: To make choice of one who has not been examined, and to entertain doubts respecting one who has been chosen, will produce irremediable sorrow

items.translit: Nanmaiyum Theemaiyum Naati Nalampurindha / Thanmaiyaan Aalap Patum
items.en: Who good and evil scanning, ever makes the good his joy; Such man of virtuous mood should king employ
items.en_prose: He should be employed (by a king), whose nature leads him to choose the good, after having weighed both the evil and the good in any undertaking

items.translit: Vaari Perukki Valampatuththu Utravai / Aaraaivaan Seyka Vinai
items.en: Who swells the revenues, spreads plenty o'er the land, Seeks out what hinders progress, his the workman's hand
items.en_prose: Let him do (the king's) work who can enlarge the sources (of revenue), increase wealth and considerately prevent the accidents (which would destroy it)

items.translit: Anparivu Thetram Avaavinmai Innaankum / Nankutaiyaan Katte Thelivu
items.en: A loyal love with wisdom, clearness, mind from avarice free; Who hath these four good gifts should ever trusted be
items.en_prose: Let the choice (of a king) fall upon him who largely possesses these four things, love, knowledge, a clear mind and freedom from covetousness

items.translit: Enaivakaiyaan Theriyak Kannum Vinaivakaiyaan / Veraakum Maandhar Palar
items.en: Even when tests of every kind are multiplied, Full many a man proves otherwise, by action tried
items.en_prose: Even when (a king) has tried them in every possible way, there are many men who change, from the nature of the works (in which they may be employed)

items.translit: Arindhaatrich Cheykirpaarku Allaal Vinaidhaan / Sirandhaanendru Evarpaar Randru
items.en: No specious fav'rite should the king's commission bear, But he that knows, and work performs with patient care
items.en_prose: (A king's) work can only be accomplished by a man of wisdom and patient endurance; it is not of a nature to be given to one from mere personal attachment

items.translit: Seyvaanai Naati Vinainaatik Kaalaththotu / Eydha Unarndhu Seyal
items.en: Let king first ask, 'Who shall the deed perform?' and 'What the deed?'Of hour befitting both assured, let every work proceed
items.en_prose: Let (a king) act, after having considered the agent (whom he is to employ), the deed (he desires to do), and the time which is suitable to it

items.translit: Ithanai Ithanaal Ivanmutikkum Endraaindhu / Adhanai Avankan Vital
items.en: 'This man, this work shall thus work out,' let thoughtful king command; Then leave the matter wholly in his servant's hand
items.en_prose: After having considered, "this man can accomplish this, by these means", let (the king) leave with him the discharge of that duty

items.translit: Vinaik Kurimai Naatiya Pindrai / Avanai Adharkuriya Naakach Cheyal
items.en: As each man's special aptitude is known, Bid each man make that special work his own
items.en_prose: Having considered what work a man is fit for, let (the king) employ him in that work

items.translit: Vinaikkan Vinaiyutaiyaan Kenmaive Raaka / Ninaippaanai Neengum Thiru
items.en: Fortune deserts the king who ill can bear, Informal friendly ways of men his tolls who share
items.en_prose: Prosperity will leave (the king) who doubts the friendship of the man who steadily labours in the discharge of his duties

items.translit: Naatorum Naatuka Mannan Vinaiseyvaan / Kotaamai Kotaa Thulaku
items.en: Let king search out his servants' deeds each day; When these do right, the world goes rightly on its way
items.en_prose: Let a king daily examine the conduct of his servants; if they do not act crookedly, the world will not act crookedly

items.translit: Patratra Kannum Pazhaimaipaa Raattudhal / Sutraththaar Kanne Ula
items.en: When wealth is fled, old kindness still to show, Is kindly grace that only kinsmen know
items.en_prose: Even when (a man's) property is all gone, relatives will act towards him with their accustomed (kindness)

items.translit: Virupparaach Chutram Iyaiyin Arupparaa / Aakkam Palavum Tharum
items.en: The gift of kin's unfailing love bestows / Much gain of good, like flower that fadeless blows
items.en_prose: If (a man's) relatives remain attached to him with unchanging love, it will be a source of everincreasing wealth

items.translit: Alavalaa Villaadhaan Vaazhkkai Kulavalaak / Kotindri Neernirain Thatru
items.en: His joy of life who mingles not with kinsmen gathered round, Is lake where streams pour in, with no encircling bound
items.en_prose: The wealth of one who does not mingle freely with his relatives, will be like the filling of water in a

items.translit: Sutraththaal Sutrap Pataozhukal Selvandhaan / Petraththaal Petra Payan
items.en: The profit gained by wealth's increase, Is living compassed round by relatives in peace
items.en_prose: To live surrounded by relatives, is the advantage to be derived from the acquisition of wealth

items.translit: Kotuththalum Insolum Aatrin Atukkiya / Sutraththaal Sutrap Patum
items.en: Who knows the use of pleasant words, and liberal gifts can give, Connections, heaps of them, surrounding him shall live
items.en_prose: He will be surrounded by numerous relatives who manifests generosity and affability

items.translit: Perungotaiyaan Penaan Vekuli Avanin / Marungutaiyaar Maanilaththu Il
items.en: Than one who gifts bestows and wrath restrains, Through the wide world none larger following gains
items.en_prose: No one, in all the world, will have so many relatives (about him), as he who makes large gift, and does not give way to anger

items.translit: Kaakkai Karavaa Karaindhunnum Aakkamum / Annanee Raarkke Ula
items.en: The crows conceal not, call their friends to come, then eat; Increase of good such worthy ones shall meet
items.en_prose: The crows do not conceal (their prey), but will call out for others (to share with them) while they eat it; wealth will be with those who show a similar disposition (towards their relatives)

items.translit: Podhunokkaan Vendhan Varisaiyaa Nokkin / Adhunokki Vaazhvaar Palar
items.en: Where king regards not all alike, but each in his degree,'Neath such discerning rule many dwell happily
items.en_prose: Many relatives will live near a king, when they observe that he does not look on all alike, but that he looks on each man according to his merit

items.translit: Thamaraakik Thatrurandhaar Sutram Amaraamaik / Kaaranam Indri Varum
items.en: Who once were his, and then forsook him, as before / Will come around, when cause of disagreement is no more
items.en_prose: Those who have been friends and have afterwards forsaken him, will return and join themselves (to him), when the cause of disagreement is not to be found in him

items.translit: Uzhaippirindhu Kaaranaththin Vandhaanai Vendhan / Izhaith Thirundhu Ennik Kolal
items.en: Who causeless went away, then to return, for any cause, ask leave; The king should sift their motives well, consider, and receive
items.en_prose: When one may have left him, and for some cause has returned to him, let the king fulfil the object (for which he has come back) and thoughtfully receive him again

items.translit: Irandha Vekuliyin Theedhe Sirandha / Uvakai Makizhchchiyir Sorvu
items.en: 'Tis greater ill, it rapture of o'erweening gladness to the soul / Bring self-forgetfulness than if transcendent wrath control
items.en_prose: More evil than excessive anger, is forgetfulness which springs from the intoxication of great joy

items.translit: Pochchaappuk Kollum Pukazhai Arivinai / Nichcha Nirappuk Kon Raangu
items.en: Perpetual, poverty is death to wisdom of the wise; When man forgets himself his glory dies
items.en_prose: Forgetfulness will destroy fame, even as constant poverty destroys knowledge

items.translit: Pochchaappaark Killai Pukazhmai Adhuulakaththu / Eppaalnoo Lorkkum Thunivu
items.en: 'To self-oblivious men no praise'; this rule / Decisive wisdom sums of every school
items.en_prose: Thoughtlessness will never acquire fame; and this tenet is upheld by all treatises in the world

items.translit: Achcha Mutaiyaarkku Aranillai Aangillai / Pochchaap Putaiyaarkku Nanku
items.en: 'To cowards is no fort's defence'; e'en so / The self-oblivious men no blessing know
items.en_prose: Just as the coward has no defence (by whatever fortifications ha may be surrounded), so the thoughtless has no good (whatever advantages he may possess)

items.translit: Munnurak Kaavaadhu Izhukkiyaan Thanpizhai / Pinnooru Irangi Vitum
items.en: To him who nought foresees, recks not of anything, The after woe shall sure repentance bring
items.en_prose: The thoughtless man, who provides not against the calamities that may happen, will afterwards repent for his fault

items.translit: Izhukkaamai Yaarmaattum Endrum Vazhukkaamai / Vaayin Adhuvoppadhu Il
items.en: Towards all unswerving, ever watchfulness of soul retain, Where this is found there is no greater gain
items.en_prose: There is nothing comparable with the possession of unfailing thoughtfulness at all times; and towards all persons

items.translit: Ariyaendru Aakaadha Illaipoch Chaavaak / Karuviyaal Potrich Cheyin
items.en: Though things are arduous deemed, there's nought may not be won, When work with mind's unslumbering energy and thought is done
items.en_prose: There is nothing too difficult to be accomplished, if a man set about it carefully, with unflinching endeavour

items.translit: Pukazhndhavai Potrich Cheyalventum Seyyaadhu / Ikazhndhaarkku Ezhumaiyum Il
items.en: Let things that merit praise thy watchful soul employ; Who these despise attain through sevenfold births no joy
items.en_prose: Let (a man) observe and do these things which have been praised (by the wise); if he neglects and fails to perform them, for him there will be no (happiness) throughout the seven births

items.translit: Ikazhchchiyin Kettaarai Ulluka Thaandham / Makizhchchiyin Maindhurum Pozhdhu
items.en: Think on the men whom scornful mind hath brought to nought, When exultation overwhelms thy wildered thought
items.en_prose: Let (a king) think of those who have been ruined by neglect, when his mind is elated with joy

items.translit: Ulliyadhu Eydhal Elidhuman Matrundhaan / Ulliyadhu Ullap Perin
items.en: 'Tis easy what thou hast in mind to gain, If what thou hast in mind thy mind retain
items.en_prose: It is easy for (one) to obtain whatever he may think of, if he can again think of it

items.translit: Orndhukan Notaadhu Iraipurindhu Yaarmaattum / Therndhusey Vaqdhe Murai
items.en: Search out, to no one favour show; with heart that justice loves / Consult, then act; this is the rule that right approves
items.en_prose: To examine into (the crimes which may be committed), to show no favour (to any one), to desire to act with impartiality towards all, and to inflict (such punishments) as may be wisely resolved on,

items.translit: Vaanokki Vaazhum Ulakellaam Mannavan / Kol Nokki Vaazhung Kuti
items.en: All earth looks up to heav'n whence raindrops fall; All subjects look to king that ruleth all
items.en_prose: When there is rain, the living creation thrives; and so when the king rules justly, his subjects thrive

items.translit: Andhanar Noorkum Araththirkum Aadhiyaai / Nindradhu Mannavan Kol
items.en: Learning and virtue of the sages spring, From all-controlling sceptre of the king
items.en_prose: The sceptre of the king is the firm support of the Vedas of the Brahmin, and of all virtues therein described

items.translit: Kutidhazheeik Kolochchum Maanila Mannan / Atidhazheei Nirkum Ulaku
items.en: Whose heart embraces subjects all, lord over mighty land / Who rules, the world his feet embracing stands
items.en_prose: The world will constantly embrace the feet of the great king who rules over his subjects with love

items.translit: Iyalpulik Kolochchum Mannavan Naatta / Peyalum Vilaiyulum Thokku
items.en: Where king, who righteous laws regards, the sceptre wields, There fall the showers, there rich abundance crowns the fields
items.en_prose: Rain and plentiful crops will ever dwell together in the country of the king who sways his sceptre with justice

items.translit: Velandru Vendri Tharuvadhu Mannavan / Koladhooung Kotaa Thenin
items.en: Not lance gives kings the victory, But sceptre swayed with equity
items.en_prose: It is not the javelin that gives victory, but the king's sceptre, if it do no injustice

items.translit: Iraikaakkum Vaiyakam Ellaam Avanai / Muraikaakkum Muttaach Cheyin
items.en: The king all the whole realm of earth protects; And justice guards the king who right respects
items.en_prose: The king defends the whole world; and justice, when administered without defect, defends the king

items.translit: Enpadhaththaan Oraa Muraiseyyaa Mannavan / Thanpadhaththaan Thaane Ketum
items.en: Hard of access, nought searching out, with partial hand / The king who rules, shall sink and perish from the land
items.en_prose: The king who gives not facile audience (to those who approach him), and who does not examine and pass judgment (on their complaints), will perish in disgrace

items.translit: Kutipurang Kaaththompik Kutram Katidhal / Vatuvandru Vendhan Thozhil
items.en: Abroad to guard, at home to punish, brings / No just reproach; 'tis work assigned to kings
items.en_prose: In guarding his subjects (against injury from others), and in preserving them himself; to punish crime

items.translit: Kolaiyir Kotiyaarai Vendhoruththal Paingoozh / Kalaikat Tadhanotu Ner
items.en: By punishment of death the cruel to restrain, Is as when farmer frees from weeds the tender grain
items.en_prose: For a king to punish criminals with death, is like pulling up the weeds in the green corn

items.translit: Kolaimerkon Taarir Kotidhe Alaimerkontu / Allavai Seydhozhukum Vendhu
items.en: Than one who plies the murderer's trade, more cruel is the king / Who all injustice works, his subjects harassing
items.en_prose: The king who gives himself up to oppression and acts unjustly (towards his subjects) is more cruel than the man who leads the life of a murderer

items.translit: Velotu Nindraan Ituven Radhupolum / Kolotu Nindraan Iravu
items.en: As 'Give' the robber cries with lance uplift, So kings with sceptred hand implore a gift
items.en_prose: The request (for money) of him who holds the sceptre is like the word of a highway robber who stands with a weapon in hand and says "give up your wealth"

items.translit: Naatorum Naati Muraiseyyaa Mannavan / Naatorum Naatu Ketum
items.en: Who makes no daily search for wrongs, nor justly rules, that king / Doth day by day his realm to ruin bring
items.en_prose: The country of the king who does not daily examine into the wrongs done and distribute justice, will daily fall to ruin

items.translit: Koozhung Kutiyum Orungizhakkum Kolkotich / Choozhaadhu Seyyum Arasu
items.en: Whose rod from right deflects, who counsel doth refuse, At once his wealth and people utterly shall lose
items.en_prose: The king, who, without reflecting (on its evil consequences), perverts justice, will lose at once both his wealth and his subjects

items.translit: Allarpattu Aatraadhu Azhudhakan Neerandre / Selvaththaith Theykkum Patai
items.en: His people's tears of sorrow past endurance, are not they / Sharp instruments to wear the monarch's wealth away
items.en_prose: Will not the tears, shed by a people who cannot endure the oppression which they suffer (from their king), become a saw to waste away his wealth ?

items.translit: Mannarkku Mannudhal Sengonmai Aqdhindrel / Mannaavaam Mannark Koli
items.en: To rulers' rule stability is sceptre right; When this is not, quenched is the rulers' light
items.en_prose: Righteous government gives permanence to (the fame of) kings; without that their fame will have no endurance

items.translit: Thuliyinmai Gnaalaththirku Etratre Vendhan / Aliyinmai Vaazhum Uyirkku
items.en: As lack of rain to thirsty lands beneath, Is lack of grace in kings to all that breathe
items.en_prose: As is the world without rain, so live a people whose king is without kindness

items.translit: Inmaiyin Innaadhu Utaimai Muraiseyyaa / Mannavan Korkeezhp Patin
items.en: To poverty it adds a sharper sting, To live beneath the sway of unjust king
items.en_prose: Property gives more sorrow than poverty, to those who live under the sceptre of a king without justice

items.translit: Muraikoti Mannavan Seyyin Uraikoti / Ollaadhu Vaanam Peyal
items.en: Where king from right deflecting, makes unrighteous gain, The seasons change, the clouds pour down no rain
items.en_prose: If the king acts contrary to justice, rain will become unseasonable, and the heavens will withhold their showers

items.translit: Aapayan Kundrum Arudhozhilor Noolmarappar / Kaavalan Kaavaan Enin
items.en: Where guardian guardeth not, udder of kine grows dry, And Brahmans' sacred lore will all forgotten lie
items.en_prose: If the guardian (of the country) neglects to guard it, the produce of the cows will fail, and the men of six duties viz, the Brahmins will forget the vedas

items.translit: Thakkaangu Naatith Thalaichchellaa Vannaththaal / Oththaangu Oruppadhu Vendhu
items.en: Who punishes, investigation made in due degree, So as to stay advance of crime, a king is he
items.en_prose: He is a king who having equitably examined (any injustice which has been brought to his notice), suitably punishes it, so that it may not be again committed

items.translit: Katidhochchi Mella Erika Netidhaakkam / Neengaamai Ventu Pavar
items.en: For length of days with still increasing joys on Heav'n who call, Should raise the rod with brow severe, but let it gently fall
items.en_prose: Let the king, who desires that his prosperity may long remain, commence his preliminary enquires with strictness, and then punish with mildness

items.translit: Veruvandha Seydhozhukum Vengola Naayin / Oruvandham Ollaik Ketum
items.en: Where subjects dread of cruel wrongs endure, Ruin to unjust king is swift and sure
items.en_prose: The cruel-sceptred king, who acts so as to put his subjects in fear, will certainly and quickly come to ruin

items.translit: Iraikatiyan Endruraikkum Innaachchol Vendhan / Uraikatuki Ollaik Ketum
items.en: 'Ah! cruel is our king', where subjects sadly say, His age shall dwindle, swift his joy of life decay
items.en_prose: The king who is spoken of as cruel will quickly perish; his life becoming shortened

items.translit: Arunjevvi Innaa Mukaththaan Perunjelvam / Peeykan Tannadhu Utaiththu
items.en: Whom subjects scarce may see, of harsh forbidding countenance; His ample wealth shall waste, blasted by demon's glance
items.en_prose: The great wealth of him who is difficult of access and possesses a sternness of countenance, is like that which has been obtained by a devil

items.translit: Katunjollan Kannilan Aayin Netunjelvam / Neetindri Aange Ketum
items.en: The tyrant, harsh in speach and hard of eye, His ample joy, swift fading, soon shall die
items.en_prose: The abundant wealth of the king whose words are harsh and whose looks are void of kindness, will instantly perish instead of abiding long, with him

items.translit: Katumozhiyum Kaiyikandha Thantamum Vendhan / Atumuran Theykkum Aram
items.en: Harsh words and punishments severe beyond the right, Are file that wears away the monarch's conquering might
items.en_prose: Severe words and excessive punishments will be a file to waste away a king's power for destroying (his enemies)

items.translit: Inaththaatri Ennaadha Vendhan Sinaththaatrich / Cheerir Sirukum Thiru
items.en: Who leaves the work to those around, and thinks of it no more; If he in wrathful mood reprove, his prosperous days are o'er
items.en_prose: The prosperity of that king will waste away, who without reflecting (on his affairs himself), commits them to his ministers, and (when a failure occurs) gives way to anger, and rages against them

items.translit: Seruvandha Pozhdhir Siraiseyyaa Vendhan / Veruvandhu Veydhu Ketum
items.en: Who builds no fort whence he may foe defy, In time of war shall fear and swiftly die
items.en_prose: The king who has not provided himself with a place of defence, will in times of war be seized with fear and quickly perish

items.translit: Kallaarp Pinikkum Katungol Adhuvalladhu / Illai Nilakkup Porai
items.en: Tyrants with fools their counsels share:Earth can no heavier burthen bear
items.en_prose: The earth bears up no greater burden than ignorant men whom a cruel sceptre attaches to itself (as the ministers of its evil deeds)

items.translit: Kannottam Ennum Kazhiperung Kaarikai / Unmaiyaan Untiv Vulaku
items.en: Since true benignity, that grace exceeding great, resides / In kingly souls, world in happy state abides
items.en_prose: The world exists through that greatest ornament (of princes), a gracious demeanour

items.translit: Kannottath Thulladhu Ulakiyal Aqdhilaar / Unmai Nilakkup Porai
items.en: The world goes on its wonted way, since grace benign is there; All other men are burthen for the earth to bear
items.en_prose: The prosperity of the world springs from the kindliness, the existence of those who have no (kindliness) is a burden to the earth

items.translit: Panennaam Paatarku Iyaipindrel Kanennaam / Kannottam Illaadha Kan
items.en: Where not accordant with the song, what use of sounding chords / What gain of eye that no benignant light affords
items.en_prose: Of what avail is a song if it be inconsistent with harmony ? what is the use of eyes which possess no kindliness

items.translit: Ulapol Mukaththevan Seyyum Alavinaal / Kannottam Illaadha Kan
items.en: The seeming eye of face gives no expressive light, When not with duly meted kindness bright
items.en_prose: Beyond appearing to be in the face, what good do they do, those eyes in which is no well-regulated kindness ?

items.translit: Kannirku Anikalam Kannottam Aqdhindrel / Punnendru Unarap Patum
items.en: Benignity is eyes' adorning grace; Without it eyes are wounds disfiguring face
items.en_prose: Kind looks are the ornaments of the eyes; without these they will be considered (by the wise) to be merely two sores

items.translit: Manno Tiyaindha Maraththanaiyar Kanno / Tiyaindhukan Notaa Thavar
items.en: Whose eyes 'neath brow infixed diffuse no ray / Of grace; like tree in earth infixed are they
items.en_prose: They resemble the trees of the earth, who although they have eyes, never look kindly (on others)

items.translit: Kannottam Illavar Kannilar Kannutaiyaar / Kannottam Inmaiyum Il
items.en: Eyeless are they whose eyes with no benignant lustre shine; Who've eyes can never lack the light of grace benign
items.en_prose: Men without kind looks are men without eyes; those who (really) have eyes are also not devoid of kind looks

items.translit: Karumam Sidhaiyaamal Kannota Vallaarkku / Urimai Utaiththiv Vulaku
items.en: Who can benignant smile, yet leave no work undone; By them as very own may all the earth be won
items.en_prose: The world is theirs (kings) who are able to show kindness, without injury to their affairs, (administration of justice)

items.translit: Oruththaatrum Panpinaar Kannumkan Notip / Poruththaatrum Panpe Thalai
items.en: To smile on those that vex, with kindly face, Enduring long, is most excelling grace
items.en_prose: Patiently to bear with, and show kindness to those who grieve us, is the most excellent of all dispositions

items.translit: Peyakkantum Nanjun Tamaivar Nayaththakka / Naakarikam Ventu Pavar
items.en: They drink with smiling grace, though poison interfused they see, Who seek the praise of all-esteemed courtesy
items.en_prose: Those who desire (to cultivate that degree of) urbanity which all shall love, even after swallowing the poison served to them by their friends, will be friendly with them

items.translit: Otrum Uraisaandra Noolum Ivaiyirantum / Thetrenka Mannavan Kan
items.en: These two: the code renowned and spies, In these let king confide as eyes
items.en_prose: Let a king consider as his eyes these two things, a spy and a book (of laws) universally esteemed

items.translit: Ellaarkkum Ellaam Nikazhpavai Egngnaandrum / Vallaridhal Vendhan Thozhil
items.en: Each day, of every subject every deed,'Tis duty of the king to learn with speed
items.en_prose: 'Tis duty of the king to learn with speed

items.translit: Otrinaan Otrip Poruldheriyaa Mannavan / Kotrang Kolakkitandhadhu Il
items.en: By spies who spies, not weighing things they bring, Nothing can victory give to that unwary king
items.en_prose: There is no way for a king to obtain conquests, who knows not the advantage of discoveries made by a spy

items.translit: Vinaiseyvaar Thamsutram Ventaadhaar Endraangu / Anaivaraiyum Aaraaivadhu Otru
items.en: His officers, his friends, his enemies, All these who watch are trusty spies
items.en_prose: He is a spy who watches all men, to wit, those who are in the king's employment, his relatives, and his enemies

items.translit: Kataaa Uruvotu Kannanjaadhu Yaantum / Ukaaamai Valladhe Otru
items.en: Of unsuspected mien and all-unfearing eyes, Who let no secret out, are trusty spies
items.en_prose: A spy is one who is able to assume an appearance which may create no suspicion (in the minds of others), who fears no man's face, and who never reveals (his purpose)

items.translit: Thurandhaar Pativaththa Raaki Irandhaaraaindhu / Enseyinum Sorviladhu Otru
items.en: As monk or devotee, through every hindrance making way, A spy, whate'er men do, must watchful mind display
items.en_prose: He is a spy who, assuming the appearance of an ascetic, goes into (whatever place he wishes), examines into (all, that is needful), and never discovers himself, whatever may be done to him

items.translit: Maraindhavai Ketkavar Raaki Arindhavai / Aiyappaatu Illadhe Otru
items.en: A spy must search each hidden matter out, And full report must render, free from doubt
items.en_prose: A spy is one who is able to discover what is hidden and who retains no doubt concerning what he has known

items.translit: Otrotrith Thandha Porulaiyum Matrumor / Otrinaal Otrik Kolal
items.en: Spying by spies, the things they tell / To test by other spies is well
items.en_prose: Let not a king receive the information which a spy has discovered and made known to him, until he has examined it by another spy

items.translit: Otrer Runaraamai Aalka Utanmoovar / Sotrokka Therap Patum
items.en: One spy must not another see: contrive it so; And things by three confirmed as truth you know
items.en_prose: Let a king employ spies so that one may have no knowledge of the other; and when the information of three agrees together, let him receive it

items.translit: Sirappariya Otrinkan Seyyarka Seyyin / Purappatuththaan Aakum Marai
items.en: Reward not trusty spy in others' sight, Or all the mystery will come to light
items.en_prose: Let not a king publicly confer on a spy any marks of his favour; if he does, he will divulge his own secret

items.translit: Utaiyar Enappatuvadhu Ookkam Aqdhillaar / Utaiyadhu Utaiyaro Matru
items.en: 'Tis energy gives men o'er that they own a true control; They nothing own who own not energy of soul
items.en_prose: Energy makes out the man of property; as for those who are destitute of it, do they (really) possess what they possess ?

items.translit: Ullam Utaimai Utaimai Porulutaimai / Nillaadhu Neengi Vitum
items.en: The wealth of mind man owns a real worth imparts, Material wealth man owns endures not, utterly departs
items.en_prose: The possession of (energy of) mind is true property; the possession of wealth passes away and abides not

items.translit: Aakkam Izhandhemendru Allaavaar Ookkam / Oruvandham Kaiththutai Yaar
items.en: 'Lost is our wealth,' they utter not this cry distressed, The men of firm concentred energy of soul possessed
items.en_prose: They who are possessed of enduring energy will not trouble themselves, saying, "we have lost our property."

items.translit: Aakkam Adharvinaaich Chellum Asaivilaa / Ookka Mutaiyaa Nuzhai
items.en: The man of energy of soul inflexible, Good fortune seeks him out and comes a friend to dwell
items.en_prose: Wealth will find its own way to the man of unfailing energy

items.translit: Vellath Thanaiya Malarneettam Maandhardham / Ullath Thanaiyadhu Uyarvu
items.en: With rising flood the rising lotus flower its stem unwinds; The dignity of men is measured by their minds
items.en_prose: The stalks of water-flowers are proportionate to the depth of water; so is men's greatness proportionate to their minds

items.translit: Ulluva Thellaam Uyarvullal Matradhu / Thallinun Thallaamai Neerththu
items.en: Whate'er you ponder, let your aim be loftly still, Fate cannot hinder always, thwart you as it will
items.en_prose: In all that a king thinks of, let him think of his greatness; and if it should be thrust from him (by fate), it will have the nature of not being thrust from him

items.translit: Sidhaivitaththu Olkaar Uravor Pudhaiyampir / Pattuppaa Toondrung Kaliru
items.en: The men of lofty mind quail not in ruin's fateful hour, The elephant retains his dignity mind arrows' deadly shower
items.en_prose: The strong minded will not faint, even when all is lost; the elephant stands firm, even when wounded by a shower of arrows

items.translit: Ullam Ilaadhavar Eydhaar Ulakaththu / Valliyam Ennunj Cherukku
items.en: The soulless man can never gain / Th' ennobling sense of power with men
items.en_prose: Those who have no (greatness of) mind, will not acquire the joy of saying in the world, "we have excercised liaberality"

items.translit: Pariyadhu Koorngottadhu Aayinum Yaanai / Veruum Pulidhaak Kurin
items.en: Huge bulk of elephant with pointed tusk all armed, When tiger threatens shrinks away alarmed
items.en_prose: Although the elephant has a large body, and a sharp tusk, yet it fears the attack of the tiger

items.translit: Uramoruvarku Ulla Verukkaiaq Thillaar / Marammakka Laadhale Veru
items.en: Firmness of soul in man is real excellance; Others are trees, their human form a mere pretence
items.en_prose: Energy is mental wealth; those men who are destitute of it are only trees in the form of men

items.translit: Kutiyennum Kundraa Vilakkam Matiyennum / Maasoora Maaindhu Ketum
items.en: Of household dignity the lustre beaming bright, Flickers and dies when sluggish foulness dims its light
items.en_prose: By the darkness, of idleness, the indestructible lamp of family (rank) will be extinguished

items.translit: Matiyai Matiyaa Ozhukal Kutiyaik / Kutiyaaka Ventu Pavar
items.en: Let indolence, the death of effort, die, If you'd uphold your household's dignity
items.en_prose: Let those, who desire that their family may be illustrious, put away all idleness from their conduct

items.translit: Matimatik Kontozhukum Pedhai Pirandha / Kutimatiyum Thanninum Mundhu
items.en: Who fosters indolence within his breast, the silly elf!The house from which he springs shall perish ere himself
items.en_prose: The (lustre of the) family of the ignorant man, who acts under the influence of destructive laziness will perish, even before he is dead

items.translit: Kutimatindhu Kutram Perukum Matimatindhu / Maanta Ugnatri Lavarkku
items.en: His family decays, and faults unheeded thrive, Who, sunk in sloth, for noble objects doth not strive
items.en_prose: Family (greatness) will be destroyed, and faults will increase, in those men who give way to laziness, and put forth no dignified exertions

items.translit: Netuneer Maravi Matidhuyil Naankum / Ketuneeraar Kaamak Kalan
items.en: Delay, oblivion, sloth, and sleep: these four / Are pleasure-boat to bear the doomed to ruin's shore
items.en_prose: Procrastination, forgetfulness, idleness, and sleep, these four things, form the vessel which is desired by those destined to destruction

items.translit: Patiyutaiyaar Patramaindhak Kannum Matiyutaiyaar / Maanpayan Eydhal Aridhu
items.en: Though lords of earth unearned possessions gain, The slothful ones no yield of good obtain
items.en_prose: It is a rare thing for the idle, even when possessed of the riches of kings who ruled over the whole earth, to derive any great benefit from it

items.translit: Itipurindhu Ellunj Chol Ketpar / Matipurindhu Maanta Ugnatri Lavar
items.en: Who hug their sloth, nor noble works attempt, Shall bear reproofs and words of just contempt
items.en_prose: Those who through idleness, and do not engage themselves in dignified exertion, will subject

items.translit: Matimai Kutimaikkan Thangindhan Onnaarkku / Atimai Pukuththi Vitum
items.en: If sloth a dwelling find mid noble family, Bondsmen to them that hate them shall they be
items.en_prose: If idleness take up its abode in a king of high birth, it will make him a slave of his enemies

items.translit: Kutiyaanmai Yulvandha Kutram Oruvan / Matiyaanmai Maatrak Ketum
items.en: Who changes slothful habits saves / Himself from all that household rule depraves
items.en_prose: When a man puts away idleness, the reproach which has come upon himself and his family will disappear

items.translit: Matiyilaa Mannavan Eydhum Atiyalandhaan / Thaaaya Thellaam Orungu
items.en: The king whose life from sluggishness is rid, Shall rule o'er all by foot of mighty god bestrid
items.en_prose: The king who never gives way to idleness will obtain entire possession of (the whole earth) passed over by him who measured (the worlds) with His foot

items.translit: Arumai Utaiththendru Asaavaamai Ventum / Perumai Muyarsi Tharum
items.en: Say not, 'Tis hard', in weak, desponding hour, For strenuous effort gives prevailing power
items.en_prose: Yield not to the feebleness which says, "this is too difficult to be done"; labour will give the greatness (of mind) which is necessary (to do it)

items.translit: Vinaikkan Vinaiketal Ompal Vinaikkurai / Theerndhaarin Theerndhandru Ulaku
items.en: In action be thou, 'ware of act's defeat; The world leaves those who work leave incomplete
items.en_prose: Take care not to give up exertion in the midst of a work; the world will abandon those who abandon their unfinished work

items.translit: Thaalaanmai Ennum Thakaimaikkan Thangitre / Velaanmai Ennunj Cherukku
items.en: In strenuous effort doth reside / The power of helping others: noble pride
items.en_prose: The lustre of munificence will dwell only with the dignity of laboriousness or efforts

items.translit: Thaalaanmai Illaadhaan Velaanmai Petikai / Vaalaanmai Polak Ketum
items.en: Beneficent intent in men by whom no strenuous work is wrought, Like battle-axe in sexless being's hand availeth nought
items.en_prose: The liberality of him, who does not labour, will fail, like the manliness of a hermaphrodite, who has a sword in its hand

items.translit: Inpam Vizhaiyaan Vinaivizhaivaan Thankelir / Thunpam Thutaiththoondrum Thoon
items.en: Whose heart delighteth not in pleasure, but in action finds delight, He wipes away his kinsmen's grief and stands the pillar of their might
items.en_prose: He who desires not pleasure, but desires labour, will be a pillar to sustain his relations, wiping away their sorrows

items.translit: Muyarsi Thiruvinai Aakkum Muyatrinmai / Inmai Pukuththi Vitum
items.en: Effort brings fortune's sure increase, Its absence brings to nothingness
items.en_prose: Labour will produce wealth; idleness will bring poverty

items.translit: Matiyulaal Maamukati Enpa Matiyilaan / Thaalulaan Thaamaraiyi Naal
items.en: In sluggishness is seen misfortune's lurid form, the wise declare; Where man unslothful toils, she of the lotus flower is there
items.en_prose: They say that the black Mudevi (the goddess of adversity) dwells with laziness, and the Latchmi (the goddess of prosperity) dwells with the labour of the industrious

items.translit: Poriyinmai Yaarkkum Pazhiyandru Arivarindhu / Aalvinai Inmai Pazhi
items.en: 'Tis no reproach unpropitious fate should ban; But not to do man's work is foul disgrace to man
items.en_prose: Adverse fate is no disgrace to any one; to be without exertion and without knowing what should be known, is disgrace

items.translit: Theyvaththaan Aakaa Theninum Muyarsidhan / Meyvaruththak Kooli Tharum
items.en: Though fate-divine should make your labour vain; Effort its labour's sure reward will gain
items.en_prose: Although it be said that, through fate, it cannot be attained, yet labour, with bodily exertion, will yield its reward

items.translit: Oozhaiyum Uppakkam Kaanpar Ulaivindrith / Thaazhaadhu Ugnatru Pavar
items.en: Who strive with undismayed, unfaltering mind, At length shall leave opposing fate behind
items.en_prose: They who labour on, without fear and without fainting will see even fate (put) behind their back

items.translit: Itukkan Varungaal Nakuka Adhanai / Atuththoorvadhu Aqdhoppa Thil
items.en: Smile, with patient, hopeful heart, in troublous hour; Meet and so vanquish grief; nothing hath equal power
items.en_prose: If troubles come, laugh; there is nothing like that, to press upon and drive away sorrow

items.translit: Vellath Thanaiya Itumpai Arivutaiyaan / Ullaththin Ullak Ketum
items.en: Though sorrow, like a flood, comes rolling on, When wise men's mind regards it,- it is gone
items.en_prose: A flood of troubles will be overcome by the (courageous) thought which the minds of the wise will entertain, even in sorrow

items.translit: Itumpaikku Itumpai Patuppar Itumpaikku / Itumpai Pataaa Thavar
items.en: Who griefs confront with meek, ungrieving heart, From them griefs, put to grief, depart
items.en_prose: They give sorrow to sorrow, who in sorrow do not suffer sorrow

items.translit: Matuththavaa Yellaam Pakatannaan Utra / Itukkan Itarppaatu Utaiththu
items.en: Like bullock struggle on through each obstructed way; From such an one will troubles, troubled, roll away
items.en_prose: Troubles will vanish (i.e., will be troubled) before the man who (struggles against difficulties) as a

items.translit: Atukki Varinum Azhivilaan Utra / Itukkan Itukkat Patum
items.en: When griefs press on, but fail to crush the patient heart, Then griefs defeated, put to grief, depart
items.en_prose: The troubles of that man will be troubled (and disappear) who, however thickly they may come upon him, does not abandon (his purpose)

items.translit: Atremendru Allar Patupavo Petremendru / Ompudhal Thetraa Thavar
items.en: Who boasted not of wealth, nor gave it all their heart, Will not bemoan the loss, when prosperous days depart
items.en_prose: Will those men ever cry out in sorrow, "we are destitute" who, (in their prosperity), give not way to (undue desire) to keep their wealth

items.translit: Ilakkam Utampitumpaik Kendru Kalakkaththaik / Kaiyaaraak Kollaadhaam Mel
items.en: 'Man's frame is sorrow's target', the noble mind reflects, Nor meets with troubled mind the sorrows it expects
items.en_prose: The great will not regard trouble as trouble, knowing that the body is the butt of trouble

items.translit: Inpam Vizhaiyaan Itumpai Iyalpenpaan / Thunpam Urudhal Ilan
items.en: He seeks not joy, to sorrow man is born, he knows; Such man will walk unharmed by touch of human woes
items.en_prose: That man never experiences sorrow, who does not seek for pleasure, and who considers distress to be natural (to man)

items.translit: Inpaththul Inpam Vizhaiyaadhaan Thunpaththul / Thunpam Urudhal Ilan
items.en: Mid joys he yields not heart to joys' control / Mid sorrows, sorrow cannot touch his soul
items.en_prose: He does not suffer sorrow, in sorrow who does not look for pleasure in pleasure

items.translit: Innaamai Inpam Enakkolin Aakundhan / Onnaar Vizhaiyunj Chirappu
items.en: Who pain as pleasure takes, he shall acquire / The bliss to which his foes in vain aspire
items.en_prose: The elevation, which even his enemies will esteem, will be gained by him, who regards pain as pleasure

items.translit: Karuviyum Kaalamum Seykaiyum Seyyum / Aruvinaiyum Maantadhu Amaichchu
items.en: A minister is he who grasps, with wisdom large, Means, time, work's mode, and functions rare he must discharge
items.en_prose: The minister is one who can make an excellent choice of means, time, manner of execution, and the difficult undertaking (itself)

items.translit: Vankan Kutikaaththal Katraridhal Aalvinaiyotu / Aindhutan Maantadhu Amaichchu
items.en: A minister must greatness own of guardian power, determined mind, Learn'd wisdom, manly effort with the former five combined
items.en_prose: The minister is one who in addition to the aforesaid five things excels in the possession of firmness,

items.translit: Piriththalum Penik Kolalum Pirindhaarp / Poruththalum Valla Thamaichchu
items.en: A minister is he whose power can foes divide, Attach more firmly friends, of severed ones can heal the breaches wide
items.en_prose: The minister is one who can effect discord (among foes), maintain the good-will of his friends and restore to friendship those who have seceded (from him)

items.translit: Theridhalum Therndhu Seyalum Orudhalaiyaach / Chollalum Valladhu Amaichchu
items.en: A minister has power to see the methods help afford, To ponder long, then utter calm conclusive word
items.en_prose: The minister is one who is able to comprehend (the whole nature of an undertaking), execute it in the best manner possible, and offer assuring advice (in time of necessity)

items.translit: Aranarindhu Aandramaindha Sollaanenj Gnaandrun / Thiranarindhaan Therchchith Thunai
items.en: The man who virtue knows, has use of wise and pleasant words / With plans for every season apt, in counsel aid affords
items.en_prose: He is the best helper (of the king) who understanding the duties, of the latter, is by his special learning, able to tender the fullest advice, and at all times conversant with the best method (of

items.translit: Madhinutpam Noolotu Utaiyaarkku Adhinutpam / Yaavula Munnir Pavai
items.en: When native subtilty combines with sound scholastic lore,'Tis subtilty surpassing all, which nothing stands before
items.en_prose: What (contrivances) are there so acute as to resist those who possess natural acuteness in addition to learning ?

items.translit: Seyarkai Arindhak Kataiththum Ulakaththu / Iyarkai Arindhu Seyal
items.en: Though knowing all that books can teach, 'tis truest tact / To follow common sense of men in act
items.en_prose: Though you are acquainted with the (theoretical) methods (of performing an act), understand the ways of the world and act accordingly

items.translit: Arikondru Ariyaan Eninum Urudhi / Uzhaiyirundhaan Kooral Katan
items.en: 'Tis duty of the man in place aloud to say / The very truth, though unwise king may cast his words away
items.en_prose: Although the king be utterly ignorant, it is the duty of the minister to give (him) sound advice

items.translit: Pazhudhennum Mandhiriyin Pakkadhadhul Thevvor / Ezhupadhu Koti Urum
items.en: A minister who by king's side plots evil things / Worse woes than countless foemen brings
items.en_prose: Far better are seventy crores of enemies (for a king) than a minister at his side who intends (his) ruin

items.translit: Muraippatach Choozhndhum Mutivilave Seyvar / Thirappaatu Ilaaa Thavar
items.en: For gain of end desired just counsel nought avails / To minister, when tact in execution fails
items.en_prose: Those ministers who are destitute of (executive) ability will fail to carry out their projects, although they may have contrived aright

items.translit: Naanalam Ennum Nalanutaimai Annalam / Yaanalaththu Ulladhooum Andru
items.en: A tongue that rightly speaks the right is greatest gain, It stands alone midst goodly things that men obtain
items.en_prose: The possession of that goodness which is called the goodness of speech is (even to others) better than any other goodness

items.translit: Aakkamung Ketum Adhanaal Varudhalaal / Kaaththompal Sollinkat Sorvu
items.en: Since gain and loss in life on speech depend, From careless slip in speech thyself defend
items.en_prose: Since (both) wealth and evil result from (their) speech, ministers should most carefully guard themselves against faultiness therein

items.translit: Kettaarp Pinikkum Thakaiyavaaik Kelaarum / Vetpa Mozhivadhaam Sol
items.en: 'Tis speech that spell-bound holds the listening ear, While those who have not heard desire to hear
items.en_prose: The (minister's) speech is that which seeks (to express) elements as bind his friends (to himself) and is so delivered as to make even his enemies desire (his friendship)

items.translit: Thiranarindhu Solluka Sollai Aranum / Porulum Adhaninooungu Il
items.en: Speak words adapted well to various hearers' state; No higher virtue lives, no gain more surely great
items.en_prose: Understand the qualities (of your hearers) and (then) make your speech; for superior to it, there is neither virtue nor wealth

items.translit: Solluka Sollaip Piridhorsol Achchollai / Vellunjol Inmai Arindhu
items.en: Speak out your speech, when once 'tis past dispute / That none can utter speech that shall your speech refute
items.en_prose: Deliver your speech, after assuring yourself that no counter speech can defeat your own

items.translit: Vetpaththaanj Chollip Pirarsol Payankotal / Maatchiyin Maasatraar Kol
items.en: Charming each hearer's ear, of others' words to seize the sense, Is method wise of men of spotless excellence
items.en_prose: It is the opinion of those who are free from defects in diplomacy that the minister should speak so as to make his hearers desire (to hear more) and grasp the meaning of what he hears himself

items.translit: Solalvallan Sorvilan Anjaan Avanai / Ikalvellal Yaarkkum Aridhu
items.en: Mighty in word, of unforgetful mind, of fearless speech,'Tis hard for hostile power such man to overreach
items.en_prose: It is impossible for any one to conquer him by intrique who possesses power of speech, and is neither faulty nor timid

items.translit: Viraindhu Thozhilketkum Gnaalam Nirandhinidhu / Solludhal Vallaarp Perin
items.en: Swiftly the listening world will gather round, When men of mighty speech the weighty theme propound
items.en_prose: If there be those who can speak on various subjects in their proper order and in a pleasing manner, the world would readily accept them

items.translit: Palasollak Kaamuruvar Mandramaa Satra / Silasollal Thetraa Thavar
items.en: Who have not skill ten faultless words to utter plain, Their tongues will itch with thousand words man's ears to pain
items.en_prose: They will desire to utter many words, who do not know how to speak a few faultless ones

items.translit: Inaruzhththum Naaraa Malaranaiyar Katradhu / Unara Viriththuraiyaa Thaar
items.en: Like scentless flower in blooming garland bound / Are men who can't their lore acquired to other's ears expound
items.en_prose: Those who are unable to set forth their acquirements (before others) are like flowers blossoming in a cluster and yet without fragrance

items.translit: Thunainalam Aakkam Tharuum Vinainalam / Ventiya Ellaan Tharum
items.en: The good external help confers is worldly gain; By action good men every needed gift obtain
items.en_prose: The efficacy of support will yield (only) wealth; (but) the efficacy of action will yield all that is desired

items.translit: Endrum Oruvudhal Ventum Pukazhotu / Nandri Payavaa Vinai
items.en: From action evermore thyself restrain / Of glory and of good that yields no gain
items.en_prose: Ministers should at all times avoid acts which, in addition to fame, yield no benefit (for the future)

items.translit: Oodhal Ventum Olimaazhkum Seyvinai / Aaadhum Ennu Mavar
items.en: Who tell themselves that nobler things shall yet be won / All deeds that dim the light of glory must they shun
items.en_prose: Those who say, "we will become (better)" should avoid the performance of acts that would destroy (their fame)

items.translit: Itukkan Patinum Ilivandha Seyyaar / Natukkatra Kaatchi Yavar
items.en: Though troubles press, no shameful deed they do, Whose eyes the ever-during vision view
items.en_prose: Those who have infallible judgement though threatened with peril will not do acts which have brought disgrace (on former ministers)

items.translit: Etrendru Iranguva Seyyarka Seyvaanel / Matranna Seyyaamai Nandru
items.en: Do nought that soul repenting must deplore, If thou hast sinned, 'tis well if thou dost sin no more
items.en_prose: Let a minister never do acts of which he would have to grieve saying, "what is this I have done"; (but) should he do (them), it were good that he grieved not

items.translit: Eendraal Pasikaanpaan Aayinunj Cheyyarka / Saandror Pazhikkum Vinai
items.en: Though her that bore thee hung'ring thou behold, no deed / Do thou, that men of perfect soul have crime decreed
items.en_prose: Though a minister may see his mother starve; let him do not act which the wise would (treat with contempt)

items.translit: Pazhimalaindhu Eydhiya Aakkaththin Saandror / Kazhinal Kurave Thalai
items.en: Than store of wealth guilt-laden souls obtain, The sorest poverty of perfect soul is richer gain
items.en_prose: Far more excellent is the extreme poverty of the wise than wealth obtained by heaping up of sinful

items.translit: Katindha Katindhoraar Seydhaarkku Avaidhaam / Mutindhaalum Peezhai Tharum
items.en: To those who hate reproof and do forbidden thing / What prospers now, in after days shall anguish bring
items.en_prose: The actions of those, who have not desisted from doing deeds forbidden (by the great), will, even if they succeed, cause them sorrow

items.translit: Azhak Konta Ellaam Azhappom / Izhappinum Pirpayakkum Narpaa Lavai
items.en: What's gained through tears with tears shall go; From loss good deeds entail harvests of blessings grow
items.en_prose: All that has been obtained with tears (to the victim) will depart with tears (to himself); but what has been by fair means; though with loss at first, will afterwards yield fruit

items.translit: Salaththaal Porulseydhe Maarththal Pasuman / Kalaththulneer Peydhireei Yatru
items.en: In pot of clay unburnt he water pours and would retain, Who seeks by wrong the realm in wealth and safety to maintain
items.en_prose: (For a minister) to protect (his king) with wealth obtained by foul means is like preserving a vessel of wet clay by filling it with water

items.translit: Vinaiththitpam Enpadhu Oruvan Manaththitpam / Matraiya Ellaam Pira
items.en: What men call 'power in action' know for 'power of mind'Externe to man all other aids you find
items.en_prose: Firmness in action is (simply) one's firmness of mind; all other (abilities) are not of this nature

items.translit: Oororaal Utrapin Olkaamai Ivvirantin / Aarenpar Aaindhavar Kol
items.en: 'Each hindrance shun', 'unyielding onward press, If obstacle be there,'These two define your way, so those that search out truth declare
items.en_prose: Not to perform a ruinous act, and not to be discouraged by the ruinous termination of an act, are the two maxims which, the wise say, from the principles of those who have investigated the subject

items.translit: Kataikkotkach Cheydhakka Thaanmai Itaikkotkin / Etraa Vizhuman Tharum
items.en: Man's fitting work is known but by success achieved; In midst the plan revealed brings ruin ne'er to be retrieved
items.en_prose: So to perform an act as to publish it (only) at its termination is (true) manliness; for to announce it beforehand, will cause irremediable sorrow

items.translit: Solludhal Yaarkkum Eliya Ariyavaam / Solliya Vannam Seyal
items.en: Easy to every man the speech that shows the way; Hard thing to shape one's life by words they say
items.en_prose: To say (how an act is to be performed) is (indeed) easy for any one; but far difficult it is to do according to what has been said

items.translit: Veereydhi Maantaar Vinaiththitpam Vendhankan / Ooreydhi Ullap Patum
items.en: The power in act of men renowned and great, With king acceptance finds and fame through all the state
items.en_prose: The firmness in action of those who have become great by the excellence (of their counsel) will, by attaining its fulfilment in the person of the king, be esteemed (by all).

items.translit: Enniya Enniyaangu Eydhu Enniyaar / Thinniyar Aakap Perin
items.en: Whate'er men think, ev'n as they think, may men obtain, If those who think can steadfastness of will retain
items.en_prose: If those who have planned (an undertaking) possess firmness (in executing it) they will obtain what they have desired even as they have desired it

items.translit: Uruvukantu Ellaamai Ventum Urulperundherkku / Achchaani Annaar Utaiththu
items.en: Despise not men of modest bearing; Look not at form, but what men are:For some there live, high functions sharing, Like linch-pin of the mighty car
items.en_prose: Let none be despised for (their) size; (for) the world has those who resemble the linch-pin of the big rolling car

items.translit: Kalangaadhu Kanta Vinaikkan Thulangaadhu / Thookkang Katindhu Seyal
items.en: What clearly eye discerns as right, with steadfast will, And mind unslumbering, that should man fulfil
items.en_prose: An act that has been firmly resolved on must be as firmly carried out without delay

items.translit: Thunpam Uravarinum Seyka Thunivaatri / Inpam Payakkum Vinai
items.en: Though toil and trouble face thee, firm resolve hold fast, And do the deeds that pleasure yield at last
items.en_prose: Though it should cause increasing sorrow (at the outset), do with firmness the act that yield bliss (in the end)

items.translit: Enaiththitpam Ey Thiyak Kannum / Vinaiththitpam Ventaarai Ventaadhu Ulaku
items.en: The world desires not men of every power possessed, Who power in act desire not,- crown of all the rest
items.en_prose: The great will not esteem those who esteem not firmness of action, whatever other abilities the latter may possess

items.translit: Soozhchchi Mutivu Thuniveydhal Aththunivu / Thaazhchchiyul Thangudhal Theedhu
items.en: The Resolve is counsel's end, If resolutions halt In weak delays, still unfulfilled, 'tis grievous fault
items.en_prose: Consultation ends in forming a resolution (to act); (but) delay in the execution of that resolve is an evil

items.translit: Thoonguka Thoongich Cheyarpaala Thoongarka / Thoongaadhu Seyyum Vinai
items.en: Slumber when sleepy work's in hand beware Thou slumber not when action calls for sleepless care
items.en_prose: Sleep over such (actions) as may be slept over; (but) never over such as may not be slept over

items.translit: Ollumvaa Yellaam Vinainandre Ollaakkaal / Sellumvaai Nokkich Cheyal
items.en: When way is clear, prompt let your action be; When not, watch till some open path you see
items.en_prose: Whenever it is possible (to overcome your enemy) the act (of fighting) is certainly good; if not, endeavour to employ some more successful method

items.translit: Vinaipakai Endrirantin Echcham Ninaiyungaal / Theeyechcham Polath Therum
items.en: With work or foe, when you neglect some little thing, If you reflect, like smouldering fire, 'twill ruin bring
items.en_prose: When duly considered, the incomplete execution of an undertaking and hostility will grow and destroy one like the (unextinguished) remnant of a fire

items.translit: Porulkaruvi Kaalam Vinaiyitanotu Aindhum / Iruldheera Ennich Cheyal
items.en: Treasure and instrument and time and deed and place of act These five, till every doubt remove, think o'er with care exact
items.en_prose: Do an act after a due consideration of the (following) five, viz money, means, time, execution and place

items.translit: Mutivum Itaiyoorum Mutriyaangu Eydhum / Patupayanum Paarththuch Cheyal
items.en: Accomplishment, the hindrances, large profits won By effort these compare,- then let the work be done
items.en_prose: An act is to be performed after considering the exertion required, the obstacles to be encountered, and the great profit to be gained (on its completion)

items.translit: Seyvinai Seyvaan Seyanmurai Avvinai / Ullarivaan Ullam Kolal
items.en: Who would succeed must thus begin first let him ask The thoughts of them who thoroughly know the task
items.en_prose: The method of performance for one who has begun an act is to ascertain the mind of him who knows the secret thereof

items.translit: Vinaiyaan Vinaiyaakkik Kotal Nanaikavul / Yaanaiyaal Yaanaiyaath Thatru
items.en: By one thing done you reach a second work's accomplishment; So furious elephant to snare its fellow brute is sent
items.en_prose: To make one undertaking the means of accomplishing another (similar to it) is like making one rutting elephant the means of capturing another

items.translit: Nattaarkku Nalla Seyalin Viraindhadhe / Ottaarai Ottik Kolal
items.en: Than kindly acts to friends more urgent thing to do, Is making foes to cling as friends attached to you
items.en_prose: One should rather hasten to secure the alliance of the foes (of one's foes) than perform good offices to one's friends

items.translit: Uraisiriyaar Ulnatungal Anjik Kuraiperin / Kolvar Periyaarp Panindhu
items.en: The men of lesser realm, fearing the people's inward dread, Accepting granted terms, to mightier ruler bow the head
items.en_prose: Ministers of small states, afraid of their people being frightened, will yield to and acknowledge their superior foes, if the latter offer them a chance of reconciliation

items.translit: Anputaimai Aandra Kutippiraththal Vendhavaam / Panputaimai Thoodhuraippaan Panpu
items.en: Benevolence high birth, the courtesy kings love:-These qualities the envoy of a king approve
items.en_prose: The qualification of an ambassador are affection (for his relations) a fitting birth, and the possession of attributes pleasing to royalty

items.translit: Anparivu Aaraaindha Solvanmai Thoodhuraippaarkku / Indri Yamaiyaadha Moondru
items.en: Love, knowledge, power of chosen words, three things, Should he possess who speaks the words of kings
items.en_prose: Love (to his sovereign), knowledge (of his affairs), and a discriminating power of speech (before other sovereigns) are the three sine qua non qualifications of an ambassador

items.translit: Noolaarul Noolvallan Aakudhal Velaarul / Vendri Vinaiyuraippaan Panpu
items.en: Mighty in lore amongst the learned must he be, Midst jav'lin-bearing kings who speaks the words of victory
items.en_prose: To be powerful in politics among those who are learned (in ethics) is the character of him who speaks

items.translit: Arivuru Vaaraaindha Kalviim Moondran / Serivutaiyaan Selka Vinaikku
items.en: Sense, goodly grace, and knowledge exquisite / Who hath these three for envoy's task is fit
items.en_prose: He may go on a mission (to foreign rulers) who has combined in him all these three viz, (natural) sense, an attractive bearing and well-tried learning

items.translit: Thokach Chollith Thoovaadha Neekki / Nakachcholli Nandri Payappadhaan Thoodhu
items.en: In terms concise, avoiding wrathful speech, who utters pleasant word, An envoy he who gains advantage for his lord
items.en_prose: He is an ambassador who (in the presence of foreign rulers) speaks briefly, avoids harshness, talks so as to make them smile, and thus brings good (to his own sovereign)

items.translit: Katrukkan Anjaan Selachchollik Kaalaththaal / Thakkadhu Arivadhaam Thoodhu
items.en: An envoy meet is he, well-learned, of fearless eye / Who speaks right home, prepared for each emergency
items.en_prose: He is an ambassador who having studied (politics) talks impressively, is not afraid of angry looks, and knows (to employ) the art suited to the time

items.translit: Katanarindhu Kaalang Karudhi Itanarindhu / Enni Uraippaan Thalai
items.en: He is the best who knows what's due, the time considered well, The place selects, then ponders long ere he his errand tell
items.en_prose: He is chief (among ambassadors) who understands the proper decorum (before foreign princes), seeks the (proper) occasion, knows the (most suitable) place, and delivers his message after (due)

items.translit: Thooimai Thunaimai Thunivutaimai Immoondrin / Vaaimai Vazhiyuraippaan Panpu
items.en: Integrity, resources, soul determined, truthfulness / Who rightly speaks his message must these marks possess
items.en_prose: The qualifications of him who faithfully delivers his (sovereign's) message are purity, the support (of foreign ministers), and boldness, with truthfulness in addition to the (aforesaid) three

items.translit: Vitumaatram Vendharkku Uraippaan Vatumaatram / Vaaiseraa Vanka Navan
items.en: His faltering lips must utter no unworthy thing, Who stands, with steady eye, to speak the mandates of his king
items.en_prose: He alone is fit to communicate (his sovereign's) reply, who possesses the firmness not to utter even inadvertently what may reflect discredit (on the latter)

items.translit: Irudhi Payappinum Enjaadhu Iraivarku / Urudhi Payappadhaam Thoodhu
items.en: Death to the faithful one his embassy may bring; To envoy gains assured advantage for his king
items.en_prose: He is the ambassador who fearlessly seeks his sovereign's good though it should cost him his life (to deliver his message)

items.translit: Akalaadhu Anukaadhu Theekkaaivaar Polka / Ikalvendharch Cherndhozhuku Vaar
items.en: Who warm them at the fire draw not too near, nor keep too much aloof; Thus let them act who dwell beneath of warlike kings the palace-roof
items.en_prose: Thus let them act who dwell beneath of warlike kings the palace-roof

items.translit: Mannar Vizhaipa Vizhaiyaamai Mannaraal / Manniya Aakkan Tharum
items.en: To those who prize not state that kings are wont to prize, The king himself abundant wealth supplies
items.en_prose: For ministers not to cover the things desired by their kings will through the kings themselves yield them everlasting wealth

items.translit: Potrin Ariyavai Potral Katuththapin / Thetrudhal Yaarkkum Aridhu
items.en: Who would walk warily, let him of greater faults beware; To clear suspicions once aroused is an achievement rare
items.en_prose: Ministers who would save themselves should avoid (the commission of) serious errors for if the king's suspicion is once roused, no one can remove it

items.translit: Sevichchollum Serndha Nakaiyum Aviththozhukal / Aandra Periyaa Rakaththu
items.en: All whispered words and interchange of smiles repress, In presence of the men who kingly power possess
items.en_prose: While in the presence of the sovereign, ministers should neither whisper to nor smile at others

items.translit: Epporulum Oraar Thotaraarmar Rapporulai / Vittakkaal Ketka Marai
items.en: Seek not, ask not, the secret of the king to hear; But if he lets the matter forth, give ear
items.en_prose: (When the king is engaged) in secret counsel (with others), ministers should neither over-hear anything whatever nor pry into it with inquisitive questions, but (wait to) listen when it is divulged (by

items.translit: Kuripparindhu Kaalang Karudhi Veruppila / Ventupa Vetpach Cholal
items.en: Knowing the signs, waiting for fitting time, with courteous care, Things not displeasing, needful things, declare
items.en_prose: Knowing the (king's disposition and seeking the right time, (the minister) should in a pleasing manner suggest things such as are desirable and not disagreeable

items.translit: Vetpana Solli Vinaiyila Egngnaandrum / Ketpinum Sollaa Vital
items.en: Speak pleasant things, but never utter idle word; Not though by monarch's ears with pleasure heard
items.en_prose: Ministers should (always) give agreeable advice but on no occasion recommend useless actions, though requested (to do so)

items.translit: Ilaiyar Inamuraiyar Endrikazhaar Nindra / Oliyotu Ozhukap Patum
items.en: Say not, 'He's young, my kinsman,' despising thus your king; But reverence the glory kingly state doth bring
items.en_prose: Ministers should behave in accordance with the (Divine) light in the person of kings and not despise them saying, "He is our junior (in age) and connected with our family!"

items.translit: Kolappattem Endrennik Kollaadha Seyyaar / Thulakkatra Kaatchi Yavar
items.en: 'We've gained his grace, boots nought what graceless acts we do', So deem not sages who the changeless vision view
items.en_prose: Those whose judgement is firm will not do what is disagreeable (to the sovereign) saying (within

items.translit: Pazhaiyam Enakkarudhip Panpalla Seyyum / Kezhudhakaimai Ketu Tharum
items.en: Who think 'We're ancient friends' and do unseemly things; To these familiarity sure ruin brings
items.en_prose: The (foolish) claim with which a minister does unbecoming acts because of his (long) familiarity (with the king) will ensure his ruin

items.translit: Kooraamai Nokkake Kuripparivaan Egngnaandrum / Maaraaneer Vaiyak Kani
items.en: Who knows the sign, and reads unuttered thought, the gem is he, Of earth round traversed by the changeless sea
items.en_prose: The minister who by looking (at the king) understands his mind without being told (of it), will be a perpetual ornament to the world which is surrounded by a never-drying sea

items.translit: Aiyap Pataaadhu Akaththadhu Unarvaanaith / Theyvaththo Toppak Kolal
items.en: Undoubting, who the minds of men can scan, As deity regard that gifted man
items.en_prose: He is to be esteemed a god who is able to ascertain without a doubt what is within (one's mind)

items.translit: Kurippir Kurippunar Vaarai Uruppinul / Yaadhu Kotuththum Kolal
items.en: Who by the sign the signs interprets plain, Give any member up his aid to gain
items.en_prose: The king should ever give whatever (is asked) of his belongings and secure him who, by the indications (of his own mind) is able to read those of another

items.translit: Kuriththadhu Kooraamaik Kolvaaro Tenai / Uruppo Ranaiyaraal Veru
items.en: Who reads what's shown by signs, though words unspoken be, In form may seem as other men, in function nobler far is he
items.en_prose: Those who understand one's thoughts without being informed (thereof) and those who do not, may (indeed) resemble one another bodily; still are they different (mentally)

items.translit: Kurippir Kurippunaraa Vaayin Uruppinul / Enna Payaththavo Kan?
items.en: By sign who knows not sings to comprehend, what gain,'Mid all his members, from his eyes does he obtain
items.en_prose: Of what use are the eyes amongst one's members, if they cannot by their own indications dive those of another ?

items.translit: Atuththadhu Kaattum Palingupol Nenjam / Katuththadhu Kaattum Mukam
items.en: As forms around in crystal mirrored clear we find, The face will show what's throbbing in the mind
items.en_prose: As the mirror reflects what is near so does the face show what is uppermost in the mind

items.translit: Mukaththin Mudhukkuraindhadhu Unto Uvappinum / Kaayinum Thaanmun Thurum
items.en: Than speaking countenance hath aught more prescient skill?Rejoice or burn with rage, 'tis the first herald still
items.en_prose: Is there anything so full of knowledge as the face ? (No) it precedes the mind, whether (the latter is) pleased or vexed

items.translit: Mukamnokki Nirka Amaiyum Akamnokki / Utra Thunarvaarp Perin
items.en: To see the face is quite enough, in presence brought, When men can look within and know the lurking thought
items.en_prose: If the king gets those who by looking into his mind can understand (and remove) what has occurred (to him) it is enough that he stand looking at their face

items.translit: Pakaimaiyum Kenmaiyum Kannuraikkum Kannin / Vakaimai Unarvaarp Perin
items.en: The eye speaks out the hate or friendly soul of man; To those who know the eye's swift varying moods to scan
items.en_prose: If a king gets ministers who can read the movements of the eye, the eyes (of foreign kings) will (themselves) reveal (to him) their hatred or friendship

items.translit: Nunniyam Enpaar Alakkungol Kaanungaal / Kannalladhu Illai Pira
items.en: The men of keen discerning soul no other test apply(When you their secret ask) than man's revealing eye
items.en_prose: The measuring-rod of those (ministers) who say "we are acute" will on inquiry be found to be their (own) eyes and nothing else

items.translit: Avaiyarinadhu Aaraaindhu Solluka Sollin / Thokaiyarindha Thooimai Yavar
items.en: Men pure in heart, who know of words the varied force, Should to their audience known adapt their well-arranged discourse
items.en_prose: Let the pure who know the arrangement of words speak with deliberation after ascertaining (the nature of) the court (then assembled)

items.translit: Itaidherindhu Nankunarndhu Solluka Sollin / Nataidherindha Nanmai Yavar
items.en: Good men to whom the arts of eloquence are known, Should seek occasion meet, and say what well they've made their own
items.en_prose: Let the good who know the uses of words speak with a clear knowledge after ascertaining the time (suited to the court)

items.translit: Avaiyariyaar Sollalmer Kolpavar Sollin / Vakaiyariyaar Valladhooum Il
items.en: Unversed in councils, who essays to speak / Knows not the way of suasive words,- and all is weak
items.en_prose: Those who undertake to speak without knowing the (nature of the) court are ignorant of the quality of words as well as devoid of the power (of learning)

items.translit: Oliyaarmun Olliya Raadhal Veliyaarmun / Vaansudhai Vannam Kolal
items.en: Before the bright ones shine as doth the light / Before the dull ones be as purest stucco white
items.en_prose: Ministers should be lights in the assembly of the enlightned, but assume the pure whiteness of mortar (ignorance) in that of fools

items.translit: Nandrendra Vatrullum Nandre Mudhuvarul / Mundhu Kilavaach Cherivu
items.en: Midst all good things the best is modest grace, That speaks not first before the elders' face
items.en_prose: The modesty by which one does not rush forward and speak in (an assembly of) superiors is the best among all (one's) good qualities

items.translit: Aatrin Nilaidhalarn Thatre Viyanpulam / Etrunarvaar Munnar Izhukku
items.en: As in the way one tottering falls, is slip before / The men whose minds are filled with varied lore
items.en_prose: (For a minister) to blunder in the presence of those who have acquired a vast store of learning and know (the value thereof) is like a good man stumbling (and falling away) from the path (of virtue)

items.translit: Katrarindhaar Kalvi Vilangum Kasatarach / Choldheridhal Vallaar Akaththu
items.en: The learning of the learned sage shines bright / To those whose faultless skill can value it aright
items.en_prose: The learning of those who have read and understood (much) will shine in the assembly of those who faultlessly examine (the nature of) words

items.translit: Unarva Thutaiyaarmun Sollal Valarvadhan / Paaththiyul Neersorin Thatru
items.en: To speak where understanding hearers you obtain, Is sprinkling water on the fields of growing grain
items.en_prose: Lecturing to those who have the ability to understand (for themselves) is like watering a bed of plants that are growing (of themselves)

items.translit: Pullavaiyul Pochchaandhum Sollarka Nallavaiyul / Nankusalach Chollu Vaar
items.en: In councils of the good, who speak good things with penetrating power, In councils of the mean, let them say nought, e'en in oblivious hour
