items.en_prose: Those who are able to speak good things impressively in an assembly of the good should not even forgetfully speak them in that of the low

items.translit: Anganaththul Ukka Amizhdhatraal Thanganaththaar / Allaarmun Kotti Kolal
items.en: Ambrosia in the sewer spilt, is word / Spoken in presence of the alien herd
items.en_prose: To utter (a good word) in the assembly of those who are of inferior rank is like dropping nectar on the ground

items.translit: Vakaiyarindhu Vallavai Vaaisoraar Sollin / Thokaiyarindha Thooimai Yavar
items.en: Men, pure in heart, who know of words the varied force, The mighty council's moods discern, nor fail in their discourse
items.en_prose: The pure who know the classification of words having first ascertained the nature (of the court) will not (through fear) falter in their speech before the powerful body

items.translit: Katraarul Katraar Enappatuvar Katraarmun / Katra Selachchollu Vaar
items.en: Who what they've learned, in penetrating words heve learned to say, Before the learn'd among the learn'd most learn'd are they
items.en_prose: Those who can agreeably set forth their acquirements before the learned will be regarded as the most learned among the learned

items.translit: Pakaiyakaththuch Chaavaar Eliyar Ariyar / Avaiyakaththu Anjaa Thavar
items.en: Many encountering death in face of foe will hold their ground; Who speak undaunted in the council hall are rarely found
items.en_prose: Many indeed may (fearlessly) die in the presence of (their) foes; (but) few are those who are fearless in the assembly (of the learned)

items.translit: Katraarmun Katra Selachchollith Thaamkatra / Mikkaarul Mikka Kolal
items.en: What you have learned, in penetrating words speak out before / The learn'd; but learn what men more learn'd can teach you more
items.en_prose: (Ministers) should agreeably set forth their acquirements before the learned and acquire more (knowledge) from their superiors (in learning)

items.translit: Aatrin Alavarindhu Karka Avaiyanjaa / Maatrang Kotuththar Poruttu
items.en: By rule, to dialectic art your mind apply, That in the council fearless you may make an apt reply
items.en_prose: In order to reply fearlessly before a foreign court, (ministers) should learn logic according to the rules (of grammar)

items.translit: Vaaloten Vankannar Allaarkku Nooloten / Nunnavai Anju Pavarkku
items.en: To those who lack the hero's eye what can the sword avail / Or science what, to those before the council keen who quail
items.en_prose: What have they to do with a sword who are not valiant, or they with learning who are afraid of an intelligent assembly ?

items.translit: Pakaiyakaththup Petikai Olvaal Avaiyakaththu / Anju Mavankatra Nool
items.en: As shining sword before the foe which 'sexless being' bears, Is science learned by him the council's face who fears
items.en_prose: The learning of him who is diffident before an assembly is like the shining sword of an hermaphrodite in the presence of his foes

items.translit: Pallavai Katrum Payamilare Nallavaiyul / Nanku Selachchollaa Thaar
items.en: Though many things they've learned, yet useless are they all, To man who cannot well and strongly speak in council hall
items.en_prose: Those who cannot agreeably speak good things before a good assembly are indeed unprofitable persons inspite of all their various acquirements

items.translit: Kallaa Thavarin Kataiyenpa Katrarindhum / Nallaa Ravaiyanju Vaar
items.en: Who, though they've learned, before the council of the good men quake, Than men unlearn'd a lower place must take
items.en_prose: They who, though they have learned and understood, are yet afraid of the assembly of the good, are said to be inferior (even) to the illiterate

items.translit: Ulareninum Illaarotu Oppar Kalananjik / Katra Selachchollaa Thaar
items.en: Who what they've learned, in penetrating words know not to say, The council fearing, though they live, as dead are they
items.en_prose: Those who through fear of the assembly are unable to set forth their learning in an interesting manner, though alive, are yet like the dead

items.translit: Thallaa Vilaiyulum Thakkaarum Thaazhvilaach / Chelvarum Servadhu Naatu
items.en: Where spreads fertility unfailing, where resides a band, Of virtuous men, and those of ample wealth, call that a 'land'
items.en_prose: A kingdom is that in which (those who carry on) a complete cultivation, virtuous persons, and

items.translit: Perumporulaal Pettakka Thaaki Arungettaal / Aatra Vilaivadhu Naatu
items.en: That is a 'land' which men desire for wealth's abundant share, Yielding rich increase, where calamities are rare
items.en_prose: A kingdom is that which is desire for its immense wealth, and which grows greatly in prosperity, being free from destructive causes

items.translit: Poraiyorungu Melvarungaal Thaangi Iraivarku / Iraiyorungu Nervadhu Naatu
items.en: When burthens press, it bears; Yet, With unfailing hand / To king due tribute pays: that is the 'land'
items.en_prose: A kingdom is that which can bear any burden that may be pressed on it (from adjoining kingdoms) and (yet) pay the full tribute to its sovereign

items.translit: Urupasiyum Ovaap Piniyum Serupakaiyum / Seraa Thiyalvadhu Naatu
items.en: That is a 'land' whose peaceful annals know, Nor famine fierce, nor wasting plague, nor ravage of the foe
items.en_prose: A kingdom is that which continues to be free from excessive starvation, irremediable epidemics, and destructive foes

items.translit: Palkuzhuvum Paazhseyyum Utpakaiyum Vendhalaikkum / Kolkurumpum Illadhu Naatu
items.en: From factions free, and desolating civil strife, and band / Of lurking murderers that king afflict, that is the 'land'
items.en_prose: A kingdom is that which is without various (irregular) associations, destructive internal enemies, and murderous savages who (sometimes) harass the sovereign

items.translit: Ketariyaak Ketta Itaththum Valangundraa / Naatenpa Naattin Thalai
items.en: Chief of all lands is that, where nought disturbs its peace; Or, if invaders come, still yields its rich increase
items.en_prose: The learned say that the best kingdom is that which knows no evil (from its foes), and, if injured (at all), suffers no diminution in its fruitfulness

items.translit: Irupunalum Vaaindha Malaiyum Varupunalum / Vallaranum Naattirku Uruppu
items.en: Waters from rains and springs, a mountain near, and waters thence; These make a land, with fortress' sure defence
items.en_prose: The constituents of a kingdom are the two waters (from above and below), well situated hills and an undestructible fort

items.translit: Piniyinmai Selvam Vilaivinpam Emam / Aniyenpa Naattiv Vaindhu
items.en: A country's jewels are these five: unfailing health, Fertility, and joy, a sure defence, and wealth
items.en_prose: Freedom from epidemics, wealth, produce, happiness and protection (to subjects); these five, the learned, say, are the ornaments of a kingdom

items.translit: Naatenpa Naataa Valaththana Naatalla / Naata Valandharu Naatu
items.en: That is a land that yields increase unsought, That is no land whose gifts with toil are bought
items.en_prose: The learned say that those are kingdom whose wealth is not laboured for, and those not, whose wealth is only obtained through labour

items.translit: Aangamai Veydhiyak Kannum Payamindre / Vendhamai Villaadha Naatu
items.en: Though blest with all these varied gifts' increase, A land gains nought that is not with its king at peace
items.en_prose: Although in possession of all the above mentioned excellences, these are indeed of no use to a country, in the absence of harmony between the sovereign and the sujects

items.translit: Aatru Pavarkkum Aranporul Anjiththar / Potru Pavarkkum Porul
items.en: A fort is wealth to those who act against their foes; Is wealth to them who, fearing, guard themselves from woes
items.en_prose: A fort is an object of importance to those who march (against their foes) as well as to those who through fear (of pursuers) would seek it for shelter

items.translit: Manineerum Mannum Malaiyum Aninizhar / Kaatum Utaiya Tharan
items.en: A fort is that which owns fount of waters crystal clear, An open space, a hill, and shade of beauteous forest near
items.en_prose: A fort is that which has everlasting water, plains, mountains and cool shady forests

items.translit: Uyarvakalam Thinmai Arumaiin Naankin / Amaivaran Endruraikkum Nool
items.en: Height, breadth, strength, difficult access:Science declares a fort must these possess
items.en_prose: The learned say that a fortress is an enclosure having these four (qualities) viz, height, breadth, strength and inaccessibility

items.translit: Sirukaappir Peritaththa Thaaki Urupakai / Ookkam Azhippa Tharan
items.en: A fort must need but slight defence, yet ample be, Defying all the foeman's energy
items.en_prose: A fort is that which has an extensive space within, but only small places to be guarded, and such as can destroy the courage of besieging foes

items.translit: Kolarkaridhaaik Kontakoozhth Thaaki Akaththaar / Nilaikkelidhaam Neeradhu Aran
items.en: Impregnable, containing ample stores of food, A fort for those within, must be a warlike station good
items.en_prose: A fort is that which cannot be captured, which abounds in suitable provisions, and affords a position of easy defence to its inmates

items.translit: Ellaap Porulum Utaiththaai Itaththudhavum / Nallaal Utaiyadhu Aran
items.en: A fort, with all munitions amply stored, In time of need should good reserves afford
items.en_prose: A fort is that which has all (needful) things, and excellent heroes that can help it against destruction (by foes)

items.translit: Mutriyum Mutraa Therindhum Araippatuththum / Patrar Kariyadhu Aran
items.en: A fort should be impregnable to foes who gird it round, Or aim there darts from far, or mine beneath the ground
items.en_prose: A fort is that which cannot be captured by blockading, assaulting, or undermining it

items.translit: Mutraatri Mutri Yavaraiyum Patraatrip / Patriyaar Velvadhu Aran
items.en: Howe'er the circling foe may strive access to win, A fort should give the victory to those who guard within
items.en_prose: That is a fort whose inmates are able to overcome without losing their ground, even abler men who have besieged it

items.translit: Munaimukaththu Maatralar Saaya Vinaimukaththu / Veereydhi Maanta Tharan
items.en: At outset of the strife a fort should foes dismay; And greatness gain by deeds in every glorious day
items.en_prose: A fort is that which derives excellence from the stratagems made (by its inmates) to defeat their enemies in the battlefield

items.translit: Enaimaatchith Thaakiyak Kannum Vinaimaatchi / Illaarkan Illadhu Aran
items.en: Howe'er majestic castled walls may rise, To craven souls no fortress strength supplies
items.en_prose: Although a fort may possess all (the above-said) excellence, it is, as it were without these, if its inmates possess not the excellence of action

items.translit: Porulal Lavaraip Porulaakach Cheyyum / Porulalladhu Illai Porul
items.en: Nothing exists save wealth, that can / Change man of nought to worthy man
items.en_prose: Besides wealth there is nothing that can change people of no importance into those of (some) importance

items.translit: Illaarai Ellaarum Elluvar Selvarai / Ellaarum Seyvar Sirappu
items.en: Those who have nought all will despise; All raise the wealthy to the skies
items.en_prose: All despise the poor; (but) all praise the rich

items.translit: Porulennum Poiyaa Vilakkam Irularukkum / Enniya Theyaththuch Chendru
items.en: Wealth, the lamp unfailing, speeds to every land, Dispersing darkness at its lord's command
items.en_prose: The imperishable light of wealth goes into regions desired (by its owner) and destroys the darkness (of enmity therein)

items.translit: Araneenum Inpamum Eenum Thiranarindhu / Theedhindri Vandha Porul
items.en: Their wealth, who blameless means can use aright, Is source of virtue and of choice delight
items.en_prose: The wealth acquired with a knowledge of the proper means and without foul practices will yield virtue and happiness

items.translit: Arulotum Anpotum Vaaraap Porulaakkam / Pullaar Purala Vital
items.en: Wealth gained by loss of love and grace, Let man cast off from his embrace
items.en_prose: (Kings) should rather avoid than seek the accumulation of wealth which does not flow in with mercy and love

items.translit: Uruporulum Ulku Porulumdhan Onnaarth / Theruporulum Vendhan Porul
items.en: Wealth that falls to him as heir, wealth from the kingdom's dues,
items.en_prose: The spoils of slaughtered foes; these are the royal revenues

items.translit: Arulennum Anpeen Kuzhavi Porulennum / Selvach Cheviliyaal Untu
items.en: 'Tis love that kindliness as offspring bears:And wealth as bounteous nurse the infant rears
items.en_prose: The child mercy which is borne by love grows under the care of the rich nurse of wealth

items.translit: Kundreri Yaanaip Por Kantatraal / Thankaiththondru Untaakach Cheyvaan Vinai
items.en: As one to view the strife of elephants who takes his stand, On hill he's climbed, is he who works with money in his hand
items.en_prose: An undertaking of one who has wealth in one's hands is like viewing an elephant-fight from a hill-top

items.translit: Seyka Porulaich Cherunar Serukkarukkum / Eqkadhanir Kooriya Thil
items.en: Make money! Foeman's insolence o'ergrown / To lop away no keener steel is known
items.en_prose: Accumulate wealth; it will destroy the arrogance of (your) foes; there is no weapon sharper than it

items.translit: Onporul Kaazhppa Iyatriyaarkku Enporul / Enai Irantum Orungu
items.en: Who plenteous store of glorious wealth have gained, By them the other two are easily obtained
items.en_prose: To those who have honestly acquired an abundance of riches, the other two, (virtue and pleasure) are things easy (of acquisition)

items.translit: Uruppamaindhu Ooranjaa Velpatai Vendhan / Verukkaiyul Ellaam Thalai
items.en: A conquering host, complete in all its limbs, that fears no wound, Mid treasures of the king is chiefest found
items.en_prose: The army which is complete in (its) parts and conquers without fear of wounds is the chief wealth of the king

items.translit: Ulaivitaththu Ooranjaa Vankan Tholaivitaththuth / Tholpataik Kallaal Aridhu
items.en: In adverse hour, to face undaunted might of conquering foe, Is bravery that only veteran host can show
items.en_prose: Ancient army can alone have the valour which makes it stand by its king at the time of defeat, fearless of wounds and unmindful of its reduced strength

items.translit: Oliththakkaal Ennaam Uvari Ela�ppakai / Naakam Uyirppak Ketum
items.en: Though, like the sea, the angry mice send forth their battle cry; What then? The dragon breathes upon them, and they die
items.en_prose: What if (a host of) hostile rats roar like the sea ? They will perish at the mere breath of the cobra

items.translit: Azhivindri Araipokaa Thaaki Vazhivandha / Vanka Nadhuve Patai
items.en: That is a host, by no defeats, by no desertions shamed, For old hereditary courage famed
items.en_prose: That indeed is an army which has stood firm of old without suffering destruction or deserting (to the enemy)

items.translit: Kootrutandru Melvarinum Kooti Edhirnirkum / Aatra Ladhuve Patai
items.en: That is a 'host' that joins its ranks, and mightily withstands, Though death with sudden wrath should fall upon its bands
items.en_prose: That indeed is an army which is capable of offering a united resistance, even if Yama advances against it with fury

items.translit: Maramaanam Maanta Vazhichchelavu Thetram / Enanaanke Emam Pataikku
items.en: Valour with honour, sure advance in glory's path, with confidence; To warlike host these four are sure defence
items.en_prose: Valour, honour, following in the excellent-footsteps (of its predecessors) and trust-worthiness; these four alone constitute the safeguard of an army

items.translit: Thaardhaangich Chelvadhu Thaanai Thalaivandha / Pordhaangum Thanmai Arindhu
items.en: A valiant army bears the onslaught, onward goes, Well taught with marshalled ranks to meet their coming foes
items.en_prose: That is an army which knowing the art of warding off an impending struggle, can bear against the dust-van (of a hostile force)

items.translit: Ataldhakaiyum Aatralum Illeninum Thaanai / Pataiththakaiyaal Paatu Perum
items.en: Though not in war offensive or defensive skilled; An army gains applause when well equipped and drilled
items.en_prose: Though destitute of courage to fight and strength (to endure), an army may yet gain renown by the splendour of its appearance

items.translit: Sirumaiyum Sellaath Thuniyum Varumaiyum / Illaayin Vellum Patai
items.en: Where weakness, clinging fear and poverty / Are not, the host will gain the victory
items.en_prose: An army can triumph (over its foes) if it is free from diminution; irremediable aversion and poverty

items.translit: Nilaimakkal Saala Utaiththeninum Thaanai / Thalaimakkal Ilvazhi Il
items.en: Though men abound, all ready for the war, No army is where no fit leaders are
items.en_prose: Though an army may contain a large number of permanent soldiers, it cannot last if it has no generals

items.translit: Ennaimun Nillanmin Thevvir Palarennai / Munnindru Kalnin Ravar
items.en: Ye foes stand not before my lord for many a one / Who did my lord withstand, now stands in stone
items.en_prose: O my foes, stand not before my leader; (for) many are those who did so but afterwards stood (in the shape of) statues

items.translit: Kaana Muyaleydha Ampinil Yaanai / Pizhaiththavel Endhal Inidhu
items.en: Who aims at elephant, though dart should fail, has greater praise / Than he who woodland hare with winged arrow slays
items.en_prose: It is more pleasant to hold the dart that has missed an elephant than that which has hit hare in the forest

items.translit: Peraanmai Enpa Tharukanon Rutrakkaal / Ooraanmai Matradhan Eqku
items.en: Fierceness in hour of strife heroic greatness shows; Its edge is kindness to our suffering foes
items.en_prose: The learned say that fierceness (incontest with a foe) is indeed great valour; but to become a benefactor in case of accident (to a foe) is the extreme (limit) of that valour

items.translit: Kaivel Kalitrotu Pokki Varupavan / Meyvel Pariyaa Nakum
items.en: At elephant he hurls the dart in hand; for weapon pressed, He laughs and plucks the javelin from his wounded breast
items.en_prose: The hero who after casting the lance in his hand on an elephant, comes (in search of another) will pluck the one (that sticks) in his body and laugh (exultingly)

items.translit: Vizhiththakan Velkona Teriya Azhiththimaippin / Ottandro Vanka Navarkku
items.en: To hero fearless must it not defeat appear, If he but wink his eye when foemen hurls his spear
items.en_prose: Is it not a defeat to the valiant to wink and destroy their ferocious look when a lance in cast at them (by their foe) ?

items.translit: Vizhuppun Pataadhanaal Ellaam Vazhukkinul / Vaikkumdhan Naalai Etuththu
items.en: The heroes, counting up their days, set down as vain / Each day when they no glorious wound sustain
items.en_prose: The hero will reckon among wasted days all those on which he had not received severe wounds

items.translit: Suzhalum Isaiventi Ventaa Uyiraar / Kazhalyaappuk Kaarikai Neerththu
items.en: Who seek for world-wide fame, regardless of their life, The glorious clasp adorns, sign of heroic strife
items.en_prose: The fastening of ankle-ring by those who disire a world-wide renown and not (the safety of) their lives is like adorning (themselves)

items.translit: Urinuyir Anjaa Maravar Iraivan / Serinum Seerkundral Ilar
items.en: Fearless they rush where'er 'the tide of battle rolls'; The king's reproof damps not the ardour of their eager souls
items.en_prose: The heroes who are not afraid of losing their life in a contest will not cool their ardour, even if the king prohibits (their fighting)

items.translit: Izhaiththadhu Ikavaamaich Chaavaarai Yaare / Pizhaiththadhu Orukkir Pavar
items.en: Who says they err, and visits them scorn, Who die and faithful guard the vow they've sworn
items.en_prose: Who would reproach with failure those who seal their oath with their death ?

items.translit: Purandhaarkan Neermalkach Chaakirpin Saakkaatu / Irandhukol Thakkadhu Utaiththu
items.en: If monarch's eyes o'erflow with tears for hero slain, Who would not beg such boon of glorious death to gain
items.en_prose: If (heroes) can so die as to fill with tears the eyes of their rulers, such a death deserves to be obtained even by begging

items.translit: Seyarkariya Yaavula Natpin Adhupol / Vinaikkariya Yaavula Kaappu
items.en: What so hard for men to gain as friendship true / What so sure defence 'gainst all that foe can do
items.en_prose: What so sure defence 'gainst all that foe can do?

items.translit: Niraineera Neeravar Kenmai Piraimadhip / Pinneera Pedhaiyaar Natpu
items.en: Friendship with men fulfilled of good Waxes like the crescent moon; Friendship with men of foolish mood, Like the full orb, waneth soon
items.en_prose: The friendship of the wise waxes like the new moon; (but) that of fools wanes like the full moon

items.translit: Navildhorum Noolnayam Polum Payildhorum / Panputai Yaalar Thotarpu
items.en: Learned scroll the more you ponder, Sweeter grows the mental food; So the heart by use grows fonder, Bound in friendship with the good
items.en_prose: Like learning, the friendship of the noble, the more it is cultivated, the more delightful does it become

items.translit: Nakudhar Poruttandru Nattal Mikudhikkan / Mersenaru Itiththar Poruttu
items.en: Nor for laughter only friendship all the pleasant day, But for strokes of sharp reproving, when from right you stray
items.en_prose: Friendship is to be practised not for the purpose of laughing but for that of being beforehand in giving one another sharp rebukes in case of transgression

items.translit: Punarchchi Pazhakudhal Ventaa Unarchchidhaan / Natpaang Kizhamai Tharum
items.en: Not association constant, not affection's token bind;'Tis the unison of feeling friends unites of kindred mind
items.en_prose: Living together and holding frequent intercourse are not necessary (for friendship); (mutual) understanding can alone create a claim for it

items.translit: Mukanaka Natpadhu Natpandru Nenjaththu / Akanaka Natpadhu Natpu
items.en: Not the face's smile of welcome shows the friend sincere, But the heart's rejoicing gladness when the friend is near
items.en_prose: The love that dwells (merely in the smiles of the face is not friendship; (but) that which dwells deep in the smiles of the heart is true friendship

items.translit: Azhivi Navaineekki Aaruyththu Azhivinkan / Allal Uzhappadhaam Natpu
items.en: Friendship from ruin saves, in way of virtue keeps; In troublous time, it weeps with him who weeps
items.en_prose: (True) friendship turns aside from evil (ways) makes (him) walk in the (good) way, and, in case of loss if shares his sorrow (with him)

items.translit: Utukkai Izhandhavan Kaipola Aange / Itukkan Kalaivadhaam Natpu
items.en: As hand of him whose vesture slips away, Friendship at once the coming grief will stay
items.en_prose: (True) friendship hastens to the rescue of the afflicted (as readily) as the hand of one whose garment is loosened (before an assembly)

items.translit: Natpirku Veetrirukkai Yaadhenin Kotpindri / Ollumvaai Oondrum Nilai
items.en: And where is friendship's royal seat? In stable mind, Where friend in every time of need support may find
items.en_prose: Friendship may be said to be on its throne when it possesses the power of supporting one at all times and under all circumstances, (in the practice or virtue and wealth)

items.translit: Inaiyar Ivaremakku Innamyaam Endru / Punaiyinum Pullennum Natpu
items.en: Mean is the friendship that men blazon forth,'He's thus to me' and 'such to him my worth'
items.en_prose: Though friends may praise one another saying, "He is so intimate with us, and we so much (with him)"; (still) such friendship will appear mean

items.translit: Naataadhu Nattalir Ketillai Nattapin / Veetillai Natpaal Pavarkku
items.en: To make an untried man your friend is ruin sure; For friendship formed unbroken must endure
items.en_prose: As those who are of a friendly nature will not forsake (a friend) after once loving (him), there is no evil so great as contracting a friendship without due inquiry

items.translit: Aaindhaaindhu Kollaadhaan Kenmai Kataimurai / Thaansaam Thuyaram Tharum
items.en: Alliance with the man you have not proved and proved again, In length of days will give you mortal pain
items.en_prose: The friendship contracted by him who has not made repeated inquiry will in the end grieve (him) to death

items.translit: Kunamum Kutimaiyum Kutramum Kundraa / Inanum Arindhiyaakka Natpu
items.en: Temper, descent, defects, associations free / From blame: know these, then let the man be friend to thee
items.en_prose: Make friendship (with one) after ascertaining (his) character, birth, defects and the whole of one's relations

items.translit: Kutippirandhu Thankan Pazhinaanu Vaanaik / Kotuththum Kolalventum Natpu
items.en: Who, born of noble race, from guilt would shrink with shame, Pay any price so you as friend that man may claim
items.en_prose: The friendship of one who belongs to a (good) family and is afraid of (being charged with) guilt, is worth even purchasing

items.translit: Azhachcholli Alladhu Itiththu Vazhakkariya / Vallaarnatapu Aaindhu Kolal
items.en: Make them your chosen friend whose words repentance move, With power prescription's path to show, while evil they reprove
items.en_prose: You should examine and secure the friendship of those who can speak so as to make you weep over a crime (before its commission) or rebuke you severely (after you have done it) and are able to teach

items.translit: Kettinum Untor Urudhi Kilaignarai / Neetti Alappadhor Kol
items.en: Ruin itself one blessing lends:'Tis staff that measures out one's friends
items.en_prose: Even in ruin there is some good; (for) it is a rod by which one may measure fully (the affection of one's) relations

items.translit: Oodhiyam Enpadhu Oruvarkup Pedhaiyaar / Kenmai Oreei Vital
items.en: 'Tis gain to any man, the sages say, Friendship of fools to put away
items.en_prose: It is indead a gain for one to renounce the friendship of fools

items.translit: Ullarka Ullam Sirukuva Kollarka / Allarkan Aatraruppaar Natpu
items.en: Think not the thoughts that dwarf the soul; nor take / For friends the men who friends in time of grief forsake
items.en_prose: Do not think of things that discourage your mind, nor contract friendship with those who would forsake you in adversity

items.translit: Ketungaalaik Kaivituvaar Kenmai Atungaalai / Ullinum Ullanj Chutum
items.en: Of friends deserting us on ruin's brink,'Tis torture e'en in life's last hour to think
items.en_prose: The very thought of the friendship of those who have deserted one at the approach of adversity will burn one's mind at the time of death

items.translit: Maruvuka Maasatraar Kenmaion Reeththum / Oruvuka Oppilaar Natpu
items.en: Cling to the friendship of the spotless one's; whate'er you pay / Renounce alliance with the men of evil way
items.en_prose: Continue to enjoy the friendship of the pure; (but) renounce even with a gift, the friendship of those who do not agree (with the world)

items.translit: Pazhaimai Enappatuvadhu Yaadhenin Yaadhum / Kizhamaiyaik Keezhndhitaa Natpu
items.en: Familiarity is friendship's silent pact, That puts restraint on no familiar act
items.en_prose: Imtimate friendship is that which cannot in the least be injured by (things done through the) right (of longstanding intimacy)

items.translit: Natpir Kuruppuk Kezhudhakaimai Matradharku / Uppaadhal Saandror Katan
items.en: Familiar freedom friendship's very frame supplies; To be its savour sweet is duty of the wise
items.en_prose: The constituents of friendship are (things done through) the right of intimacy; to be pleased with such a right is the duty of the wise

items.translit: Pazhakiya Natpevan Seyyung Kezhudhakaimai / Seydhaangu Amaiyaak Katai
items.en: When to familiar acts men kind response refuse, What fruit from ancient friendship's use
items.en_prose: Of what avail is long-standing friendship, if friends do not admit as their own actions done through the right of intimacy ?

items.translit: Vizhaidhakaiyaan Venti Iruppar Kezhudhakaiyaar / Kelaadhu Nattaar Seyin
items.en: When friends unbidden do familiar acts with loving heart, Friends take the kindly deed in friendly part
items.en_prose: If friends, through the right of friendship, do (anything) without being asked, the wise will be pleased with them on account of its desirability

items.translit: Pedhaimai Ondro Perungizhamai Endrunarka / Nodhakka Nattaar Seyin
items.en: Not folly merely, but familiar carelessness, Esteem it, when your friends cause you distress
items.en_prose: If friends should perform what is painful, understand that it is owing not only to ignorance, but also to the strong claims of intimacy

items.translit: Ellaikkan Nindraar Thuravaar Tholaivitaththum / Thollaikkan Nindraar Thotarpu
items.en: Who stand within the bounds quit not, though loss impends, Association with the old familiar friends
items.en_prose: Those who stand within the limits (of true friendship) will not even in adversity give up the intimacy of long-standing friends

items.translit: Azhivandha Seyyinum Anparaar Anpin / Vazhivandha Kenmai Yavar
items.en: True friends, well versed in loving ways, Cease not to love, when friend their love betrays
items.en_prose: Those who have (long) stood in the path of affection will not give it up even if their friends cause (them) their ruin

items.translit: Kelizhukkam Kelaak Kezhudhakaimai Vallaarkku / Naalizhukkam Nattaar Seyin
items.en: In strength of friendship rare of friend's disgrace who will not hear, The day his friend offends will day of grace to him appear
items.en_prose: To those who understand that by which they should not listen to (tales about) the faults of their friends, that is a (profitable) day on which the latter may commit a fault

items.translit: Ketaaa Vazhivandha Kenmaiyaar Kenmai / Vitaaar Vizhaiyum Ulaku
items.en: Friendship of old and faithful friends, Who ne'er forsake, the world commends
items.en_prose: They will be loved by the world, who have not forsaken the friendship of those with whom they have kept up an unbroken long-standing intimacy

items.translit: Vizhaiyaar Vizhaiyap Patupa Pazhaiyaarkan / Panpin Thalaippiriyaa Thaar
items.en: Ill-wishers even wish them well, who guard / For ancient friends, their wonted kind regard
items.en_prose: Even enemies will love those who have never changed in their affection to their long-standingfriends

items.translit: Parukuvaar Polinum Panpilaar Kenmai / Perukalir Kundral Inidhu
items.en: Though evil men should all-absorbing friendship show, Their love had better die away than grow
items.en_prose: The decrease of friendship with those who look as if they would eat you up (through excess of love) while they are really destitute of goodness is far better than its increase

items.translit: Urinnattu Arinoruum Oppilaar Kenmai / Perinum Izhappinum En?
items.en: What though you gain or lose friendship of men of alien heart, Who when you thrive are friends, and when you fail depart
items.en_prose: Of what avail is it to get or lose the friendship of those who love when there is gain and leave when there is none ?

items.translit: Uruvadhu Seerdhookkum Natpum Peruvadhu / Kolvaarum Kalvarum Ner
items.en: These are alike: the friends who ponder friendship's gain / Those who accept whate'er you give, and all the plundering train
items.en_prose: Friendship who calculate the profits (of their friendship), prostitutes who are bent on obtaining their gains, and thieves are (all) of the same character

items.translit: Amarakaththu Aatrarukkum Kallaamaa Annaar / Thamarin Thanimai Thalai
items.en: A steed untrained will leave you in the tug of war; Than friends like that to dwell alone is better far
items.en_prose: Solitude is more to be desired than the society of those who resemble the untrained horses which throw down (their riders) in the fields of battle

items.translit: Seydhemanj Chaaraach Chiriyavar Punkenmai / Eydhalin Eydhaamai Nandru
items.en: 'Tis better not to gain than gain the friendship profitless / Of men of little minds, who succour fails when dangers press
items.en_prose: It is far better to avoid that to contract the evil friendship of the base who cannot protect (their friends) even when appointed to do so

items.translit: Pedhai Perungezheei Natpin Arivutaiyaar / Edhinmai Koti Urum
items.en: Better ten million times incur the wise man's hate, Than form with foolish men a friendship intimate
items.en_prose: The hatred of the wise is ten-million times more profitable than the excessive intimacy of the fool

items.translit: Nakaivakaiya Raakiya Natpin Pakaivaraal / Paththatuththa Koti Urum
items.en: From foes ten million fold a greater good you gain, Than friendship yields that's formed with laughers vain
items.en_prose: What comes from enemies is a hundred million times more profitable than what comes from the friendship of those who cause only laughter

items.translit: Ollum Karumam Utatru Pavarkenmai / Sollaataar Sora Vital
items.en: Those men who make a grievous toil of what they do / On your behalf, their friendship silently eschew
items.en_prose: Gradually abandon without revealing (beforehand) the friendship of those who pretend inability to carry out what they (really) could do

items.translit: Kanavinum Innaadhu Manno Vinaiveru / Solveru Pattaar Thotarpu
items.en: E'en in a dream the intercourse is bitterness / With men whose deeds are other than their words profess
items.en_prose: The friendship of those whose actions do not agree with their words will distress (one) even in (one's) dreams

items.translit: Enaiththum Kurukudhal Ompal Manaikkezheei / Mandril Pazhippaar Thotarpu
items.en: In anywise maintain not intercourse with those, Who in the house are friends, in hall are slandering foes
items.en_prose: Avoid even the least approach to a contraction of friendship with those who would love you in private but ridicule you in public

items.translit: Seeritam Kaanin Eridharkup Pattatai / Neraa Nirandhavar Natpu
items.en: Anvil where thou shalt smitten be, when men occasion find, Is friendship's form without consenting mind
items.en_prose: The friendship of those who behave like friends without inward affection is a weapon that may be thrown when a favourable opportunity presents itself

items.translit: Inampondru Inamallaar Kenmai Makalir / Manampola Veru Patum
items.en: Friendship of those who seem our kin, but are not really kind / Will change from hour to hour like woman's mind
items.en_prose: The friendship of those who seem to be friends while they are not, will change like the love of women

items.translit: Palanalla Katrak Kataiththu Mananallar / Aakudhal Maanaark Karidhu
items.en: To heartfelt goodness men ignoble hardly may attain, Although abundant stores of goodly lore they gain
items.en_prose: Though (one's) enemies may have mastered many good books, it will be impossible for them to become truly loving at heart

items.translit: Mukaththin Iniya Nakaaa Akaththinnaa / Vanjarai Anjap Patum
items.en: 'Tis fitting you should dread dissemblers' guile, Whose hearts are bitter while their faces smile
items.en_prose: One should fear the deceitful who smile sweetly with their face but never love with their heart

items.translit: Manaththin Amaiyaa Thavarai Enaiththondrum / Sollinaal Therarpaatru Andru
items.en: When minds are not in unison, 'its never; just, In any words men speak to put your trust
items.en_prose: In nothing whatever is it proper to rely on the words of those who do not love with their heart

items.translit: Nattaarpol Nallavai Sollinum Ottaarsol / Ollai Unarap Patum
items.en: Though many goodly words they speak in friendly tone, The words of foes will speedily be known
items.en_prose: Though (one's) foes may utter good things as though they were friends, once will at once understand (their evil, import)

items.translit: Solvanakkam Onnaarkan Kollarka Vilvanakkam / Theengu Kuriththamai Yaan
items.en: To pliant speech from hostile lips give thou no ear;'Tis pliant bow that show the deadly peril near
items.en_prose: Since the bending of the bow bespeaks evil, one should not accept (as good) the humiliating speeches of one's foes

items.translit: Thozhudhakai Yullum Pataiyotungum Onnaar / Azhudhakan Neerum Anaiththu
items.en: In hands that worship weapon ten hidden lies; Such are the tears that fall from foeman's eyes
items.en_prose: A weapon may be hid in the very hands with which (one's) foes adore (him) (and) the tears they shed are of the same nature

items.translit: Mikachcheydhu Thammellu Vaarai Nakachcheydhu / Natpinul Saappullar Paatru
items.en: 'Tis just, when men make much of you, and then despise, To make them smile, and slap in friendship's guise
items.en_prose: It is the duty of kings to affect great love but make it die (inwardly); as regard those foes who shew them great friendship but despise them (in their heart)

items.translit: Pakainatpaam Kaalam Varungaal Mukanattu / Akanatpu Oreei Vital
items.en: When time shall come that foes as friends appear, Then thou, to hide a hostile heart, a smiling face may'st wear
items.en_prose: When one's foes begin to affect friendship, one should love them with one's looks, and, cherishing no love in the heart, give up (even the former)

items.translit: Pedhaimai Enpadhondru Yaadhenin Edhangontu / Oodhiyam Poka Vital
items.en: What one thing merits folly's special name.Letting gain go, loss for one's own to claim
items.en_prose: Folly is one (of the chief defects); it is that which (makes one) incur loss and forego gain

items.translit: Pedhaimaiyul Ellaam Pedhaimai Kaadhanmai / Kaiyalla Thankat Seyal
items.en: 'Mid follies chiefest folly is to fix your love / On deeds which to your station unbefitting prove
items.en_prose: The greatest folly is that which leads one to take delight in doing what is forbidden

items.translit: Naanaamai Naataamai Naarinmai Yaadhondrum / Penaamai Pedhai Thozhil
items.en: Ashamed of nothing, searching nothing out, of loveless heart, Nought cherishing, 'tis thus the fool will play his part
items.en_prose: Shamelessness indifference (to what must be sought after), harshness, and aversion for everything (that ought to be desired) are the qualities of the fool

items.translit: Odhi Unarndhum Pirarkkuraiththum Thaanatangaap / Pedhaiyin Pedhaiyaar Il
items.en: The sacred law he reads and learns, to other men expounds,-Himself obeys not; where can greater fool be found
items.en_prose: There are no greater fools than he who, though he has read and understood (a great deal) and even taught it to others, does not walk according to his own teaching

items.translit: Orumaich Cheyalaatrum Pedhai Ezhumaiyum / Thaanpuk Kazhundhum Alaru
items.en: The fool will merit hell in one brief life on earth, In which he entering sinks through sevenfold round of birth
items.en_prose: A fool can procure in a single birth a hell into which he may enter and suffer through all the seven births

items.translit: Poipatum Ondro Punaipoonum Kaiyariyaap / Pedhai Vinaimer Kolin
items.en: When fool some task attempts with uninstructed pains, It fails; nor that alone, himself he binds with chains
items.en_prose: If the fool, who knows not how to act undertakes a work, he will (certainly) fail (But) is it all ? He will even adorn himself with fetters

items.translit: Edhilaar Aarath Thamarpasippar Pedhai / Perunjelvam Utrak Katai
items.en: When fools are blessed with fortune's bounteous store, Their foes feed full, their friends are prey to hunger sore
items.en_prose: If a fool happens to get an immense fortune, his neighbours will enjoy it while his relations starve

items.translit: Maiyal Oruvan Kaliththatraal Pedhaidhan / Kaiyondru Utaimai Perin
items.en: When folly's hand grasps wealth's increase, 'twill be / As when a mad man raves in drunken glee
items.en_prose: A fool happening to possess something is like the intoxication of one who is (already) giddy

items.translit: Peridhinidhu Pedhaiyaar Kenmai Pirivinkan / Peezhai Tharuvadhon Ril
items.en: Friendship of fools is very pleasant thing, Parting with them will leave behind no sting
items.en_prose: The friendship between fools is exceedingly delightful (to each other): for at parting there will be

items.translit: Kazhaaakkaal Palliyul Vaiththatraal Saandror / Kuzhaaaththup Pedhai Pukal
items.en: Like him who seeks his couch with unwashed feet, Is fool whose foot intrudes where wise men meet
items.en_prose: The appearance of a fool in an assembly of the learned is like placing (one's) unwashed feet on a bed

items.translit: Arivinmai Inmaiyul Inmai Piridhinmai / Inmaiyaa Vaiyaa Thulaku
items.en: Want of knowledge, 'mid all wants the sorest want we deem; Want of other things the world will not as want esteem
items.en_prose: The want of wisdom is the greatest of all wants; but that of wealth the world will not regard as such

items.translit: Arivilaan Nenjuvandhu Eedhal Piridhiyaadhum / Illai Peruvaan Thavam
items.en: The gift of foolish man, with willing heart bestowed, is nought, But blessing by receiver's penance bought
items.en_prose: (The cause of) a fool cheerfully giving (something) is nothing else but the receiver's merit (in a former birth)

items.translit: Arivilaar Thaandhammaip Peezhikkum Peezhai / Seruvaarkkum Seydhal Aridhu
items.en: With keener anguish foolish men their own hearts wring, Than aught that even malice of their foes can bring
items.en_prose: The suffering that fools inflict upon themselves is hardly possible even to foes

items.translit: Venmai Enappatuva Thiyaadhenin Onmai / Utaiyamyaam Ennum Serukku
items.en: What is stupidity? The arrogance that cries,'Behold, we claim the glory of the wise.'
items.en_prose: What is called want of wisdom is the vanity which says, "We are wise"

items.translit: Kallaadha Merkon Tozhukal Kasatara / Valladhooum Aiyam Tharum
items.en: If men what they have never learned assume to know, Upon their real learning's power a doubt 'twill throw
items.en_prose: Fools pretending to know what has not been read (by them) will rouse suspicion even as to what they have thoroughly mastered

items.translit: Atram Maraiththalo Pullarivu Thamvayin / Kutram Maraiyaa Vazhi
items.en: Fools are they who their nakedness conceal, And yet their faults unveiled reveal
items.en_prose: Even to cover one's nakedness would be folly, if (one's) faults were not covered (by forsaking them)

items.translit: Arumarai Sorum Arivilaan Seyyum / Perumirai Thaane Thanakku
items.en: From out his soul who lets the mystic teachings die, Entails upon himself abiding misery
items.en_prose: The fool who neglects precious counsel does, of his own accord, a great injury to himself

items.translit: Evavum Seykalaan Thaandheraan Avvuyir / Poom Alavumor Noi
items.en: Advised, he heeds not; of himself knows nothing wise; This man's whole life is all one plague until he dies
items.en_prose: The fool will not perform (his duties) even when advised nor ascertain them himself; such a soul is a

items.translit: Kaanaadhaan Kaattuvaan Thaankaanaan Kaanaadhaan / Kantaanaam Thaankanta Vaaru
items.en: That man is blind to eyes that will not see who knowledge shows;-The blind man still in his blind fashion knows
items.en_prose: One who would teach a fool will (simply) betray his folly; and the fool would (still) think himself "wise in his own conceit"

items.translit: Ulakaththaar Untenpadhu Illenpaan Vaiyaththu / Alakaiyaa Vaikkap Patum
items.en: Who what the world affirms as false proclaim, O'er all the earth receive a demon's name
items.en_prose: He who denies the existence of what the world believes in will be regarded as a demon on earth

items.translit: Ikalenpa Ellaa Uyirkkum Pakalennum / Panpinmai Paarikkum Noi
items.en: Hostility disunion's plague will bring, That evil quality, to every living thing
items.en_prose: The disease which fosters the evil of disunion among all creatures is termed hatred by the wise

items.translit: Pakalkarudhip Patraa Seyinum Ikalkarudhi / Innaasey Yaamai Thalai
items.en: Though men disunion plan, and do thee much despite'Tis best no enmity to plan, nor evil deeds requite
items.en_prose: Though disagreeable things may be done from (a feeling of) disunion, it is far better that nothing painful be done from (that of) hatred

items.translit: Ikalennum Evvanoi Neekkin Thavalillaath / Thaavil Vilakkam Tharum
items.en: If enmity, that grievous plague, you shun, Endless undying praises shall be won
items.en_prose: To rid one-self of the distressing dtsease of hatred will bestow (on one) a never-decreasing imperishable fame

items.translit: Inpaththul Inpam Payakkum Ikalennum / Thunpaththul Thunpang Ketin
items.en: Joy of joys abundant grows, When malice dies that woe of woes
items.en_prose: If hatred which is the greatest misery is destroyed, it will yield the greatest delight

items.translit: Ikaledhir Saaindhozhuka Vallaarai Yaare / Mikalookkum Thanmai Yavar
items.en: If men from enmity can keep their spirits free, Who over them shall gain the victory
items.en_prose: Who indeed would think of conquering those who naturally shrink back from hatred ?

items.translit: Ikalin Mikalinidhu Enpavan Vaazhkkai / Thavalum Ketalum Naniththu
items.en: The life of those who cherished enmity hold dear, To grievous fault and utter death is near
items.en_prose: Failure and ruin are not far from him who says it is sweet to excel in hatred

items.translit: Mikalmeval Meypporul Kaanaar Ikalmeval / Innaa Arivi Navar
items.en: The very truth that greatness gives their eyes can never see, Who only know to work men woe, fulfilled of enmity
items.en_prose: Who only know to work men woe, fulfilled of enmity

items.translit: Ikalirku Edhirsaaidhal Aakkam Adhanai / Mikalookkin Ookkumaam Ketu
items.en: 'Tis gain to turn the soul from enmity; Ruin reigns where this hath mastery
items.en_prose: Shrinking back from hatred will yield wealth; indulging in its increase will hasten ruin

items.translit: Ikalkaanaan Aakkam Varungaal Adhanai / Mikalkaanum Ketu Thararku
items.en: Men think not hostile thought in fortune's favouring hour, They cherish enmity when in misfortune's power
items.en_prose: At the approach of wealth one will not think of hatred (but) to secure one's ruin, one will look to its increase

items.translit: Ikalaanaam Innaadha Ellaam Nakalaanaam / Nannayam Ennum Serukku
items.en: From enmity do all afflictive evils flow; But friendliness doth wealth of kindly good bestow
items.en_prose: All calamities are caused by hatred; but by the delight (of friendship) is caused the great wealth of good virtues

items.translit: Valiyaarkku Maaretral Ompuka Ompaa / Meliyaarmel Meka Pakai
items.en: With stronger than thyself, turn from the strife away; With weaker shun not, rather court the fray
items.en_prose: Avoid offering resistance to the strong; (but) never fail to cherish enmity towards the weak

items.translit: Anpilan Aandra Thunaiyilan Thaandhuvvaan / Enpariyum Edhilaan Thuppu
items.en: No kinsman's love, no strength of friends has he; How can he bear his foeman's enmity
items.en_prose: How can he who is unloving, destitute of powerful aids, and himself without strength overcome the might of his foe ?

items.translit: Anjum Ariyaan Amaivilan Eekalaan / Thanjam Eliyan Pakaikku
items.en: A craven thing! knows nought, accords with none, gives nought away; To wrath of any foe he falls an easy prey
items.en_prose: In the estimation of foes miserably weak is he, who is timid, ignorant, unsociable and niggardly

items.translit: Neengaan Vekuli Niraiyilan Egngnaandrum / Yaanganum Yaarkkum Elidhu
items.en: His wrath still blazes, every secret told; each day / This man's in every place to every foe an easy prey
items.en_prose: He who neither refrains from anger nor keeps his secrets will at all times and in all places be easily conquered by all

items.translit: Vazhinokkaan Vaaippana Seyyaan Pazhinokkaan / Panpilan Patraarkku Inidhu
items.en: No way of right he scans, no precepts bind, no crimes affright, No grace of good he owns; such man's his foes' delight
items.en_prose: (A) pleasing (object) to his foes is he who reads not moral works, does nothing that is enjoined by them cares not for reproach and is not possessed of good qualities

items.translit: Kaanaach Chinaththaan Kazhiperung Kaamaththaan / Penaamai Penap Patum
items.en: Blind in his rage, his lustful passions rage and swell; If such a man mislikes you, like it well
items.en_prose: Highly to be desired is the hatred of him whose anger is blind, and whose lust increases beyond measure

items.translit: Kotuththum Kolalventum Mandra Atuththirundhu / Maanaadha Seyvaan Pakai
items.en: Unseemly are his deeds, yet proffering aid, the man draws nigh:His hate- 'tis cheap at any price- be sure to buy
items.en_prose: It is indeed necessary to obtain even by purchase the hatred of him who having begun (a work) does what is not conductive (to its accomplishment)

items.translit: Kunanilanaaik Kutram Palavaayin Maatraarkku / Inanilanaam Emaap Putaiththu
items.en: No gracious gifts he owns, faults many cloud his fame; His foes rejoice, for none with kindred claim
items.en_prose: He will become friendless who is without (any good) qualities and whose faults are many; (such a character) is a help to (his) foes

items.translit: Seruvaarkkuch Chenikavaa Inpam Arivilaa / Anjum Pakaivarp Perin
items.en: The joy of victory is never far removed from those / Who've luck to meet with ignorant and timid foes
items.en_prose: There will be no end of lofty delights to the victorious, if their foes are (both) ignorant and timid

items.translit: Kallaan Vekulum Siruporul Egngnaandrum / Ollaanai Ollaa Tholi
items.en: The task of angry war with men unlearned in virtue's lore / Who will not meet, glory shall meet him never more
items.en_prose: The light (of fame) will never be gained by him who gains not the trifling reputation of having fought an unlearned (foe)

items.translit: Pakaiennum Panpi Ladhanai Oruvan / Nakaiyeyum Ventarpaatru Andru
items.en: For Hate, that ill-conditioned thing not e'en in jest / Let any evil longing rule your breast
items.en_prose: The evil of hatred is not of a nature to be desired by one even in sport

items.translit: Viller Uzhavar Pakaikolinum Kollarka / Soller Uzhavar Pakai
items.en: Although you hate incur of those whose ploughs are bows, Make not the men whose ploughs are words your foes
items.en_prose: Though you may incur the hatred of warriors whose ploughs are bows, incur not that of ministers whose ploughs are words

items.translit: Emur Ravarinum Ezhai Thamiyanaaip / Pallaar Pakaikol Pavan
items.en: Than men of mind diseased, a wretch more utterly forlorn, Is he who stands alone, object of many foeman's scorn
items.en_prose: He who being alone, incurs the hatred of many is more infatuated than even mad men

items.translit: Pakainatpaak Kontozhukum Panputai Yaalan / Thakaimaikkan Thangitru Ulaku
items.en: The world secure on his dexterity depends, Whose worthy rule can change his foes to friends
items.en_prose: Whose worthy rule can change his foes to friends

items.translit: Thandhunai Indraal Pakaiyirantaal Thaanoruvan / Indhunaiyaak Kolkavatrin Ondru
items.en: Without ally, who fights with twofold enemy o'ermatched, Must render one of these a friend attached
items.en_prose: He who is alone and helpless while his foes are two should secure one of them as an agreeable help (to himself)

items.translit: Thera�num Theraa Vitinum Azhivinkan / Theraan Pakaaan Vital
items.en: Whether you trust or not, in time of sore distress, Questions of diff'rence or agreement cease to press
items.en_prose: Though (one's foe is) aware or not of one's misfortune one should act so as neither to join nor separate (from him)

items.translit: Novarka Nondhadhu Ariyaarkku Mevarka / Menmai Pakaivar Akaththu
items.en: To those who know them not, complain not of your woes; Nor to your foeman's eyes infirmities disclose
items.en_prose: Relate not your suffering even to friends who are ignorant of it, nor refer to your weakness in the presence of your foes

items.translit: Vakaiyarindhu Tharseydhu Tharkaappa Maayum / Pakaivarkan Patta Serukku
items.en: Know thou the way, then do thy part, thyself defend; Thus shall the pride of those that hate thee have an end
items.en_prose: The joy of one's foes will be destroyed if one guards oneself by knowing the way (of acting) and securing assistance

items.translit: Ilaidhaaka Mulmaram Kolka Kalaiyunar / Kaikollum Kaazhththa Itaththu
items.en: Destroy the thorn, while tender point can work thee no offence; Matured by time, 'twill pierce the hand that plucks it thence
items.en_prose: A thorny tree should be felled while young, (for) when it is grown it will destroy the hand of the feller

items.translit: Uyirppa Ularallar Mandra Seyirppavar / Semmal Sidhaikkalaa Thaar
items.en: But breathe upon them, and they surely die, Who fail to tame the pride of angry enemy
items.en_prose: Those who do not destroy the pride of those who hate (them) will certainly not exist even to breathe

items.translit: Nizhalneerum Innaadha Innaa Thamarneerum / Innaavaam Innaa Seyin
items.en: Water and shade, if they unwholesome prove, will bring you pain / And qualities of friends who treacherous act, will be your bane
items.en_prose: Shade and water are not pleasant, (if) they cause disease; so are the qualities of (one's) relations not agreeable, (if) they cause pain

items.translit: Vaalpola Pakaivarai Anjarka Anjuka / Kelpol Pakaivar Thotarpu
items.en: Dread not the foes that as drawn swords appear; Friendship of foes, who seem like kinsmen, fear
items.en_prose: Fear not foes (who say they would cut) like a sword; (but) fear the friendship of foes (who seemingly

items.translit: Utpakai Anjiththar Kaakka Ulaivitaththu / Matpakaiyin Maanath Therum
items.en: Of hidden hate beware, and guard thy life; In troublous time 'twill deeper wound than potter's knife
items.en_prose: Fear internal enmity and guard yourself; (if not) it will destroy (you) in an evil hour, as surely as the tool which cuts the potter's clay

items.translit: Manamaanaa Utpakai Thondrin Inamaanaa / Edham Palavum Tharum
items.en: If secret enmities arise that minds pervert, Then even kin unkind will work thee grievous hurt
items.en_prose: The secret enmity of a person whose mind in unreformed will lead to many evils causing disaffection among (one's) relations

items.translit: Uralmuraiyaan Utpakai Thondrin Iralmuraiyaan / Edham Palavum Tharum
items.en: Amid one's relatives if hidden hath arise,'Twill hurt inflict in deadly wise
items.en_prose: If there appears internal hatred in a (king's) family; it will lead to many a fatal crime

items.translit: Ondraamai Ondriyaar Katpatin Egngnaandrum / Pondraamai Ondral Aridhu
items.en: If discord finds a place midst those who dwelt at one before,'Tis ever hard to keep destruction from the door
items.en_prose: If hatred arises among (one's) own people, it will be hardly possible (for one) to escape death

items.translit: Seppin Punarchchipol Kootinum Kootaadhe / Utpakai Utra Kuti
items.en: As casket with its cover, though in one they live alway, No union to the house where hate concealed hath sway
items.en_prose: Never indeed will a family subject to internal hatred unite (really) though it may present an apparent union like that of a casket and its lid

items.translit: Aramporudha Ponpolath Theyum Uramporudhu / Utpakai Utra Kuti
items.en: As gold with which the file contends is worn away, So strength of house declines where hate concealed hath sway
items.en_prose: A family subject to internal hatred will wear out and lose its strength like iron that has been filed away

items.translit: Etpaka Vanna Sirumaiththe Aayinum / Utpakai Ulladhaang Ketu
items.en: Though slight as shred of 'seasame' seed it be, Destruction lurks in hidden enmity
items.en_prose: Although internal hatred be as small as the fragment of the sesamum (seed), still does destruction dwell in it

items.translit: Utampaatu Ilaadhavar Vaazhkkai Kutangarul / Paampotu Utanurain Thatru
items.en: Domestic life with those who don't agree, Is dwelling in a shed with snake for company
items.en_prose: Living with those who do not agree (with one) is like dwelling with a cobra (in the same) hut

items.translit: Aatruvaar Aatral Ikazhaamai Potruvaar / Potralul Ellaam Thalai
items.en: The chiefest care of those who guard themselves from ill, Is not to slight the powers of those who work their mighty will
items.en_prose: Not to disregard the power of those who can carry out (their wishes) is more important than all the watchfulness of those who guard (themselves against evil)

items.translit: Periyaaraip Penaadhu Ozhukir Periyaaraal / Peraa Itumpai Tharum
items.en: If men will lead their lives reckless of great men's will, Such life, through great men's powers, will bring perpetual ill
items.en_prose: To behave without respect for the great (rulers) will make them do (us) irremediable evils

items.translit: Ketalventin Kelaadhu Seyka Atalventin / Aatru Pavarkan Izhukku
items.en: Who ruin covet let them shut their ears, and do despite / To those who, where they list to ruin have the might
items.en_prose: If a person desires ruin, let him not listen to the righteous dictates of law, but commit crimes against those who are able to slay (other sovereigns)

items.translit: Kootraththaik Kaiyaal Viliththatraal Aatruvaarkku / Aatraadhaar Innaa Seyal
items.en: When powerless man 'gainst men of power will evil deeds essay, Tis beck'ning with the hand for Death to seize them for its prey
items.en_prose: The weak doing evil to the strong is like beckoning Yama to come (and destroy them)

items.translit: Yaantuch Chendru Yaantum Ularaakaar / Vendhuppin Vendhu Serappat Tavar
items.en: Who dare the fiery wrath of monarchs dread, Where'er they flee, are numbered with the dead
items.en_prose: Those who have incurred the wrath of a cruel and mighty potentate will not prosper wherever they may go

items.translit: Eriyaal Sutappatinum Uyvuntaam Uyyaar / Periyaarp Pizhaiththozhuku Vaar
items.en: Though in the conflagration caught, he may escape from thence:He 'scapes not who in life to great ones gives offence
items.en_prose: Though burnt by a fire (from a forest), one may perhaps live; (but) never will he live who has shown disrespect to the great (devotees)

items.translit: Vakaimaanta Vaazhkkaiyum Vaanporulum Ennaam / Thakaimaanta Thakkaar Serin
items.en: Though every royal gift, and stores of wealth your life should crown, What are they, if the worthy men of mighty virtue frown
items.en_prose: If a king incurs the wrath of the righteous great, what will become of his government with its splendid auxiliaries and (all) its untold wealth ?

items.translit: Kundrannaar Kundra Madhippin Kutiyotu / Nindrannaar Maaivar Nilaththu
items.en: If they, whose virtues like a mountain rise, are light esteemed; They die from earth who, with their households, ever-during seemed
items.en_prose: If (the) hill-like (devotees) resolve on destruction, those who seemed to be everlasting will be destroyed root and branch from the earth

items.translit: Endhiya Kolkaiyaar Seerin Itaimurindhu / Vendhanum Vendhu Ketum
items.en: When blazes forth the wrath of men of lofty fame, Kings even fall from high estate and perish in the flame
items.en_prose: Kings even fall from high estate and perish in the flame

items.translit: Irandhamaindha Saarputaiyar Aayinum Uyyaar / Sirandhamaindha Seeraar Serin
items.en: Though all-surpassing wealth of aid the boast, If men in glorious virtue great are wrath, they're lost
items.en_prose: Though in possession of numerous auxiliaries, they will perish who are-exposed to the wrath of the noble whose penance is boundless

items.translit: Manaivizhaivaar Maanpayan Eydhaar Vinaivizhaiyaar / Ventaap Porulum Adhu
items.en: Who give their soul to love of wife acquire not nobler gain; Who give their soul to strenuous deeds such meaner joys disdain
items.en_prose: Those who lust after their wives will not attain the excellence of virtue; and it is just this that is not desired by those who are bent on acquiring wealth

items.translit: Penaadhu Penvizhaivaan Aakkam Periyadhor / Naanaaka Naanuth Tharum
items.en: Who gives himself to love of wife, careless of noble name / His wealth will clothe him with o'erwhelming shame
items.en_prose: The wealth of him who, regardless (of his manliness), devotes himself to his wife's feminine nature will cause great shame (to ali men) and to himself;

items.translit: Illaalkan Thaazhndha Iyalpinmai Egngnaandrum / Nallaarul Naanuth Tharum
items.en: Who to his wife submits, his strange, unmanly mood / Will daily bring him shame among the good
items.en_prose: The frailty that stoops to a wife will always make (her husband) feel ashamed among the good

items.translit: Manaiyaalai Anjum Marumaiyi Laalan / Vinaiyaanmai Veereydha Lindru
items.en: No glory crowns e'en manly actions wrought / By him who dreads his wife, nor gives the other world a thought
items.en_prose: The undertaking of one, who fears his wife and is therefore destitute of (bliss), will never be applauded

items.translit: Illaalai Anjuvaan Anjumar Regngnaandrum / Nallaarkku Nalla Seyal
items.en: Who quakes before his wife will ever tremble too, Good deeds to men of good deserts to do
items.en_prose: He that fears his wife will always be afraid of doing good deeds (even) to the good

items.translit: Imaiyaarin Vaazhinum Paatilare Illaal / Amaiyaardhol Anju Pavar
items.en: Though, like the demi-gods, in bliss they dwell secure from harm, Those have no dignity who fear the housewife's slender arm
items.en_prose: They that fear the bamboo-like shoulders of their wives will be destitute of manliness though they may flourish like the Gods

items.translit: Penneval Seydhozhukum Aanmaiyin Naanutaip / Penne Perumai Utaiththu
items.en: The dignity of modest womanhood excels / His manliness, obedient to a woman's law who dwells
items.en_prose: Even shame faced womanhood is more to be esteemed than the shameless manhood that performs

items.translit: Nattaar Kuraimutiyaar Nandraatraar Nannudhalaal / Pettaangu Ozhuku Pavar
items.en: Who to the will of her with beauteous brow their lives conform, Aid not their friends in need, nor acts of charity perform
items.en_prose: Those who yield to the wishes of their wives will neither relieve the wants of (their) friends nor perform virtuous deeds

items.translit: Aravinaiyum Aandra Porulum Piravinaiyum / Peneval Seyvaarkan Il
items.en: No virtuous deed, no seemly wealth, no pleasure, rests / With them who live obedient to their wives' behests
items.en_prose: From those who obey the commands of their wives are to be expected neither deeds of virtue, nor those of wealth nor (even) those of pleasure

items.translit: Enserndha Nenjath Thitanutaiyaarkku Egngnaandrum / Penserndhaam Pedhaimai Il
items.en: Where pleasures of the mind, that dwell in realms of thought, abound, Folly, that springs from overweening woman's love, is never found
items.en_prose: The foolishness that results from devotion to a wife will never be found in those who possess a reflecting mind and a prosperity (flowing) therefrom

items.translit: Anpin Vizhaiyaar Porulvizhaiyum Aaidhotiyaar / Insol Izhukkuth Tharum
items.en: Those that choice armlets wear who seek not thee with love, But seek thy wealth, their pleasant words will ruin prove
items.en_prose: The sweet words of elegant braceleted (prostitutes) who desire (a man) not from affection but from avarice, will cause sorrow

items.translit: Payandhookkip Panpuraikkum Panpin Makalir / Nayandhookki Nallaa Vital
items.en: Who weigh the gain, and utter virtuous words with vicious heart, Weighing such women's worth, from their society depart
items.en_prose: One must ascertain the character of the ill-natured women who after ascertaining the wealth (of a man) speak (as if they were) good natured-ones, and avoid intercourse (with them)

items.translit: Porutpentir Poimmai Muyakkam Iruttaraiyil / Edhil Pinandhazheei Atru
items.en: As one in darkened room, some stranger corpse inarms, Is he who seeks delight in mercenary women's charms
items.en_prose: The false embraces of wealth-loving women are like (hired men) embracing a strange corpse in a dark room

items.translit: Porutporulaar Punnalan Thoyaar Arutporul / Aayum Arivi Navar
items.en: Their worthless charms, whose only weal is wealth of gain, From touch of these the wise, who seek the wealth of grace, abstain
items.en_prose: The wise who seek the wealth of grace will not desire the base favours of those who regard wealth (and not pleasure) as (their) riches

items.translit: Podhunalaththaar Punnalam Thoyaar Madhinalaththin / Maanta Arivi Navar
items.en: From contact with their worthless charms, whose charms to all are free, The men with sense of good and lofty wisdom blest will flee;
items.en_prose: Those whose knowledge is made excellent by their (natural) sense will not covet the trffling delights

items.translit: Thannalam Paarippaar Thoyaar Thakaiserukkip / Punnalam Paarippaar Thol
items.en: From touch of those who worthless charms, with wanton arts, display, The men who would their own true good maintain will turn away
items.en_prose: Those who would spread (the fame of) their own goodness will not desire the shoulders of those, who rejoice in their accomplishments and bestow their despicable favours (on all who pay)

items.translit: Nirainenjam Illavar Thoivaar Piranenjir / Penip Punarpavar Thol
items.en: Who cherish alien thoughts while folding in their feigned embrace, These none approach save those devoid of virtue's grace
items.en_prose: Those who are destitute of a perfectly (reformed) mind will covet the shoulders of those who embrace (them) while their hearts covet other things

items.translit: Aayum Arivinar Allaarkku Anangenpa / Maaya Makalir Muyakku
items.en: As demoness who lures to ruin woman's treacherous love / To men devoid of wisdom's searching power will prove
items.en_prose: The wise say that to such as are destitute of discerning sense the embraces of faithless women are (as ruinous as those of) the celestail female

items.translit: Varaivilaa Maanizhaiyaar Mendhol Puraiyilaap / Pooriyarkal Aazhum Alaru
items.en: The wanton's tender arm, with gleaming jewels decked, Is hell, where sink degraded souls of men abject
items.en_prose: The delicate shoulders of prostitutes with excellent jewels are a hell into which are plunged the ignorant base

items.translit: Irumanap Pentirum Kallum Kavarum / Thiruneekkap Pattaar Thotarpu
items.en: Women of double minds, strong drink, and dice; to these giv'n o'er, Are those on whom the light of Fortune shines no more
items.en_prose: Treacherous women, liquor, and gambling are the associates of such as have forsaken by Fortune

items.translit: Utkap Pataaar Oliyizhappar Egngnaandrum / Katkaadhal Kontozhuku Vaar
items.en: Who love the palm's intoxicating juice, each day, No rev'rence they command, their glory fades away
items.en_prose: Those who always thirst after drink will neither inspire fear (in others) nor retain the light (of their fame)

items.translit: Unnarka Kallai Unilunka Saandroraan / Ennap Pataventaa Thaar
items.en: Drink not inebriating draught Let him count well the cost / Who drinks, by drinking, all good men's esteem is lost
items.en_prose: Let no liquor be drunk; if it is desired, let it be drunk by those who care not for esteem of the great

items.translit: Eendraal Mukaththeyum Innaadhaal Enmatruch / Chaandror Mukaththuk Kali
items.en: The drunkard's joy is sorrow to his mother's eyes; What must it be in presence of the truly wise
items.en_prose: Intoxication is painful even in the presence of (one's) mother; what will it not then be in that of the wise ?

items.translit: Naanennum Nallaal Purangotukkum Kallennum / Penaap Perungutrath Thaarkku
items.en: Shame, goodly maid, will turn her back for aye on them / Who sin the drunkard's grievous sin, that all condemn
items.en_prose: The fair maid of modesty will turn her back on those who are guilty of the great and abominable crime of drunkenness

items.translit: Kaiyari Yaamai Utaiththe Porulkotuththu / Meyyari Yaamai Kolal
items.en: With gift of goods who self-oblivion buys, Is ignorant of all that man should prize
items.en_prose: To give money and purchase unconsciousness is the result of one's ignorance of (one's own actions)

items.translit: Thunjinaar Seththaarin Verallar Egngnaandrum / Nanjunpaar Kallun Pavar
items.en: Sleepers are as the dead, no otherwise they seem; Who drink intoxicating draughts, they poison quaff, we deem
items.en_prose: They that sleep resemble the deed; (likewise) they that drink are no other than poison-eaters

items.translit: Ullotri Ulloor Nakappatuvar Egngnaandrum / Kallotrik Kansaai Pavar
items.en: Who turn aside to drink, and droop their heavy eye, Shall be their townsmen's jest, when they the fault espy
items.en_prose: Those who always intoxicate themselves by a private (indulgence in) drink; will have their secrets detected and laughed at by their fellow-townsmen

items.translit: Kaliththariyen Enpadhu Kaivituka Nenjaththu / Oliththadhooum Aange Mikum
items.en: No more in secret drink, and then deny thy hidden fraud; What in thy mind lies hid shall soon be known abroad
items.en_prose: Let (the drunkard) give up saying "I have never drunk"; (for) the moment (he drinks) he will simply betray his former attempt to conceal

items.translit: Kaliththaanaik Kaaranam Kaattudhal Keezhneerk / Kuliththaanaith Theeththureei Atru
items.en: Like him who, lamp in hand, would seek one sunk beneath the wave / Is he who strives to sober drunken man with reasonings grave
items.en_prose: Reasoning with a drunkard is like going under water with a torch in search of a drowned man

items.translit: Kallunnaap Pozhdhir Kaliththaanaik Kaanungaal / Ullaankol Untadhan Sorvu
items.en: When one, in sober interval, a drunken man espies, Does he not think, 'Such is my folly in my revelries'
items.en_prose: When (a drunkard) who is sober sees one who is not, it looks as if he remembered not the evil effects of his (own) drink

items.translit: Ventarka Vendritinum Soodhinai Vendradhooum / Thoontirpon Meenvizhungi Atru
items.en: Seek not the gamester's play; though you should win, Your gain is as the baited hook the fish takes in
items.en_prose: Though able to win, let not one desire gambling; (for) even what is won is like a fish swallowing the iron in fish-hook

items.translit: Ondreydhi Noorizhakkum Soodharkkum Untaangol / Nandreydhi Vaazhvadhor Aaru
items.en: Is there for gamblers, too, that gaining one a hundred lose, some way / That they may good obtain, and see a prosperous day
items.en_prose: That they may good obtain, and see a prosperous day? Is there indeed a means of livelihood that can bestow happiness on gamblers who gain one and lose a hundred?

items.translit: Urulaayam Ovaadhu Koorin Porulaayam / Pooip Purame Patum
items.en: If prince unceasing speak of nought but play, Treasure and revenue will pass from him away
items.en_prose: If the king is incessantly addicted to the rolling dice in the hope of gain, his wealth and the resources thereof will take their departure and fall into other's hands

items.translit: Sirumai Palaseydhu Seerazhikkum Soodhin / Varumai Tharuvadhondru Il
items.en: Gaming brings many woes, and ruins fair renown; Nothing to want brings men so surely down
items.en_prose: There is nothing else that brings (us) poverty like gambling which causes many a misery and destroys (one's) reputation

items.translit: Kavarum Kazhakamum Kaiyum Tharukki / Ivariyaar Illaaki Yaar
items.en: The dice, and gaming-hall, and gamester's art, they eager sought, Thirsting for gain- the men in other days who came to nought
items.en_prose: Penniless are those who by reason of their attachment would never forsake gambling, the gamblingplace and the handling (of dice)

items.translit: Akataaraar Allal Uzhapparsoo Thennum / Mukatiyaan Mootappat Taar
items.en: Gambling's Misfortune's other name: o'er whom she casts her veil, They suffer grievous want, and sorrows sore bewail
items.en_prose: Those who are swallowed by the goddess called "gambling" will never have their hunger satisfied, but suffer the pangs of hell in the next world

items.translit: Pazhakiya Selvamum Panpum Ketukkum / Kazhakaththuk Kaalai Pukin
items.en: Ancestral wealth and noble fame to ruin haste, If men in gambler's halls their precious moments waste
items.en_prose: To waste time at the place of gambling will destroy inherited wealth and goodness of character

items.translit: Porul Ketuththup Poimer Koleei / Arulketuththu Allal Uzhappikkum Soodhu
items.en: Gambling wastes wealth, to falsehood bends the soul: it drives away / All grace, and leaves the man to utter misery a prey
items.en_prose: Gambling destroys property, teaches falsehood, puts an end to benevolence, and brings in misery (here and hereafter)

items.translit: Utaiselvam Oonoli Kalviendru Aindhum / Ataiyaavaam Aayang Kolin
items.en: Clothes, wealth, food, praise, and learning, all depart / From him on gambler's gain who sets his heart
items.en_prose: The habit of gambling prevents the attainment of these five: clothing, wealth, food, fame and learning

items.translit: Izhaththoru�um Kaadhalikkum Soodhepol Thunpam / Uzhaththoru�um Kaadhatru Uyir
items.en: Howe'er he lose, the gambler's heart is ever in the play; E'en so the soul, despite its griefs, would live on earth alway
items.en_prose: As the gambler loves (his vice) the more he loses by it, so does the soul love (the body) the more it suffers through it

items.translit: Mikinum Kuraiyinum Noiseyyum Noolor / Valimudhalaa Enniya Moondru
items.en: The learned books count three, with wind as first; of these, As any one prevail, or fail; 'twill cause disease
items.en_prose: If (food and work are either) excessive or deficient, the three things enumerated by (medical) writers, flatulence, biliousness, and phlegm, will cause (one) disease

items.translit: Marundhena Ventaavaam Yaakkaikku Arundhiyadhu / Atradhu Potri Unin
items.en: No need of medicine to heal your body's pain, If, what you ate before digested well, you eat again
items.en_prose: No medicine is necessary for him who eats after assuring (himself) that what he has (already) eaten has been digested

items.translit: Atraal Aravarindhu Unka Aqdhutampu / Petraan Netidhuykkum Aaru
items.en: Who has a body gained may long the gift retain, If, food digested well, in measure due he eat again
items.en_prose: If (one's food has been) digested let one eat with moderation; (for) that is the way to prolong the life of an embodied soul

items.translit: Atradhu Arindhu Kataippitiththu Maaralla / Thuykka Thuvarap Pasiththu
items.en: Knowing the food digested well, when hunger prompteth thee, With constant care, the viands choose that well agree
items.en_prose: (First) assure yourself that your food has been digested and never fail to eat, when very hungry, whatever is not disagreeable (to you)

items.translit: Maarupaatu Illaadha Unti Maruththunnin / Oorupaatu Illai Uyirkku
items.en: With self-denial take the well-selected meal; So shall thy frame no sudden sickness feel
items.en_prose: There will be no disaster to one's life if one eats with moderation, food that is not disagreeable

items.translit: Izhivarindhu Unpaankan Inpampol Nirkum / Kazhiper Iraiyaankan Noi
items.en: On modest temperance as pleasures pure, So pain attends the greedy epicure
items.en_prose: As pleasure dwells with him who eats moderately, so disease (dwells) with the glutton who eats voraciously

items.translit: Theeyala Vandrith Theriyaan Peridhunnin / Noyala Vindrip Patum
items.en: Who largely feeds, nor measure of the fire within maintains, That thoughtless man shall feel unmeasured pains
items.en_prose: He will be afflicted with numberless diseases, who eats immoderately, ignorant (of the rules of health)

items.translit: Noinaati Noimudhal Naati Adhudhanikkum / Vaainaati Vaaippach Cheyal
items.en: Disease, its cause, what may abate the ill:Let leech examine these, then use his skill
items.en_prose: Let the physician enquire into the (nature of the) disease, its cause and its method of cure and treat it faithfully according to (medical rule)

items.translit: Utraan Alavum Piniyalavum Kaalamum / Katraan Karudhich Cheyal
items.en: The habitudes of patient and disease, the crises of the ill / These must the learned leech think over well, then use his skill
items.en_prose: The learned (physician) should ascertain the condition of his patient; the nature of his disease, and the season (of the year) and (then) proceed (with his treatment)

items.translit: Utravan Theerppaan Marundhuzhaich Chelvaanendru / Appaal Naar Kootre Marundhu
items.en: For patient, leech, and remedies, and him who waits by patient's side, The art of medicine must fourfold code of laws provide
items.en_prose: Medical science consists of four parts, viz, patient, physician, medicine and compounder; and each of these (again) contains four sub-divisions

items.translit: Irpirandhaar Kanalladhu Illai Iyalpaakach / Cheppamum Naanum Orungu
items.en: Save in the scions of a noble house, you never find / Instinctive sense of right and virtuous shame combined
items.en_prose: Consistency (of thought, word and deed) and fear (of sin) are conjointly natural only to the high-born

items.translit: Ozhukkamum Vaaimaiyum Naanum Im / Moondrum Izhukkaar Kutippiran Thaar
items.en: In these three things the men of noble birth fail not:In virtuous deed and truthful word, and chastened thought
items.en_prose: The high-born will never deviate from these three; good manners, truthfulness and modesty

items.translit: Nakaieekai Insol Ikazhaamai Naankum / Vakaiyenpa Vaaimaik Kutikku
items.en: The smile, the gift, the pleasant word, unfailing courtesy / These are the signs, they say, of true nobility
items.en_prose: A cheerful countenance, liberality, pleasant words, and an unreviling disposition, these four are said to be the proper qualities of the truly high-born

items.translit: Atukkiya Koti Perinum Kutippirandhaar / Kundruva Seydhal Ilar
items.en: Millions on millions piled would never win / The men of noble race to soul-degrading sin
items.en_prose: Though blessed with immense wealth, the noble will never do anything unbecoming

items.translit: Vazhanguva Thulveezhndhak Kannum Pazhanguti / Panpil Thalaippiridhal Indru
items.en: Though stores for charity should fail within, the ancient race / Will never lose its old ancestral grace
items.en_prose: Though their means fall off, those born in ancient families, will not lose their character (for liberality)

items.translit: Salampatrich Chaalpila Seyyaarmaa Satra / Kulampatri Vaazhdhum En Paar
items.en: Whose minds are set to live as fits their sire's unspotted fame, Stooping to low deceit, commit no deeds that gender shame
items.en_prose: Those who seek to preserve the irreproachable honour of their families will not viciously do what is detrimental thereto

items.translit: Kutippirandhaar Kanvilangum Kutram Visumpin / Madhikkan Maruppol Uyarndhu
items.en: The faults of men of noble race are seen by every eye, As spots on her bright orb that walks sublime the evening sky
items.en_prose: As spots on her bright orb that walks sublime the evening sky

items.translit: Nalaththinkan Naarinmai Thondrin Avanaik / Kulaththinkan Aiyap Patum
