items.en: Set not; so may'st thou prosper, moon! that eyes may see / My love who went away, but ever bides with me
items.en_prose: May you live, O Moon! Do not set, that I mine see him who has departed without quitting my soul

items.translit: Kaadhalar Thoodhotu Vandha Kanavinukku / Yaadhusey Venkol Virundhu
items.en: It came and brought to me, that nightly vision rare, A message from my love,- what feast shall I prepare
items.en_prose: Where with shall I feast the dream which has brought me my dear one's messenger ?

items.translit: Kayalunkan Yaanirappath Thunjir Kalandhaarkku / Uyalunmai Saatruven Man
items.en: If my dark, carp-like eye will close in sleep, as I implore, The tale of my long-suffering life I'll tell my loved one o'er
items.en_prose: If my fish-like painted eyes should, at my begging, close in sleep, I could fully relate my sufferings to my lord

items.translit: Nanavinaal Nalkaa Thavaraik Kanavinaal / Kaantalin Unten Uyir
items.en: Him, who in waking hour no kindness shows, In dreams I see; and so my lifetime goes
items.en_prose: My life lasts because in my dream I behold him who does not favour me in my waking hours

items.translit: Kanavinaan Untaakum Kaamam Nanavinaan / Nalkaarai Naatith Thararku
items.en: Some pleasure I enjoy when him who loves not me / In waking hours, the vision searches out and makes me see
items.en_prose: There is pleasure in my dream, because in it I seek and obtain him who does not visit me in my wakefulness

items.translit: Nanavinaal Kantadhooum Aange Kanavundhaan / Kanta Pozhudhe Inidhu
items.en: As what I then beheld in waking hour was sweet, So pleasant dreams in hour of sleep my spirit greet
items.en_prose: I saw him in my waking hours, and then it was pleasant; I see him just now in my dream, and it is (equally) pleasant

items.translit: Nanavena Ondrillai Aayin Kanavinaal / Kaadhalar Neengalar Man
items.en: And if there were no waking hour, my love / In dreams would never from my side remove
items.en_prose: Were there no such thing as wakefulness, my beloved (who visited me) in my dream would not depart from me

items.translit: Nanavinaal Nalkaak Kotiyaar Kanavanaal / Enemmaip Peezhip Padhu
items.en: The cruel one, in waking hour, who all ungracious seems, Why should he thus torment my soul in nightly dreams
items.en_prose: The cruel one who would not favour me in my wakefulness, what right has he to torture me in my dreams?

items.translit: Thunjungaal Tholmelar Aaki Vizhikkungaal / Nenjaththar Aavar Viraindhu
items.en: And when I sleep he holds my form embraced; And when I wake to fill my heart makes haste
items.en_prose: When I am asleep he rests on my shoulders, (but) when I awake he hastens into my soul

items.translit: Nanavinaal Nalkaarai Novar Kanavinaal / Kaadhalark Kaanaa Thavar
items.en: In dreams who ne'er their lover's form perceive, For those in waking hours who show no love will grieve
items.en_prose: They who have no dear ones to behold in their dreams blame him who visits me not in my waking hours

items.translit: Nanavinaal Namneeththaar Enpar Kanavinaal / Kaanaarkol Ivvoo Ravar
items.en: They say, that he in waking hours has left me lone; In dreams they surely see him not,- these people of the town;
items.en_prose: The women of this place say he has forsaken me in my wakefulness I think they have not seen him visit me in my dreams

items.translit: Maalaiyo Allai Manandhaar Uyirunnum / Velainee Vaazhi Pozhudhu
items.en: Thou art not evening, but a spear that doth devour / The souls of brides; farewell, thou evening hour
items.en_prose: Live, O you evening are you (the former) evening? No, you are the season that slays (married) women

items.translit: Punkannai Vaazhi Marulmaalai Emkelpol / Vankanna Thonin Thunai
items.en: Thine eye is sad; Hail, doubtful hour of eventide!Of cruel eye, as is my spouse, is too thy bride
items.en_prose: A long life to you, O dark evening! You are sightless Is your help-mate (also) as hard-hearted as mine

items.translit: Paniarumpip Paidhalkol Maalai Thuniarumpith / Thunpam Valara Varum
items.en: With buds of chilly dew wan evening's shade enclose; My anguish buds space and all my sorrow grows
items.en_prose: The evening that (once) came in with trembling and dimness (now) brings me an aversion for life and increasing sorrow

items.translit: Kaadhalar Ilvazhi Maalai Kolaikkalaththu / Edhilar Pola Varum
items.en: When absent is my love, the evening hour descends, As when an alien host to field of battle wends
items.en_prose: In the absence of my lover, evening comes in like slayers on the field of slaughter

items.translit: Kaalaikkuch Cheydhanandru Enkol Evankolyaan / Maalaikkuch Cheydha Pakai?
items.en: O morn, how have I won thy grace? thou bring'st relief / O eve, why art thou foe! thou dost renew my grief
items.en_prose: O eve, why art thou foe! thou dost renew my grief

items.translit: Maalainoi Seydhal Manandhaar Akalaadha / Kaalai Arindha Thilen
items.en: The pangs that evening brings I never knew, Till he, my wedded spouse, from me withdrew
items.en_prose: Previous to my husband's departure, I know not the painful nature of evening

items.translit: Kaalai Arumpip Pakalellaam Podhaaki / Maalai Malarumin Noi
items.en: My grief at morn a bud, all day an opening flower, Full-blown expands in evening hour
items.en_prose: This malady buds forth in the morning, expands all day long and blossoms in the evening

items.translit: Azhalpolum Maalaikkuth Thoodhaaki Aayan / Kuzhalpolum Kollum Patai
items.en: The shepherd's pipe is like a murderous weapon, to my ear, For it proclaims the hour of ev'ning's fiery anguish near
items.en_prose: The shepherd's flute now sounds as a fiery forerunner of night, and is become a weapon that slays (me)

items.translit: Padhimaruntu Paidhal Uzhakkum Madhimaruntu / Maalai Patardharum Pozhdhu
items.en: If evening's shades, that darken all my soul, extend; From this afflicted town will would of grief ascend
items.en_prose: When night comes on confusing (everyone's) mind, the (whole) town will lose its sense and be plunged in sorrow

items.translit: Porulmaalai Yaalarai Ulli Marulmaalai / Maayumen Maayaa Uyir
items.en: This darkening eve, my darkling soul must perish utterly; Remembering him who seeks for wealth, but seeks not me
items.en_prose: My (hitherto) unextinguished life is now lost in this bewildering night at the thought of him who has the nature of wealth

items.translit: Sirumai Namakkozhiyach Chetchendraar Ulli / Narumalar Naanina Kan
items.en: Thine eyes grown dim are now ashamed the fragrant flow'rs to see, Thinking on him, who wand'ring far, leaves us in misery
items.en_prose: While we endure the unbearable sorrow, your eyes weep for him who is gone afar, and shun (the sight of) fragrant flowers

items.translit: Nayandhavar Nalkaamai Solluva Polum / Pasandhu Panivaarum Kan
items.en: The eye, with sorrow wan, all wet with dew of tears, As witness of the lover's lack of love appears
items.en_prose: The discoloured eyes that shed tears profusely seem to betray the unkindness of our beloved

items.translit: Thanandhamai Saala Arivippa Polum / Manandhanaal Veengiya Thol
items.en: These withered arms, desertion's pangs abundantly display, That swelled with joy on that glad nuptial day
items.en_prose: The shoulders that swelled on the day of our union (now) seem to announce our separation clearly (to the public)

items.translit: Panaineengip Paindhoti Sorum Thunaineengith / Tholkavin Vaatiya Thol
items.en: When lover went, then faded all their wonted charms, And armlets' golden round slips off from these poor wasted arms
items.en_prose: In the absence of your consort, your shoulders having lost their former beauty and fulness, your bracelets of pure gold have become loose

items.translit: Kotiyaar Kotumai Uraikkum Thotiyotu / Tholkavin Vaatiya Thol
items.en: These wasted arms, the bracelet with their wonted beauty gone, The cruelty declare of that most cruel one
items.en_prose: The (loosened) bracelets, and the shoulders from which the old beauty has faded, relate the cruelty of the pitiless one

items.translit: Thotiyotu Tholnekizha Noval Avaraik / Kotiyar Enakkooral Nondhu
items.en: I grieve, 'tis pain to me to hear him cruel chid, Because the armlet from my wasted arm has slid
items.en_prose: I am greatly pained to hear you call him a cruel man, just because your shoulders are reduced and your bracelets loosened

items.translit: Paatu Perudhiyo Nenje Kotiyaarkken / Vaatudhot Poosal Uraiththu
items.en: My heart! say ought of glory wilt thou gain, If to that cruel one thou of thy wasted arms complain
items.en_prose: Can you O my soul! gain glory by relating to the (so-called) cruel one the clamour of my fading shoulders?

items.translit: Muyangiya Kaikalai Ookkap Pasandhadhu / Paindhotip Pedhai Nudhal
items.en: One day the fervent pressure of embracing arms I checked, Grew wan the forehead of the maid with golden armlet decked
items.en_prose: When I once loosened the arms that were in embrace, the forehead of the gold-braceleted women turned sallow

items.translit: Muyakkitaith Thanvali Pozhap Pasapputra / Pedhai Perumazhaik Kan
items.en: As we embraced a breath of wind found entrance there; The maid's large liquid eyes were dimmed with care
items.en_prose: When but a breath of breeze penetrated our embrace, her large cool eyes became sallow

items.translit: Kannin Pasappo Paruvaral Eydhindre / Onnudhal Seydhadhu Kantu
items.en: The dimness of her eye felt sorrow now, Beholding what was done by that bright brow
items.en_prose: Was it at the sight of what the bright forehead had done that the sallowness of her eyes became sad?

items.translit: Ninaiththondru Sollaayo Nenje Enaiththondrum / Evvanoi Theerkkum Marundhu
items.en: My heart, canst thou not thinking of some med'cine tell, Not any one, to drive away this grief incurable
items.en_prose: O my soul, will you not think and tell me some medicine be it what it may, that can cure this incurable malady?

items.translit: Kaadhal Avarilar Aakanee Novadhu / Pedhaimai Vaazhiyen Nenju
items.en: Since he loves not, thy smart / Is folly, fare thee well my heart
items.en_prose: Is folly, fare thee well my heart!

items.translit: Irundhulli Enparidhal Nenje Parindhullal / Paidhalnoi Seydhaarkan Il
items.en: What comes of sitting here in pining thought, O heart? He knows / No pitying thought, the cause of all these wasting woes
items.en_prose: O my soul! why remain (here) and suffer thinking (of him)? There are no lewd thoughts (of you) in him who has caused you this disease of sorrow

items.translit: Kannum Kolachcheri Nenje Ivaiyennaith / Thinnum Avarkkaanal Utru
items.en: O rid me of these eyes, my heart; for they, Longing to see him, wear my life away
items.en_prose: O my soul! take my eyes also with you, (if not), these would eat me up (in their desire) to see him

items.translit: Setraar Enakkai Vitalunto Nenjeyaam / Utraal Uraaa Thavar
items.en: O heart, as a foe, can I abandon utterly / Him who, though I long for him, longs not for me
items.en_prose: O my soul! can he who loves not though he is beloved, be forsaken saying he hates me (now)?

items.translit: Kalandhunarththum Kaadhalark Kantaar Pulandhunaraai / Poikkaaivu Kaaidhien Nenju
items.en: My heart, false is the fire that burns; thou canst not wrath maintain, If thou thy love behold, embracing, soothing all thy pain
items.en_prose: O my soul! when you see the dear one who remove dislike by intercourse, you are displeased and continue to be so Nay, your displeasure is (simply) false

items.translit: Kaamam Vituondro Naanvitu Nannenje / Yaano Poreniv Virantu
items.en: Or bid thy love, or bid thy shame depart; For me, I cannot bear them both, my worthy heart
items.en_prose: O my good soul, give up either lust or honour, as for me I can endure neither

items.translit: Parindhavar Nalkaarendru Engip Pirindhavar / Pinselvaai Pedhaien Nenju
items.en: Thou art befooled, my heart, thou followest him who flees from thee; And still thou yearning criest: 'He will nor pity show nor love to me.'
items.en_prose: You are a fool, O my soul! to go after my departed one, while you mourn that he is not kind enough to favour you

items.translit: Ullaththaar Kaadha Lavaraal Ullinee / Yaaruzhaich Cheriyen Nenju
items.en: My heart! my lover lives within my mind; Roaming, whom dost thou think to find
items.en_prose: O my soul! to whom would you repair, while the dear one is within yourself?

items.translit: Thunnaath Thurandhaarai Nenjaththu Utaiyemaa / Innum Izhaththum Kavin
items.en: If I should keep in mind the man who utterly renounces me, My soul must suffer further loss of dignity
items.en_prose: If I retain in my heart him who has left me without befriending me, I shall lose even the (inward) beauty that remains

items.translit: Kaamak Kanichchi Utaikkum Niraiyennum / Naanuththaazh Veezhththa Kadhavu
items.en: Of womanly reserve love's axe breaks through the door, Barred by the bolt of shame before
items.en_prose: The axe of lust can break the door of chastity which is bolted with the bolt of modesty

items.translit: Kaamam Enavondro Kannindren Nenjaththai / Yaamaththum Aalum Thozhil
items.en: What men call love is the one thing of merciless power; It gives my soul no rest, e'en in the midnight hour
items.en_prose: Even at midnight is my mind worried by lust, and this one thing, alas! is without mercy

items.translit: Maraippenman Kaamaththai Yaano Kurippindrith / Thummalpol Thondri Vitum
items.en: I would my love conceal, but like a sneeze / It shows itself, and gives no warning sign
items.en_prose: I would conceal my lust, but alas, it yields not to my will but breaks out like a sneeze

items.translit: Niraiyutaiyen Enpenman Yaanoen Kaamam / Maraiyirandhu Mandru Patum
items.en: In womanly reserve I deemed myself beyond assail; But love will come abroad, and casts away the veil
items.en_prose: I say I would be firm, but alas, my malady breaks out from its concealment and appears in public

items.translit: Setraarpin Sellaap Perundhakaimai Kaamanoi / Utraar Arivadhondru Andru
items.en: The dignity that seeks not him who acts as foe, Is the one thing that loving heart can never know
items.en_prose: The dignity that would not go after an absent lover is not known to those who are sticken by love

items.translit: Setravar Pinseral Venti Aliththaro / Etrennai Utra Thuyar
items.en: My grief how full of grace, I pray you see!It seeks to follow him that hateth me
items.en_prose: The sorrow I have endured by desiring to go after my absent lover, in what way is it excellent?

items.translit: Naanena Ondro Ariyalam Kaamaththaal / Peniyaar Petpa Seyin
items.en: No sense of shame my gladdened mind shall prove, When he returns my longing heart to bless with love
items.en_prose: I know nothing like shame when my beloved does from love (just) what is desired (by me)

items.translit: Panmaayak Kalvan Panimozhi Andronam / Penmai Utaikkum Patai
items.en: The words of that deceiver, versed in every wily art, Are instruments that break through every guard of woman's heart
items.en_prose: Are not the enticing words of my trick-abounding roguish lover the weapon that breaks away my feminine firmness?

items.translit: Pulappal Enachchendren Pullinen Nenjam / Kalaththal Uruvadhu Kantu
items.en: 'I 'll shun his greeting'; saying thus with pride away I went:I held him in my arms, for straight I felt my heart relent
items.en_prose: I said I would feign dislike and so went (away); (but) I embraced him the moment I say my mind began to unite with him!

items.translit: Ninandheeyil Ittanna Nenjinaarkku Unto / Punarndhooti Nirpem Enal
items.en: 'We 'll stand aloof and then embrace': is this for them to say, Whose hearts are as the fat that in the blaze dissolves away
items.en_prose: Is it possible for those whose hearts melt like fat in the fire to say they can feign a strong dislike and remain so?

items.translit: Vaalatrup Purkendra Kannum Avarsendra / Naalotrith Theyndha Viral
items.en: My eyes have lost their brightness, sight is dimmed; my fingers worn, With nothing on the wall the days since I was left forlorn
items.en_prose: My finger has worn away by marking (on the wall) the days he has been absent while my eyes have lost their lustre and begin to fail

items.translit: Ilangizhaai Indru Marappinen Tholmel / Kalangazhiyum Kaarikai Neeththu
items.en: O thou with gleaming jewels decked, could I forget for this one day, Henceforth these bracelets from my arms will slip, my beauty worn away
items.en_prose: O you bright-jewelled maid, if I forget (him) today, my shoulders will lose their beauty even in the other life and make my bracelets loose

items.translit: Urannasaii Ullam Thunaiyaakach Chendraar / Varalnasaii Innum Ulen
items.en: On victory intent, His mind sole company he went; And I yet life sustain And long to see his face again
items.en_prose: I still live by longing for the arrival of him who has gone out of love for victory and with valour as his guide

items.translit: Kootiya Kaamam Pirindhaar Varavullik / Kotuko Terumen Nenju
items.en: 'He comes again, who left my side, and I shall taste love's joy,'-My heart with rapture swells, when thoughts like these my mind employ
items.en_prose: My heart is rid of its sorrow and swells with rapture to think of my absent lover returning with his love

items.translit: Kaankaman Konkanaik Kannaarak Kantapin / Neengumen Mendhol Pasappu
items.en: O let me see my spouse again and sate these longing eyes!That instant from my wasted frame all pallor flies
items.en_prose: May I look on my lover till I am satisfied and thereafter will vanish the sallowness of my slender shoulders

items.translit: Varukaman Konkan Orunaal Parukuvan / Paidhalnoi Ellaam Keta
items.en: O let my spouse but come again to me one day!I'll drink that nectar: wasting grief shall flee away
items.en_prose: May my husband return some day; and then will I enjoy (him) so as to destroy all this agonizing sorrow

items.translit: Pulappenkol Pulluven Kollo Kalappenkol / Kananna Kelir Viran
items.en: Shall I draw back, or yield myself, or shall both mingled be, When he returns, my spouse, dear as these eyes to me
items.en_prose: On the return of him who is as dear as my eyes, am I displeased or am I to embrace (him); or am I to do both?

items.translit: Vinaikalandhu Vendreeka Vendhan Manaikalandhu / Maalai Ayarkam Virundhu
items.en: O would my king would fight, o'ercome, devide the spoil; At home, to-night, the banquet spread should crown the toil
items.en_prose: Let the king fight and gain (victories); (but) let me be united to my wife and feast the evening

items.translit: Orunaal Ezhunaalpol Sellumsen Sendraar / Varunaalvaiththu Engu Pavarkku
items.en: One day will seem like seven to those who watch and yearn / For that glad day when wanderers from afar return
items.en_prose: To those who suffer waiting for the day of return of their distant lovers one day is as long as seven days

items.translit: Perinennaam Petrakkaal Ennaam Urinennaam / Ullam Utaindhukkak Kaal
items.en: What's my return, the meeting hour, the wished-for greeting worth, If she heart-broken lie, with all her life poured forth
items.en_prose: After (my wife) has died of a broken heart, what good will there be if she is to receive me, has received me, or has even embraced me?

items.translit: Karappinung Kaiyikan Thollaanin Unkan / Uraikkal Uruvadhon Runtu
items.en: Thou hid'st it, yet thine eye, disdaining all restraint, Something, I know not, what, would utter of complaint
items.en_prose: Though you would conceal (your feelings), your painted eyes would not, for, transgressing (their bounds), they tell (me) something

items.translit: Kanniraindha Kaarikaik Kaamperdhot Pedhaikkup / Penniraindha Neermai Peridhu
items.en: The simple one whose beauty fills mine eye, whose shoulders curve / Like bambu stem, hath all a woman's modest sweet reserve
items.en_prose: Unusually great is the female simplicity of your maid whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders resemble the bamboo

items.translit: Maniyil Thikazhdharu Noolpol Matandhai / Aniyil Thikazhvadhondru Untu
items.en: As through the crystal beads is seen the thread on which they 're strung / So in her beauty gleams some thought cannot find a tongue
items.en_prose: There is something that is implied in the beauty of this woman, like the thread that is visible in a garland of gems

items.translit: Mukaimokkul Ulladhu Naatrampol Pedhai / Nakaimokkul Ulladhon Runtu
items.en: As fragrance in the opening bud, some secret lies / Concealed in budding smile of this dear damsel's eyes
items.en_prose: There is something in the unmatured smile of this maid like the fragrance that is contained in an unblossomed bud

items.translit: Seridhoti Seydhirandha Kallam Urudhuyar / Theerkkum Marundhondru Utaiththu
items.en: The secret wiles of her with thronging armlets decked, Are medicines by which my raising grief is checked
items.en_prose: The well-meant departure of her whose bangles are tight-fitting contains a remedy that can cure my great sorrow

items.translit: Peridhaatrip Petpak Kalaththal Aridhaatri / Anpinmai Soozhva Thutaiththu
items.en: While lovingly embracing me, his heart is only grieved:It makes me think that I again shall live of love bereaved
items.en_prose: The embrace that fills me with comfort and gladness is capable of enduring (my former) sorrow and meditating on his want of love

items.translit: Thannan Thuraivan Thanandhamai Namminum / Munnam Unarndha Valai
items.en: My severance from the lord of this cool shore, My very armlets told me long before
items.en_prose: My bracelets have understood before me the (mental) separation of him who rules the cool seashore

items.translit: Nerunatruch Chendraarem Kaadhalar Yaamum / Ezhunaalem Meni Pasandhu
items.en: My loved one left me, was it yesterday?Days seven my pallid body wastes away
items.en_prose: It was but yesterday my lover departed (from me); and it is seven days since my complexion turned sallow

items.translit: Thotinokki Mendholum Nokki Atinokki / Aqdhaan Tavalsey Thadhu
items.en: She viewed her tender arms, she viewed the armlets from them slid; She viewed her feet: all this the lady did
items.en_prose: She looked at her bracelets, her tender shoulders, and her feet; this was what she did there (significantly)

items.translit: Penninaal Penmai Utaiththenpa Kanninaal / Kaamanoi Solli Iravu
items.en: To show by eye the pain of love, and for relief to pray, Is womanhood's most womanly device, men say
items.en_prose: To express their love-sickness by their eyes and resort to begging bespeaks more than ordinary female excellence

items.translit: Ullak Kaliththalum Kaana Makizhdhalum / Kallukkil Kaamaththir Kuntu
items.en: Gladness at the thought, rejoicing at the sight, Not palm-tree wine, but love, yields such delight
items.en_prose: To please by thought and cheer by sight is peculiar, not to liquor but lust

items.translit: Thinaiththunaiyum Ootaamai Ventum Panaith / Thunaiyum Kaamam Niraiya Varin
items.en: When as palmyra tall, fulness of perfect love we gain, Distrust can find no place small as the millet grain
items.en_prose: If women have a lust that exceeds even the measure of the palmyra fruit, they will not desire (to feign) dislike even as much as the millet

items.translit: Penaadhu Petpave Seyyinum Konkanaik / Kaanaa Thamaiyala Kan
items.en: Although his will his only law, he lightly value me, My heart knows no repose unless my lord I see
items.en_prose: Though my eyes disregard me and do what is pleasing to my husband, still will they not be satisfied unless they see him

items.translit: Ootarkan Sendrenman Thozhi Adhumarandhu / Kootarkan Sendradhu En Nenju
items.en: My friend, I went prepared to show a cool disdain; My heart, forgetting all, could not its love restrain
items.en_prose: My heart, forgetting all, could not its love restrain

items.translit: Ezhudhungaal Kolkaanaak Kannepol Konkan / Pazhikaanen Kanta Itaththu
items.en: The eye sees not the rod that paints it; nor can ISee any fault, when I behold my husband nigh
items.en_prose: Like the eyes which see not the pencil that paints it, I cannot see my husband's fault (just) when I meet him

items.translit: Kaanungaal Kaanen Thavaraaya Kaanaakkaal / Kaanen Thavaral Lavai
items.en: When him I see, to all his faults I 'm blind; But when I see him not, nothing but faults I find
items.en_prose: When I see my husband, I do not see any faults; but when I do not see him, I do not see anything but faults

items.translit: Uyththal Arindhu Punalpaai Pavarepol / Poiththal Arindhen Pulandhu
items.en: As those of rescue sure, who plunge into the stream, So did I anger feign, though it must falsehood seem
items.en_prose: Like those who leap into a stream which they know will carry them off, why should a wife feign dislike which she knows cannot hold out long?

items.translit: Iliththakka Innaa Seyinum Kaliththaarkkuk / Kallatre Kalvanin Maarpu
items.en: Though shameful ill it works, dear is the palm-tree wine / To drunkards; traitor, so to me that breast of thine
items.en_prose: O you rogue! your breast is to me what liquor is to those who rejoice in it, though it only gives them an unpleasant disgrace

items.translit: Malarinum Mellidhu Kaamam Silaradhan / Sevvi Thalaippatu Vaar
items.en: Love is tender as an opening flower In season due / To gain its perfect bliss is rapture known to few
items.en_prose: Sexual delight is more delicate than a flower, and few are those who understand its real nature

items.translit: Kannin Thuniththe Kalanginaal Pulludhal / Enninum Thaanvidhup Putru
items.en: Her eye, as I drew nigh one day, with anger shone:By love o'erpowered, her tenderness surpassed my own
items.en_prose: She once feigned dislike in her eyes, but the warmth of her embrace exceeded my own

items.translit: Avarnenju Avarkkaadhal Kantum Evannenje / Neeemakku Aakaa Thadhu
items.en: You see his heart is his alone / O heart, why not be all my own
items.en_prose: O my soul! although you have seen how his soul stands by him, how is it you do not stand by me?

items.translit: Uraaa Thavarkkanta Kannum Avaraich / Cheraaarenach Cheriyen Nenju
items.en: 'Tis plain, my heart, that he 's estranged from thee; Why go to him as though he were not enemy
items.en_prose: O my soul! although you have known him who does not love me, still do you go to him, saying "he will not be displeased."

items.translit: Kettaarkku Nattaaril Enpadho Nenjenee / Pettaangu Avarpin Selal
items.en: 'The ruined have no friends, 'they say; and so, my heart, To follow him, at thy desire, from me thou dost depart
items.en_prose: O my soul! do you follow him at pleasure under the belief that the ruined have no friends?

items.translit: Inianna Ninnotu Soozhvaaryaar Nenje / Thuniseydhu Thuvvaaikaan Matru
items.en: 'See, thou first show offended pride, and then submit,' I bade; Henceforth such council who will share with thee my heart
items.en_prose: O my soul! you would not first seem sulky and then enjoy (him); who then would in future consult you about such things?

items.translit: Peraaamai Anjum Perinpirivu Anjum / Araaa Itumpaiththen Nenju
items.en: I fear I shall not gain, I fear to lose him when I gain; And thus my heart endures unceasing pain
items.en_prose: My soul fears when it is without him; it also fears when it is with him; it is subject to incessant sorrow

items.translit: Thaniye Irundhu Ninaiththakkaal Ennaith / Thiniya Irundhadhen Nenju
items.en: My heart consumes me when I ponder lone, And all my lover's cruelty bemoan
items.en_prose: My mind has been (here) in order to eat me up (as it were) whenever I think of him in my solitude

items.translit: Naanum Marandhen Avarmarak Kallaaen / Maanaa Matanenjir Pattu
items.en: Fall'n 'neath the sway of this ignoble foolish heart, Which will not him forget, I have forgotten shame
items.en_prose: I have even forgotten my modesty, having been caught in my foolish mind which is not dignified enough to forget him

items.translit: Ellin Ilivaamendru Enni Avardhiram / Ullum Uyirkkaadhal Nenju
items.en: If I contemn him, then disgrace awaits me evermore; My soul that seeks to live his virtues numbers o'er
items.en_prose: My soul which clings to life thinks only of his (own) gain in the belief that it would be disgraceful for it to despise him

items.translit: Thunpaththirku Yaare Thunaiyaavaar Thaamutaiya / Nenjan Thunaiyal Vazhi
items.en: And who will aid me in my hour of grief, If my own heart comes not to my relief
items.en_prose: Who would help me out of one's distress, when one's own soul refuses help to one?

items.translit: Thanjam Thamarallar Edhilaar Thaamutaiya / Nenjam Thamaral Vazhi
items.en: A trifle is unfriendliness by aliens shown, When our own heart itself is not our own
items.en_prose: It is hardly possible for strangers to behave like relations, when one's own soul acts like a stranger

items.translit: Pullaa Thiraaap Pulaththai Avar / Urum Allalnoi Kaankam Siridhu
items.en: Be still reserved, decline his profferred love; A little while his sore distress we 'll prove
items.en_prose: Let us witness awhile his keen suffering; just feign dislike and embrace him not

items.translit: Uppamain Thatraal Pulavi Adhusiridhu / Mikkatraal Neela Vital
items.en: A cool reserve is like the salt that seasons well the mess, Too long maintained, 'tis like the salt's excess
items.en_prose: A little dislike is like salt in proportion; to prolong it a little is like salt a little too much

items.translit: Alandhaarai Allalnoi Seydhatraal Thammaip / Pulandhaaraip Pullaa Vital
items.en: 'Tis heaping griefs on those whose hearts are grieved; To leave the grieving one without a fond embrace
items.en_prose: For men not to embrace those who have feigned dislike is like torturing those already in agony

items.translit: Ooti Yavarai Unaraamai Vaatiya / Valli Mudhalarin Thatru
items.en: To use no kind conciliating art when lover grieves, Is cutting out the root of tender winding plant that droops
items.en_prose: Not to reconcile those who have feigned dislike is like cutting a faded creeper at its root

items.translit: Nalaththakai Nallavarkku Eer Pulaththakai / Pooanna Kannaar Akaththu
items.en: Even to men of good and worthy mind, the petulance / Of wives with flowery eyes lacks not a lovely grace
items.en_prose: An increased shyness in those whose eyes are like flowers is beautiful even to good and virtuous husbands

items.translit: Thuniyum Pulaviyum Illaayin Kaamam / Kaniyum Karukkaayum Atru
items.en: Love without hatred is ripened fruit; Without some lesser strife, fruit immature
items.en_prose: Sexual pleasure, without prolonged and short-lived dislike, is like too ripe, and unripe fruit

items.translit: Ootalin Untaangor Thunpam Punarvadhu / Neetuva Thandru Kol Endru
items.en: A lovers' quarrel brings its pain, when mind afraid / Asks doubtful, 'Will reunion sweet be long delayed?'
items.en_prose: The doubt as to whether intercourse would take place soon or not, creates a sorrow (even) in feigned dislike

items.translit: Nodhal Evanmatru Nondhaarendru Aqdhariyum / Kaadhalar Illaa Vazhi
items.en: What good can grieving do, when none who love / Are there to know the grief thy soul endures
items.en_prose: What avails sorrow when I am without a wife who can understand the cause of my sorrow?

items.translit: Neerum Nizhaladhu Inidhe Pulaviyum / Veezhunar Kanne Inidhu
items.en: Water is pleasant in the cooling shade; So coolness for a time with those we love
items.en_prose: Like water in the shade, dislike is delicious only in those who love

items.translit: Ootal Unanga Vituvaarotu Ennenjam / Kootuvem Enpadhu Avaa
items.en: Of her who leaves me thus in variance languishing, To think within my heart with love is fond desire
items.en_prose: It is nothing but strong desire that makes her mind unite with me who can leave her to her own dislike

items.translit: Penniyalaar Ellaarum Kannin Podhuunpar / Nannen Paraththanin Maarpu
items.en: From thy regard all womankind Enjoys an equal grace; O thou of wandering fickle mind, I shrink from thine embrace
items.en_prose: You are given to prostitution; all those who are born as womankind enjoy you with their eyes in an ordinary way I will not embrace you

items.translit: Ooti Irundhemaath Thumminaar Yaamdhammai / Neetuvaazh Kenpaak Karindhu
items.en: One day we silent sulked; he sneezed: The reason well I knew; He thought that I, to speak well pleased, Would say, 'Long life to you!'
items.en_prose: When I continued to be sulky he sneezed and thought I would (then) wish him a long life

items.translit: Kottup Pooch Chootinum Kaayum / Oruththiyaik Kaattiya Sootineer Endru
items.en: I wreathed with flowers one day my brow, The angry tempest lowers; She cries, 'Pray, for what woman now Do you put on your flowers?'
items.en_prose: Even if I were adorned with a garland of branch-flowers, she would say I did so to show it to another woman

items.translit: Yaarinum Kaadhalam Endrenaa Ootinaal / Yaarinum Yaarinum Endru
items.en: 'I love you more than all beside,' 'T was thus I gently spoke;'What all, what all?' she instant cried; And all her anger woke
items.en_prose: When I said I loved her more than any other woman, she said "more than others, yes, more than others," and remained sulky

items.translit: Immaip Pirappil Piriyalam Endrenaak / Kannirai Neerkon Tanal
items.en: 'While here I live, I leave you not,' I said to calm her fears / She cried, 'There, then, I read your thought'; And straight dissolved in tears
items.en_prose: When I said I would never part from her in this life her eyes were filled with tears

items.translit: Ullinen Endrenmar Renmarandheer Endrennaip / Pullaal Pulaththak Kanal
items.en: 'Each day I called to mind your charms,' 'O, then, you had forgot,'She cried, and then her opened arms, Forthwith embraced me not
items.en_prose: When I said I had remembered her, she said I had forgotten her and relaxing her embrace, began to feign dislike

items.translit: Vazhuththinaal Thumminen Aaka Azhiththazhudhaal / Yaarullith Thummineer Endru
items.en: She hailed me when I sneezed one day; But straight with anger seized, She cried; 'Who was the woman, pray, Thinking of whom you sneezed?'
items.en_prose: When I sneezed she blessed me, but at once changed (her mind) and wept, asking, "At the thought of whom did you sneeze?"

items.translit: Thummuch Cheruppa Azhudhaal Numarullal / Emmai Maraiththiro Endru
items.en: And so next time I checked my sneeze; She forthwith wept and cried,(That woman difficult to please), 'Your thoughts from me you hide'
items.en_prose: When I suppressed my sneezing, she wept saying, "I suppose you (did so) to hide from me your own people's remembrance of you"

items.translit: Thannai Unarththinum Kaayum Pirarkkumneer / Inneerar Aakudhir Endru
items.en: I then began to soothe and coax, To calm her jealous mind;'I see', quoth she, 'to other folks How you are wondrous kind
items.en_prose: 'I see', quoth she, 'to other folks How you are wondrous kind' Even when I try to remove her dislike, she is displeased and says, "This is the way you behave

items.translit: Ninaiththirundhu Nokkinum Kaayum Anaiththuneer / Yaarulli Nokkineer Endru
items.en: I silent sat, but thought the more, And gazed on her Then she / Cried out, 'While thus you eye me o'er, Tell me whose form you see'
items.en_prose: Even when I look on her contemplating (her beauty), she is displeased and says, "With whose thought have you (thus) looked on my person?"

items.translit: Illai Thavaravarkku Aayinum Ootudhal / Valladhu Avaralikku Maaru
items.en: Although there be no fault in him, the sweetness of his love / Hath power in me a fretful jealousy to move
items.en_prose: Although my husband is free from defects, the way in which he embraces me is such as to make me feign dislike

items.translit: Ootalin Thondrum Sirudhuni Nallali / Vaatinum Paatu Perum
items.en: My 'anger feigned' gives but a little pain; And when affection droops, it makes it bloom again
items.en_prose: His love will increase though it may (at first seem to) fade through the short-lived distress caused by (my) dislike

items.translit: Pulaththalin Puththelnaatu Unto Nilaththotu / Neeriyain Thannaar Akaththu
items.en: Is there a bliss in any world more utterly divine, Than 'coyness' gives, when hearts as earth and water join
items.en_prose: Is there a celestial land that can please like the feigned dislike of those whose union resembles that of earth and water?

items.translit: Pulli Vitaaap Pulaviyul Thondrumen / Ullam Utaikkum Patai
items.en: 'Within the anger feigned' that close love's tie doth bind, A weapon lurks, which quite breaks down my mind
items.en_prose: In prolonged dislike after an embrace there is a weapon that can break my heart

items.translit: Thavarilar Aayinum Thaamveezhvaar Mendrol / Akaralin Aangon Rutaiththu
items.en: Though free from fault, from loved one's tender arms / To be estranged a while hath its own special charms
items.en_prose: Though free from defects, men feel pleased when they cannot embrace the delicate shoulders of those whom they love

items.translit: Unalinum Untadhu Aralinidhu Kaamam / Punardhalin Ootal Inidhu
items.en: 'Tis sweeter to digest your food than 'tis to eat; In love, than union's self is anger feigned more sweet
items.en_prose: To digest what has been eaten is more delightful than to eat more; likewise love is more delightful in dislike than intercourse

items.translit: Ootalil Thotravar Vendraar Adhumannum / Kootalir Kaanap Patum
items.en: In lovers' quarrels, 'tis the one that first gives way, That in re-union's joy is seen to win the day
items.en_prose: Those are conquerors whose dislike has been defeated and that is proved by the love (which

items.translit: Ootip Perukuvam Kollo Nudhalveyarppak / Kootalil Thondriya Uppu
items.en: And shall we ever more the sweetness know of that embrace / With dewy brow; to which 'feigned anger' lent its piquant grace
items.en_prose: Will I enjoy once more through her dislike, the pleasure of that love that makes her forehead perspire?

items.translit: Ootuka Manno Oliyizhai Yaamirappa / Neetuka Manno Iraa
items.en: Let her, whose jewels brightly shine, aversion feign / That I may still plead on, O night, prolong thy reign
items.en_prose: May the bright-jewelled one feign dislike, and may the night be prolonged for me to implore her!

items.translit: Ootudhal Kaamaththirku Inpam Adharkinpam / Kooti Muyangap Perin
items.en: A 'feigned aversion' coy to pleasure gives a zest; The pleasure's crowned when breast is clasped to breast
items.en_prose: Dislike adds delight to love; and a hearty embrace (thereafter) will add delight to dislike

items.translit: aṟam ceya virumpu
items.meaning_ta: தருமம் செய்ய ஆசைப்படு.

items.translit: āṟuvatu ciṉam
items.meaning_ta: கோபம் தணியத் தகுவதாம்.

items.translit: iyalvatu karavēl
items.meaning_ta: கொடுக்க முடிந்த பொருளை இரப்பவர்க்கு ஒளியாமல் கொடு.

items.translit: īvatu vilakkēl
items.meaning_ta: ஒருவர் மற்றொருவர்க்குக் கொடுப்பதைக் கொடுக்க வேண்டாமென்று தடுக்காதே.

items.translit: uṭaiyatu viḷampēl
items.meaning_ta: உன்னுடைய பொருளை அல்லது கல்வி முதலிய சிறப்பை நீயே புகழ்ந்து பேசவேண்டா.

items.translit: ūkkamatu kaiviṭēl
items.meaning_ta: எத்தொழில் செய்யும்பொழுதும் மனவலிமை யினைக் கைவிடாதே.

items.translit: eṇ eḻuttu ikaḻēl
items.meaning_ta: கணிதத்தையும், இலக்கணத்தையும் இகழாமல் நன்றாகக் கற்றுக்கொள்.

items.translit: ēṟpatu ikaḻcci
items.meaning_ta: இரந்துண்டு வாழ்வது பழிப்பாகையால் ஒருவரிடத்தும் சென்று ஒன்றை வேண்டாதே.

items.translit: aiyam iṭṭu uṇ
items.meaning_ta: இரப்பவர்க்குப் பிச்சையிட்டுப் பின்பு உண்ணு.

items.translit: oppuravu oḻuku
items.meaning_ta: உலகத்தோடு பொருந்த நடந்துகொள்.

items.translit: ōtuvatu oḻiyēl
items.meaning_ta: அறிவு தரும் நல்ல நூல்களை எப்பொழுதும் படித்துக்கொண்டிரு.

items.translit: auviyam pēcēl
items.meaning_ta: ஒருவரிடத்தும் பொறாமைகொண்டு பேசாதே.

items.translit: aḵkam curukkēl
items.meaning_ta: மிகுந்த இலாபத்துக்கு ஆசைப்பட்டுத் தானியங்களைக் குறைத்து விற்காதே.

items.translit: kaṇṭoṉṟu collēl
items.meaning_ta: பார்க்காததைப் பார்க்காதவற்றைப் பார்த்ததாகப் பேசாதே

items.translit: ṅap pōl vaḷai
items.meaning_ta: 'ங' என்னும் எழுத்தானது எப்படி தான் பயன்னுள்ளதாக இருந்து தன் வருக்க எழுத்துகளைத் தழுவுகிறதோ அது போல நாமும் நம்மைச் சார்ந்தவர்களால் என்ன பயன் என்று பாராமல் அவர்களைக் காக்க வேண்டும். "ங" என்னும் எழுத்தைக் கூர்ந்து நோக்கினால், ஒருவர் வளைந்து வணக்கம் சொல்வது போல் உள்ளது விளங்கும். அதைப்போலப் பணிவாகப் பெரியவர் முன் வளைய வேண்டும் என்று ஔவை உரைத்ததாகவும் எடுத்துக்கொள்ளலாம்.

items.translit: caṉi nīrāṭu
items.meaning_ta: சனி(குளிர்ந்த) நீராடு.

items.translit: ñayampaṭa urai
items.meaning_ta: கேட்பவருக்கு இன்பம் உண்டாகும் படி இனிமையாகப் பேசு.

items.translit: iṭampaṭa vīṭu eṭēl
items.meaning_ta: உன் தேவைக்கு மேல் வீட்டை பெரிதாகக் கட்டாதே.

items.translit: iṇakkam aṟintu iṇaṅku
items.meaning_ta: ஒருவரிடம் நட்பு கொள்ளும் முன்,அவர் நல்ல குணங்களும்,நல்ல செய்கைகளும் கொண்டவரா எனத் தெரிந்த பிறகு அவருடன் நட்பு கொள்ளவும்.

items.translit: tantai tāyp pēṇ
items.meaning_ta: உன் தந்தையையும் தாயையும் அவர்களுடைய முதுமைக் காலம் வரை அன்புடன் காப்பாற்று.

items.translit: naṉṟi maṟavēl
items.meaning_ta: ஒருவர் உனக்குச் செய்த உதவியை ஒரு போதும் மறவாதே

items.translit: paruvattē payir cey
items.meaning_ta: எச்செயலையும் அதற்குரிய காலத்திலேயே செய்ய வேண்டும்.

items.translit: maṇ paṟittu uṇṇēl
items.meaning_ta: பிறர் நிலத்தைத் திருடி அதன் மூலம் வாழாதே (அல்லது) நீதி மன்றத்தில் இருந்து கொண்டே லஞ்சம் வாங்கிக்கொண்டு தீர்ப்பு வழங்காதே (என்றும் பொருள் கொள்ளலாம்)

items.translit: iyalpu alātaṉa ceyyēl
items.meaning_ta: நல்லொழுக்கத்துக்கு மாறான செயல்களைச் செய்யாதே.

items.translit: aravam āṭṭēl
items.meaning_ta: பாம்புகளைப் பிடித்து விளையாடாதே.

items.translit: ilavam pañcil tuyil
items.meaning_ta: 'இலவம் பஞ்சு' எனும் ஒரு வகை பஞ்சினால் செய்யப்பட்ட படுக்கையிலே உறங்கு

items.translit: vañcakam pēcēl
items.meaning_ta: கபடச்(உண்மைக்கு புறம்பான,கவர்ச்சிகரமான) சொற்களைப் பேசாதே

items.translit: aḻaku alātaṉa ceyyēl
items.meaning_ta: இழிவான செயல்களை செய்யாதே

items.translit: iḷamaiyil kal
items.meaning_ta: இளமை பருவத்தில் இருந்தே கற்கவேண்டியவைகளைத் (இலக்கணத்தையும், கணிதத்தையும்) தவறாமல் கற்றுக்கொள்.

items.translit: aṟaṉai maṟavēl
items.meaning_ta: தருமத்தை எப்போதும் மறவாமல் செய்

items.translit: aṉantal āṭēl
items.meaning_ta: மிகுதியாகத் தூங்காதே

items.translit: kaṭivatu maṟa
items.meaning_ta: யாரையும் கோபத்தில் கடிந்து பேசிவிடாதே.

items.translit: kāppatu viratam
items.meaning_ta: தான் செய்யத் தொடங்கிய தருமத்தை விடாமல் செய்வதே விரதமாகும் (அல்லது) பிற உயிர்களுக்குதீ துன்பம் செய்யாமல் அவற்றைக் காப்பாற்றுவதே தவம் ஆகும்.

items.translit: kiḻamaippaṭa vāḻ
items.meaning_ta: உன் உடலாலும் பொருளாலும் பிறருக்கு நன்மை செய்து வாழ்.

items.translit: kīḻmai akaṟṟu
items.meaning_ta: இழிவான குணஞ் செயல்களை நீக்கு.

items.translit: kuṇamatu kaiviṭēl
items.meaning_ta: நன்மை தரக்கூடிய நல்ல குணங்களைப் பின்பற்றுவதை நிறுத்திவிடாதே(கைவிடேல்).

items.translit: kūṭip piriyēl
items.meaning_ta: நல்லவரோடு நட்பு செய்து பின் அவரைப் பிரியாதே.

items.translit: keṭuppatu oḻi
items.meaning_ta: பிறருக்குக் கேடு விளைவிக்கும் செயல்களைச் செய்யாதே.

items.translit: kēḷvi muyal
items.meaning_ta: கற்றவர் சொல்லும் நூற் பொருளைக் கேட்பதற்கு முயற்சி செய்.

items.translit: kaiviṉai karavēl
items.meaning_ta: உங்களுக்குத் தெரிந்த கைத்தொழிலை மற்றவர்களிடமிருந்து ஒளியாமற் செய்து கொண்டிருக்கவும்.

items.translit: koḷḷai virumpēl
items.meaning_ta: பிறர் பொருளைத் திருடுவதற்கு ஆசைப்படாதே.

items.translit: kōtāṭṭu oḻi
items.meaning_ta: குற்றமான விளையாட்டை விட்டு விடு (நீக்கு).

items.translit: kauvai akaṟṟu
items.meaning_ta: வாழ்வில் செயற்கையாக ஏற்படும் துன்பத்தை நீக்கு.

items.translit: cakkara neṟi nil
items.meaning_ta: தருமசக்கர நெறிப்படி வாழ வேண்டும். (அரசன் = ஆள்பவர், தலைவர்).

items.translit: cāṉṟōr iṉattu iru
items.meaning_ta: அறிவொழுக்கங்களில் நிறைந்த பெரியோர்களுடன் சேர்ந்து இரு.

items.translit: cittiram pēcēl
items.meaning_ta: பொய்யான வார்தைகளை மெய் போலப் பேசாதே.

items.translit: cīrmai maṟavēl
items.meaning_ta: புகழுக்குக் காரணமான நல்ல குணங்களை மறந்து விடாதே.

items.translit: cuḷikkac collēl
items.meaning_ta: கேட்பவருக்குக் கோபமும் வெறுப்பும் உண்டாகும் படி பேசாதீர்.

items.translit: cūtu virumpēl
items.meaning_ta: ஒருபொதும் சூதாட்டத்தை விரும்பாதே.

items.translit: ceyvaṉa tiruntac cey
items.meaning_ta: செய்யும் செயல்களைச் தவறோ குறையோ ஏதும் இல்லாமல் செய்யவும்.

items.translit: cēriṭam aṟintu cēr
items.meaning_ta: நீ பழகும் நபர்கள் நல்ல குணங்கள் உடையவர்களா என நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து பின்பு அவர்களுடன் பழகு.

items.translit: caiyeṉat tiriyēl
items.meaning_ta: பெரியோர் 'சீ' என வெறுக்கும் படி வீணாய்த் திரியாதே.

items.translit: coṟ cōrvu paṭēl
items.meaning_ta: பிறருடன் பேசும் பொழுது மறந்தும் குற்றமுண்டாகப் பேசாதே.

items.translit: cōmpit tiriyēl
items.meaning_ta: முயற்சியின்றிச் சோம்பேறியாகத் திரியாதே.

items.translit: takkōṉ eṉat tiri
items.meaning_ta: பெரியோர்கள் உன்னைத் தக்கவன்(யோக்கியன்,நல்லவன்) என்று புகழும்படி நடந்துக்கொள்.

items.translit: tāṉamatu virumpu
items.meaning_ta: யாசிப்பவர்களுக்குத் தானம் செய்.

items.translit: tirumālukku aṭimai cey
items.meaning_ta: நாராயணமூர்த்திக்குத் தொண்டு செய்.

items.translit: tīviṉai akaṟṟu
items.meaning_ta: பாவச் செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் இரு.

items.translit: tuṉpattiṟku iṭam koṭēl
items.meaning_ta: முயற்சி செய்யும் பொழுது வரும் உடம்பின் வருத்தத்திற்கு அஞ்சி அதனை விட்டு விடாதே.

items.translit: tūkki viṉai cey
items.meaning_ta: ஒரு வேலையை முடிப்பதற்க்கான வழிமுறைகளை நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்து பின்பு அச்செயலைச் செய்யத் தொடங்கவும்.

items.translit: teyvam ikaḻēl
items.meaning_ta: கடவுளைப் பழிக்காதே.

items.translit: tēcattōṭu oṭṭi vāḻ
items.meaning_ta: உன் நாட்டில் வசிக்கும் மக்களுடன் பகை இல்லாமல் வாழ்.

items.translit: taiyal col kēḷēl
items.meaning_ta: மனைவி சொல் கேட்டு ஆராயாமல் நடவாதே.

items.translit: toṉmai maṟavēl
items.meaning_ta: பழமையாகிய நட்பினை மறந்துவிடாதே.

items.translit: tōṟpaṉa toṭarēl
items.meaning_ta: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்தால் தோல்வியில் தான முடியும் எனத் தெரிந்தே அதைத் தொடங்காதே.

items.translit: naṉmai kaṭaippiṭi
items.meaning_ta: நல்வினை செய்தலை எவ்வளவு இடையுறு வந்தாலும் உறுதியாகத் தொடரவும்.

items.translit: nāṭu oppaṉa cey
items.meaning_ta: நாட்டில் உள்ள பலரும் ஒத்துக்கொள்ளத்தக்க நல்ல காரியங்களைச் செய்.

items.translit: nilaiyil piriyēl
items.meaning_ta: உன்னுடைய நல்ல நிலையில் இருந்து என்றும் தாழ்ந்து விடாதே.

items.translit: nīr viḷaiyāṭēl
items.meaning_ta: வெள்ளத்தில் நீந்தி விளையாடாதே.

items.translit: nuṇmai nukarēl
items.meaning_ta: நோயைத் தரும் சிற்றுண்டிகளை அதிகமாக உண்ணாதே.

items.translit: nūl pala kal
items.meaning_ta: அறிவை வளர்க்கும் பல நூல்களைப் படி.

items.translit: neṟpayir viḷaivu cey
items.meaning_ta: நெற்பயிரை விளையச் செய்வதை உன் வாழ்க்கை தொழிலாகக் கொண்டு வாழ்.

items.translit: nērpaṭa oḻuku
items.meaning_ta: ஒழுக்கந் தவறாமல் நேர்வழியில் நட.

items.translit: naiviṉai naṇukēl
items.meaning_ta: பிறர் வருந்தத் தகுந்த தீ வினைகளைச் செய்யாதே.

items.translit: noyya uraiyēl
items.meaning_ta: பயன் இல்லாத அற்ப வார்த்தைகளைப் பேசாதே.

items.translit: nōykku iṭam koṭēl
items.meaning_ta: மிகுந்த உணவு உறக்கம் முதலியவற்றால் நோய்க்கு வழிவகை செய்யாதே.

items.translit: paḻippaṉa pakarēl
items.meaning_ta: பெரியோர்களால் பழிக்கப்படும் இழிவான சொற்களான பொய்,கடுஞ்சொல் ஆகியவற்றைப் பேசாதே.

items.translit: pāmpoṭu paḻakēl
items.meaning_ta: பாம்புபோல கொடிய குணம் கொண்டவர்கள் உடன் பழகாதே.

items.translit: piḻaipaṭac collēl
items.meaning_ta: குற்றம் உண்டாகும் படி எதையும் பேசாதே.

items.translit: pīṭu peṟa nil
items.meaning_ta: பெறுமையை அடையும் படியான நல்ல நிலையிலே நில்.

items.translit: pukaḻntāraip pōṟṟi vāḻ
items.meaning_ta: உன்னையே நம்பியவர்களைக் காப்பாற்றி வாழ்.

items.translit: pūmi tirutti uṇ
items.meaning_ta: விளைநிலத்தை உழுது அதில் பயிர்செய்து உண்.(அ)விவசாயத்தை வாழ்க்கைத் தொழிலாகக் கொள்.

items.translit: periyārait tuṇaik koḷ
items.meaning_ta: அறிவிலே சிறந்த பெரியோர்களை உனக்குத் துணையாகப் பேணிக்கொள்.

items.translit: pētaimai akaṟṟu
items.meaning_ta: அறியாமையைப் போக்கு.

items.translit: paiyalōṭu iṇaṅkēl
items.meaning_ta: அறிவில்லாத சிறுவனோடு கூடித் திரியாதே.

items.translit: poruḷtaṉaip pōṟṟi vāḻ
items.meaning_ta: பொருள்களை(செல்வம் உட்பட)வீண் செலவு செய்யாமற் பாதுகாத்து வாழ்.

items.translit: pōrt toḻil puriyēl
items.meaning_ta: யாருடனும் தேவையில்லாமல் சண்டை பொடுவதை ஒரு வேலையாகச் செய்யாதே.

items.translit: maṉam taṭumāṟēl
items.meaning_ta: எதனாலும் மனக்கலக்கம் அடையாதே.

items.translit: māṟṟāṉukku iṭam koṭēl
items.meaning_ta: பகைவன் உன்னை துன்புறுத்தி உன்னை வெல்வதற்கு இடம் கொடுக்காதே.

items.translit: mikaipaṭac collēl
items.meaning_ta: சாதாரணமான விஷயத்தை மாயாஜால வார்தைகளால் பெரிதாகக் கூறாதே.

items.translit: mītūṇ virumpēl
items.meaning_ta: மிகுதியாக உண்ணுதலை விரும்பாதே.

items.translit: muṉaimukattu nillēl
items.meaning_ta: எப்போதும் யாருடனாவது சண்டையிடுவதற்காக போர் முனையிலே நிற்காதே.

items.translit: mūrkkarōṭu iṇaṅkēl
items.meaning_ta: மூர்க்க குணம் கொண்டவர்கள் உடன் பழகாதே.

items.translit: melli nallāḷ tōḷcēr
items.meaning_ta: பிற மாதரை விரும்பாமல் உன் மனைவியுடன் மட்டும் சேர்ந்து வாழ்.

items.translit: mēṉmakkaḷ col kēḷ
items.meaning_ta: நல்லொழுக்கம் உடைய பெரியோர் சொல்லைக் கேட்டு நட.

items.translit: mai viḻiyār maṉai akal
items.meaning_ta: விலைமாந்தர் உடன் உறவு கொள்ளாமல் விலகி நில்.

items.translit: moḻivatu aṟa moḻi
items.meaning_ta: சொல்லப் படும் பொருளைச் சந்தேகம் நீங்கும் படி சொல்.

items.translit: mōkattai muṉi
items.meaning_ta: நிலையில்லாத பொருள்களின் மேலுள்ள ஆசையை வெறுத்திடு.

items.translit: vallamai pēcēl
items.meaning_ta: உன்னுடைய சாமர்த்தியத்தை நீயே புகழ்ந்து பேசாதே.

items.translit: vātu muṟkūṟēl
items.meaning_ta: பெரியோர்களிடத்தில் முரண்பட்டு வாதிடாதே.

items.translit: vittai virumpu
items.meaning_ta: கல்வியாகிய நற்பொருளை விரும்பு.

items.translit: vīṭu peṟa nil
items.meaning_ta: முக்தியைப் பெறுவதற்கான சன்மார்க்கத்திலே வாழ்க்கையை நடத்து.

items.translit: uttamaṉāy iru
items.meaning_ta: உயர்ந்த குணங்கள் கொண்டவனாக வாழ்.

items.translit: ūruṭaṉ kūṭi vāḻ
items.meaning_ta: ஊராருடன் நன்மை தீமைகளில் கலந்து வாழ்.

items.translit: veṭṭeṉap pēcēl
items.meaning_ta: யாருடனும் கத்தி வெட்டுப் போலக் கடினமாகப் பேசாதே.

items.translit: vēṇṭi viṉai ceyēl
items.meaning_ta: வேண்டுமென்றே தீய செயல்களைச் செய்யாதே.

items.translit: vaikaṟait tuyil eḻu
items.meaning_ta: நாள்தோறும் சூரியன் உதிக்கும் முன்பே தூக்கத்தில் இருந்து எழுந்திரு.

items.translit: oṉṉārait tēṟēl
items.meaning_ta: பகைவர்களை நம்பாதே.

items.translit: ōram collēl
items.meaning_ta: எந்த வழக்கிலும் ஒருபுடைச் சார்பாகப் பேசாமல் நடுநிலையுடன் பேசு.
